```{r loadData}
#### load variables
xlsx_file_path <- file.path(input_dir,paste0(params$study_name,"_list_of_vars.xlsx"))
tab_names<-openxlsx::getSheetNames(xlsx_file_path)
### list with separate element for each tab
list_of_vars <- lapply(tab_names,
                           openxlsx::read.xlsx,xlsxFile=xlsx_file_path)
names(list_of_vars) <- tab_names



xlsx_file_path <- file.path(input_dir,paste0(params$study_name,"_list_of_rawDatasets.xlsx"))
tab_names<-openxlsx::getSheetNames(xlsx_file_path)
### list with separate element for each tab
list_of_raw <- lapply(tab_names,
                           openxlsx::read.xlsx,xlsxFile=xlsx_file_path)
names(list_of_raw) <- tab_names

raw_df_TOA <- list_of_raw[["TOA"]] %>%
  ### add TOA_adj
    ### recalculate TOA_adj == all match when topped at 12 challenges
  dplyr::mutate(TOA_adj = ifelse(Infection_status == 0,
                                  TOA + 1,
                                  TOA),
                TOA_adj = ifelse(TOA_adj > 12, 12, TOA_adj),
                Sex = str_to_sentence(str_remove_all(str_remove_all(str_after_last(Group,"_"),"1"),"2")),
                Sex = factor(Sex, c("Male","Female"))
                )
  
metadata_df <- list_of_raw[["metadata"]]

### raw data is wide format
phen_long <- list_of_raw[["data"]] %>%
  ### add TOA data
  dplyr::left_join(raw_df_TOA, by = c("Sample_ID","studyLetterForMS")) %>%
  ### also add study number
  dplyr::left_join(metadata_df %>%
                     dplyr::select(Sample_ID,Study_number),
                   by = "Sample_ID") %>%
  ### make longer
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!all_of(c(colnames(raw_df_TOA),"Study_number")),names_to = "var_comp_time", values_to = "amount") %>%
  ## separate var_comp_time
  dplyr::mutate(variable = str_before_first(var_comp_time, "____"),
                Specimen = str_before_first(str_after_first(var_comp_time,"____"),"____"),
                Time_Point = str_after_last(var_comp_time,"____"),
                var_comp_time = NULL,
                Animal_comp_time = paste0("m",Sample_ID,"__",Specimen,"__",Time_Point),
                weeks_n = ifelse(grepl(paste(c("wk","Wk","Post"),collapse = '|'),Time_Point),
                                 as.numeric(1), ### if it's post, then 1
                                 as.numeric(0)),
                studyLetterForMS = factor(studyLetterForMS, c("studyA1","studyA2","studyB","studyC","studyD","studyE","studyF")),
                Group_simp = str_before_last(Group,"_") ###remove sex from Group
                )   %>%
##first remove na
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(amount))%>%
  arrange(Sample_ID, Specimen, variable, weeks_n) %>%
  group_by(Sample_ID, Specimen, variable) %>%
  ### NEW: explicitly pull the Baseline value for this Sample_ID/Specimen/
  ### variable group, rather than assuming it's row 1 after sorting. If no
  ### Baseline row exists in the group at all (e.g. studyD for olink),
  ### amount[Time_Point == "Baseline"][1] is NA, so FC/delta become NA for
  ### every row in the group -- instead of silently using the earliest
  ### post-baseline value as a fake reference.
  dplyr::mutate(baseline_amount = amount[Time_Point == "Baseline"][1],
                FC = 100 * (amount / baseline_amount),
                delta = amount - baseline_amount,
                baseline_amount = NULL) %>%
  ungroup()
  


#phen_long <- readRDS(file = file.path(input_dir, paste0(params$study_name,"_phen_long.rds")))

list_of_vars <- readRDS(file = file.path(input_dir, paste0(params$study_name,"_list_of_vars.rds")))



```

```{r TOA, results='asis'}

####### select animals for the aquistion curve
# phen_long_to_use <- phen_long_to_use1 %>%
#   dplyr::filter(!!rlang::sym(group_var_to_use) %in% groups_to_use) %>%
#   dplyr::select(c(!!rlang::sym(group_var_to_use),Study_number,Sample_ID,TOA_adj,Infection_status)) %>%
#   unique(.) %>% 
#   dplyr::arrange(!!rlang::sym(group_var_to_use),Sample_ID) %>%
#   
#     ### collapse rows and take first value ***need to see if this is correct**
#   dplyr::group_by(!!rlang::sym(group_var_to_use), Sample_ID) %>%
#   dplyr::reframe(across(everything(), ~ dplyr::first(.))) %>% 
#   ungroup()


summ <- phen_long_to_use1 %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(status = recode(Infection_status, "0"=0,"1"=1), ## status needs to be 0,1
                time = as.numeric(TOA_adj),
                vaccine = factor(!!rlang::sym(group_var_to_use), groups_to_use))


## survival function
#Surv(summ$time, summ$status) #calculates censored samples (i.e. that never had infection in time period observed)

### set title for 2 or 3 groups
if(length(groups_to_use)>2){
  title_to_use <- paste0(groups_to_use[1]," n=",dim(filter(summ, vaccine == groups_to_use[1]))[1],"; ",
                      groups_to_use[2]," n=",dim(filter(summ, vaccine == groups_to_use[2]))[1],"; ",
                      groups_to_use[3]," n=",dim(filter(summ, vaccine == groups_to_use[3]))[1])
}else{
   title_to_use <- paste0(groups_to_use[1]," n=",dim(filter(summ, vaccine == groups_to_use[1]))[1],"; ",
                      groups_to_use[2]," n=",dim(filter(summ, vaccine == groups_to_use[2]))[1])
 
}


survfit2(Surv(time, status) ~ vaccine, data=summ) %>%
  ggsurvfit(linewidth=1)+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=0:12, expand=c(0.02,0))+
  scale_y_continuous(label = scales::percent, breaks=seq(0,1, by=0.2), expand=c(0.015,0))+
  labs(title = title_to_use,
       x = "Weeks",
       y = "% uninfected macaques")+
  scale_color_manual(values=colors_to_use)+
  scale_fill_manual(values=colors_to_use)+
  add_confidence_interval()+
  add_pvalue(location = "annotation")+
  ggsurvfit::add_risktable(times=c(seq(0,12,1)))+
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(), 
        axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")
        )





 cat("\n")
  cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!


```

## Supp Figure 2 (Weights & Dates) {.tabset}

```{r setScheme}

### Shape = Adjuvant x Sex (4 shapes) - shared across all scatterplots
adjSex_shape_vec <- c(
  "Alum_Male"    = 24,  # triangle-up
  "Alum_Female"  = 22,  # square
  "ALFQA_Male"   = 25,  # triangle-down
  "ALFQA_Female" = 23   # diamond
)

### fixed pale ("baseline") colors per group - shared across all scatterplots
baseline_pale_color_vec <- c(
  "DNA"   = "#FFD6AE",
  "ALVAC" = "#C4FDFF"
)



### helper: given a vector of Group and a vector of is_baseline (logical),
### return point fill / border colors following the shared scheme:
###   baseline     -> fill = white,        border = group color
###   non-baseline -> fill = group color,  border = black
get_point_fill <- function(group_vec, is_baseline_vec, group_colors_to_use){
  ifelse(is_baseline_vec, "white", unname(group_colors_to_use[as.character(group_vec)]))
}
get_point_border <- function(group_vec, is_baseline_vec, group_colors_to_use){
  ifelse(is_baseline_vec, unname(group_colors_to_use[as.character(group_vec)]), "black")
}




```







```{r weightsAndDates_byGroup}
group_colors_to_use <- c("DNA"="darkorange1",
                         "ALVAC"="turquoise3")

grouping_var_name  <- "Group_ignoreALFQA"
grouping_var_label <- "Platform"

group_levels_order <- c("DNA", "ALVAC")
naive_group_level  <- "Naive"

group_colors_base <- c(group_colors_to_use, "Naive" = "grey50")


### DNA and ALVAC are pooled across studies (unlike studyLetterForMS,
### which is already sex-separated), so all three levels -- DNA,
### ALVAC, and Naive -- get split into <level>, <level>_F, <level>_M
split_by_sex_levels <- c("DNA", "ALVAC", "Naive")

ncol_agevsweight <- 3

```

### By `r paste0(grouping_var_label)` {.tabset}

```{r weightsAndDates, results='asis', fig.width=10}

## Reads: grouping_var_name, grouping_var_label, group_levels_order,
## naive_group_level, group_colors_base -- set by whichever prep
## chunk (A or B) ran immediately before this.
##
## Produces, using {grouping_var_name} as the grouping variable:
##   1. Weight at first challenge, by group (+ sex-split, + naive)
##   2. Age at first challenge, by group (+ sex-split, + naive)
##   3. Age at first immunization, by group (vaccinated groups only)
##   4. Age at Immunization vs Age at Challenge scatter (+ "All" panel)
##   5. Weight vs Age at Challenge scatter (per-group panels, no "All")
## ============================================================


### extend the adjSex shape vector with 2 Naive shapes (distinct from
### the existing 4: 24,22,25,23 -> add 21 (circle) and 3 (star/cross)
adjSex_shape_vec_wts <- c(
  adjSex_shape_vec,
  "Naive_Male"   = 21,  # circle
  "Naive_Female" = 3    # cross
)

### helper: build the long-format plot_group data. For any level
### named in split_by_sex_levels, animals in that level appear 3x --
### once as the combined level, once as "<level>_F" (females only),
### once as "<level>_M" (males only). All other levels pass through
### unchanged (one row per animal, plot_group = their raw level).
### Given a base data frame that already has one row per animal with
### columns: Sample_ID, <grouping_var>, Sex.
build_plot_group_df <- function(df_animal, grouping_var_name, split_by_sex_levels) {

  grouping_sym <- rlang::sym(grouping_var_name)

  df_animal <- df_animal %>%
    dplyr::mutate(.raw_level = as.character(!!grouping_sym))

  ### levels that do NOT get sex-split: pass through as-is
  df_passthrough <- df_animal %>%
    dplyr::filter(!(.raw_level %in% split_by_sex_levels)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(plot_group = .raw_level)

  ### levels that DO get sex-split: build combined + _F + _M for each
  df_split_combo <- df_animal %>%
    dplyr::filter(.raw_level %in% split_by_sex_levels) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(plot_group = .raw_level)

  df_split_F <- df_animal %>%
    dplyr::filter(.raw_level %in% split_by_sex_levels, Sex == "Female") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(plot_group = paste0(.raw_level, "_F"))

  df_split_M <- df_animal %>%
    dplyr::filter(.raw_level %in% split_by_sex_levels, Sex == "Male") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(plot_group = paste0(.raw_level, "_M"))

  dplyr::bind_rows(df_passthrough, df_split_combo, df_split_F, df_split_M) %>%
    dplyr::select(-.raw_level)
}

### full plot_group factor order: for each level in group_levels_order
### PLUS naive_group_level (in that order), if it's sex-split, expand
### to <level>, <level>_F, <level>_M; otherwise just <level>.
### naive_group_level is appended separately here because it is not
### part of group_levels_order for groupings like Group_ignoreALFQA
### (where the raw column never contains "Naive" -- it's backfilled
### in during data prep, see weights_df_base/age_df_base above).
all_levels_for_expansion <- unique(c(group_levels_order, naive_group_level))

full_group_levels <- purrr::map(all_levels_for_expansion, function(lvl) {
  if (lvl %in% split_by_sex_levels) {
    c(lvl, paste0(lvl, "_F"), paste0(lvl, "_M"))
  } else {
    lvl
  }
}) %>% unlist()

### color vector for the full set of plot groups: non-split levels
### keep their base color; split levels keep their base color for the
### combined version, and get lightened tints for _F/_M
lighten <- function(hex, amount = 0.4) {
  rgb_mat <- grDevices::col2rgb(hex)
  rgb_light <- rgb_mat + (255 - rgb_mat) * amount
  grDevices::rgb(rgb_light[1], rgb_light[2], rgb_light[3], maxColorValue = 255)
}

plot_group_color_vec <- purrr::map(all_levels_for_expansion, function(lvl) {
  base_color <- unname(group_colors_base[lvl])
  if (is.na(base_color)) base_color <- "grey50"
  if (lvl %in% split_by_sex_levels) {
    setNames(
      c(base_color, lighten(base_color, 0.35), lighten(base_color, 0.65)),
      c(lvl, paste0(lvl, "_F"), paste0(lvl, "_M"))
    )
  } else {
    setNames(base_color, lvl)
  }
}) %>% unlist()

### vax_levels_order retained for the Age at Immunization plot, which
### excludes naive entirely (unchanged rows only, no sex-split there
### regardless of split_by_sex_levels, since naive has no immunization
### date to begin with)
vax_levels_order <- setdiff(group_levels_order, naive_group_level)

weights_df_base <- metadata_df %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_ID, weight_at_first_challenge) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(weight_at_first_challenge)) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    unique(raw_df_TOA[, c("Sample_ID", "Group", grouping_var_name, "Sex")]),
    by = "Sample_ID"
  ) %>%
  ### backfill naive/control animals' grouping value to naive_group_level
  ### where it's NA (e.g. Group_ignoreALFQA is NA for naive animals,
  ### since that column only ever contains "DNA"/"ALVAC")
  dplyr::mutate(
    !!grouping_var_name := ifelse(grepl("Naive", Group) & is.na(.data[[grouping_var_name]]),
                                  naive_group_level, .data[[grouping_var_name]])
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[grouping_var_name]])) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Sex = factor(Sex, c("Male", "Female")),
    Group_simp = str_before_last(Group, "_"),
    Adjuvant_raw = str_after_first(Group_simp, "_"),
    Adjuvant_raw = ifelse(grepl("Naive", Group), "Naive", Adjuvant_raw),
    AdjSex = factor(paste0(Adjuvant_raw, "_", as.character(Sex)),
                    names(adjSex_shape_vec_wts))
  )

weights_df <- build_plot_group_df(weights_df_base, grouping_var_name, split_by_sex_levels) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(plot_group = factor(plot_group, full_group_levels))

weights_stat_test <- weights_df %>%
  rstatix::wilcox_test(weight_at_first_challenge ~ plot_group) %>%
  dplyr::filter(p < 0.05) %>%

  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(name = grouping_var_label, values = plot_group_color_vec, guide = "none") +
  scale_color_manual(name = grouping_var_label, values = plot_group_color_vec, guide = "none") +
  scale_shape_manual(name = "Adjuvant/Sex (shape)", values = adjSex_shape_vec_wts) +
  guides(shape = guide_legend(override.aes = list(fill = "grey50", color = "black"))) +
  ylab("Weight at first challenge (kg)") +

    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_blank(), axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")
  )

if (nrow(weights_stat_test) > 0) {

age_challenge_vax_only <- age_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(as.character(.data[[grouping_var_name]]) != naive_group_level) %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_ID, age_at_first_challenge)

age_vs_age_df <- age_immun_df %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_ID, plot_group, AdjSex, age_at_first_immunization) %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(age_challenge_vax_only, by = "Sample_ID") %>%
  dplyr::rename(study_group = plot_group)

age_vs_age_corr <- age_vs_age_df %>%
  dplyr::group_by(study_group) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    R = ifelse(dplyr::n() >= 3,
              signif(stats::cor(age_at_first_immunization, age_at_first_challenge,
                                method = "spearman", use = "pairwise"), 2),
              NA_real_),
    p = ifelse(dplyr::n() >= 3,
              signif(stats::cor.test(age_at_first_immunization, age_at_first_challenge,
                                     method = "spearman")$p.value, 2),
              NA_real_),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(label = paste0("R = ", R, ", p = ", p))

age_vs_age_corr_all <- age_vs_age_df %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    R = signif(stats::cor(age_at_first_immunization, age_at_first_challenge,
                          method = "spearman", use = "pairwise"), 2),
    p = signif(stats::cor.test(age_at_first_immunization, age_at_first_challenge,
                               method = "spearman")$p.value, 2)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(label = paste0("R = ", R, ", p = ", p))

age_vs_age_df_plot <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  age_vs_age_df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(facet_col = factor(as.character(study_group), all_panel_levels)),
  age_vs_age_df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(facet_col = factor("All", all_panel_levels))
)

  age_vs_age_corr %>%
    dplyr::mutate(facet_col = factor(as.character(study_group), all_panel_levels)),
  age_vs_age_corr_all %>%
    dplyr::mutate(facet_col = factor("All", all_panel_levels))
)

  ylab("Time from immunization to challenge (weeks)") +
  scale_y_continuous(n.breaks = 10) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_blank(), axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")
  )

if (nrow(delta_stat_test) > 0) {
  p <- p + ggpubr::stat_pvalue_manual(delta_stat_test, label = "p", tip.length = 0.01)
}

plot(p)

cat("\n")
cat(' \n \n')

```

This chunk replaces the need for `testSex` + `modelCoxbyAgeWeight` (and their `_outputtables` chunks) to run before `forestplots`. It pulls together only the data objects, covariate-centering logic, and helper functions that `build_covariate_panel()` / `build_interaction_panel()` actually consume.

Insert this as a new chunk, e.g. right before `forestplots`, named `forestplots_prep` with `include = FALSE` (no visible output needed):


``` {r forestplots_prep, include=FALSE}

## ============================================================
## Minimal data/function prep needed to produce the TOA forest plots
## in the `forestplots` chunk. Consolidated out of the old
## `testSex` + `modelCoxbyAgeWeight` chunks (and their `_outputtables`
## companions), which built up individual m1-m17 / mw*/mc*/mi* Cox
## models + LRTs for the "run models"/"output tables" sub-tabs that
## are no longer shown -- only the forest-plot machinery is kept here.
## ============================================================

## --------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Base animal-level data, studyF excluded (vaginal-ring
## confound). Platform/Sex/Adjuvant/Study as factors.
## --------------------------------------------------------
df_for_cox <- raw_df_TOA %>%
  dplyr::filter(studyLetterForMS != "studyF") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Platform = factor(Group_ignoreALFQA, levels = c("Naive", "DNA", "ALVAC")),
    Sex      = factor(Sex, levels = c("Male", "Female")),
    Adjuvant = factor(str_before_first(str_after_first(Group,"_"),"_"), levels = c("Alum", "ALFQA")),
    Study    = factor(studyLetterForMS)
  )

## --------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Continuous covariates (Weight, AgeChallenge, AgeImmun), pulled
## from the Weights & Dates section's *_base objects (already built
## earlier in the doc) and merged onto df_for_cox.
## --------------------------------------------------------
covariates_for_cox <- weights_df_base %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_ID, weight_at_first_challenge) %>%
  dplyr::full_join(
    age_df_base %>% dplyr::select(Sample_ID, age_at_first_challenge),
    by = "Sample_ID"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::full_join(
    age_immun_df_base %>% dplyr::select(Sample_ID, age_at_first_immunization),
    by = "Sample_ID"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Sample_ID = as.character(Sample_ID))

df_for_cox_cont <- df_for_cox %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Sample_ID = as.character(Sample_ID)) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(covariates_for_cox, by = "Sample_ID")

vax_only_df_cont <- dplyr::mutate(
  dplyr::filter(df_for_cox_cont, Platform != "Naive"),
  Platform = droplevels(Platform)
)

## --------------------------------------------------------
## Center Weight/AgeChallenge within each population subset
## separately (not one global mean), so "covariate = 0" in the
## interaction models means "at that subset's average animal".
## AgeImmun is NA for Naive animals, so it's only centered within
## the vaccinated-only subset.
## --------------------------------------------------------
center_var <- function(x) x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)

df_for_cox_cont <- df_for_cox_cont %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    weight_c   = center_var(weight_at_first_challenge),
    ageChall_c = center_var(age_at_first_challenge)
  )

vax_only_df_cont <- vax_only_df_cont %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    weight_c   = center_var(weight_at_first_challenge),
    ageChall_c = center_var(age_at_first_challenge),
    ageImmun_c = center_var(age_at_first_immunization)
  )

## --------------------------------------------------------
## 3. build_covariate_panel(): MAIN-EFFECT forest plot builder.
## Fits Platform + every subset of covariate_vars, extracts the
## Platform-of-interest coefficient from each, and assembles an
## UpSet-style covariate-adjustment matrix + forest plot.
## --------------------------------------------------------
build_covariate_panel <- function(data,
                                   platform_level,
                                   covariate_vars,
                                   covariate_labels,
                                   contrast_label,
                                   palette = c("green", "turquoise3", "purple4")) {

  other_level <- setdiff(unique(as.character(data$Platform)), platform_level)
  stopifnot(length(other_level) == 1)

  data <- data %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Platform = stats::relevel(factor(Platform), ref = other_level))

  term_of_interest <- paste0("Platform", platform_level)

  all_combo_rows <- purrr::map_dfr(0:length(covariate_vars), function(k) {

    combo_list <- if (k == 0) list(character(0)) else utils::combn(covariate_vars, k, simplify = FALSE)

    purrr::map_dfr(combo_list, function(covs) {

      rhs <- if (length(covs) == 0) "Platform" else paste("Platform", paste(covs, collapse = " + "), sep = " + ")

      fit <- survival::coxph(
        stats::as.formula(paste0("survival::Surv(TOA_adj, Infection_status) ~ ", rhs)),
        data = data
      )

      coef_row <- broom::tidy(fit, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
        dplyr::filter(term == term_of_interest)

      adjustment_label <- if (length(covs) == 0) {
        "Unadjusted"
      } else {
        paste0("+ ", paste(covariate_labels[covs], collapse = " + "))
      }

      dplyr::mutate(coef_row,
        adjustment   = adjustment_label,
        n_covariates = length(covs),
        covs_raw     = list(covs)
      )
    })
  })

  all_combo_rows <- all_combo_rows %>%
    dplyr::rowwise() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      sort_key = paste(as.integer(covariate_vars %in% covs_raw), collapse = "")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()

  panel_rows <- all_combo_rows %>%
    dplyr::arrange(n_covariates, desc(sort_key)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      adjustment = factor(adjustment, rev(unique(adjustment))),
      row_id     = as.integer(adjustment),
      p_label    = dplyr::if_else(
        p.value < 0.001,
        "<0.001",
        formatC(p.value, digits = 3, format = "f")
      ),
      sig        = p.value < 0.05
    )

  ## --- UpSet membership matrix ---
  upset_long <- panel_rows %>%
    dplyr::select(adjustment, row_id, covs_raw) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(covariate = list(covariate_vars)) %>%
    tidyr::unnest(covariate) %>%
    dplyr::rowwise() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(is_member = covariate %in% covs_raw) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      covariate_label = factor(covariate_labels[covariate], levels = covariate_labels[covariate_vars])
    )

  upset_segments <- upset_long %>%
    dplyr::filter(is_member) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(row_id, adjustment) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      x_min = min(as.integer(covariate_label)),
      x_max = max(as.integer(covariate_label)),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  p_upset <- ggplot() +
    geom_point(
      data = upset_long,
      aes(x = covariate_label, y = adjustment),
      color = "grey85", size = 2.2
    ) +
    geom_segment(
      data = upset_segments,
      aes(x = x_min, xend = x_max, y = adjustment, yend = adjustment),
      color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.6
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data = dplyr::filter(upset_long, is_member),
      aes(x = covariate_label, y = adjustment),
      color = "grey20", size = 2.6
    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey93"),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x.top    = element_text(size = 7, angle = 40, hjust = 0),
      axis.text.y        = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y       = element_blank(),
      plot.margin        = margin(r = 2)
    )

  ## --- p-value column ---
  p_pvalue <- ggplot(panel_rows, aes(x = 1, y = adjustment)) +
    geom_text(aes(label = p_label), size = 3, hjust = 0.5) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.9, 1.1), breaks = NULL) +
    labs(x = "p-value", y = NULL) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      panel.grid   = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y  = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      panel.border = element_blank(),
      plot.margin  = margin(l = 2)
    )

  ## --- forest plot ---
  n_total  <- nrow(data)
  n_events <- sum(data$Infection_status, na.rm = TRUE)

  p_forest <- ggplot(panel_rows, aes(x = estimate, y = adjustment, color = factor(n_covariates))) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high), height = 0.2) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = sig), size = 2.2) +
    scale_shape_manual(name = "p < 0.05", values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 1)) +
    scale_color_manual(
      name = "# covariates\nadjusted for",
      values = grDevices::colorRampPalette(palette)(length(covariate_vars) + 1)
    ) +
    scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 10)) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.1, 10)) +
    labs(x = "Hazard Ratio (log scale)", y = NULL,
         title = paste0(contrast_label, " effect across all covariate-adjustment combinations"),
         subtitle = paste0(nrow(panel_rows),
                           " models (all subsets of ", paste(covariate_labels[covariate_vars], collapse = ", "),
                           "); n=", n_total, ", ", n_events, " events")) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "bottom",
          plot.margin = margin(l = 2, r = 2))

  p_combined <- p_upset + p_forest + p_pvalue +
    patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(1, 2.4, 0.4))

  list(rows = panel_rows, plot = p_combined)
}

## --------------------------------------------------------
## 4. build_interaction_panel(): fits every combination of
## Platform*covariate interaction terms up to `max_size` at once,
## and assembles the analogous UpSet + forest panel for interaction
## hazard ratios.
## --------------------------------------------------------
build_interaction_panel <- function(data,
                                     platform_level,
                                     covariate_vars,
                                     covariate_labels,
                                     contrast_label,
                                     max_size = length(covariate_vars),
                                     color_low = "turquoise3",
                                     color_high = "purple4") {

  other_level <- setdiff(unique(as.character(data$Platform)), platform_level)
  stopifnot(length(other_level) == 1)

  data <- data %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Platform = stats::relevel(factor(Platform), ref = other_level))

  term_of_interest <- paste0("Platform", platform_level)

  interaction_rows <- purrr::map_dfr(1:max_size, function(k) {

    combo_list <- utils::combn(covariate_vars, k, simplify = FALSE)

    purrr::map_dfr(combo_list, function(covs) {

      rhs <- paste(paste0("Platform * ", covs), collapse = " + ")

      fit <- survival::coxph(
        stats::as.formula(paste0(
          "survival::Surv(TOA_adj, Infection_status) ~ ", rhs
        )),
        data = data
      )

      fit_tidy <- broom::tidy(fit, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)

      purrr::map_dfr(covs, function(cov) {

        interaction_prefix <- paste0(term_of_interest, ":", cov)

        matched_rows <- fit_tidy %>%
          dplyr::filter(startsWith(term, interaction_prefix))

        if (nrow(matched_rows) == 0) {
          warning(paste0("No interaction term matched for prefix: ", interaction_prefix,
                         " -- available terms: ", paste(fit_tidy$term, collapse = ", ")))
        }

        matched_rows %>%
          dplyr::mutate(
            covariate    = unname(covariate_labels[cov]),
            active_cov   = cov,
            covs_raw     = list(covs),
            n_covariates = length(covs),
            p_label      = dplyr::if_else(
              p.value < 0.001,
              "<0.001",
              formatC(p.value, digits = 3, format = "f")
            ),
            sig          = p.value < 0.05
          )
      })
    })
  })

  interaction_rows <- interaction_rows %>%
    dplyr::rowwise() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      sort_key = paste(as.integer(covariate_vars %in% covs_raw), collapse = "")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()

  interaction_rows <- interaction_rows %>%
    dplyr::mutate(active_cov_order = match(active_cov, covariate_vars)) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(active_cov_order, n_covariates, desc(sort_key)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      row_label = paste0(covariate, " | model ", dplyr::row_number()),
      row_label = factor(row_label, rev(unique(row_label))),
      row_id    = as.integer(row_label)
    )

  covariate_color_vec <- setNames(
    grDevices::colorRampPalette(c(color_low, color_high))(length(covariate_vars)),
    covariate_vars
  )

  upset_long <- interaction_rows %>%
    dplyr::select(row_label, row_id, covs_raw, active_cov) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(covariate_col = list(covariate_vars)) %>%
    tidyr::unnest(covariate_col) %>%
    dplyr::rowwise() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      is_member = covariate_col %in% covs_raw,
      is_active = covariate_col == active_cov
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      covariate_label = factor(covariate_labels[covariate_col], levels = covariate_labels[covariate_vars]),
      dot_color = ifelse(is_active, unname(covariate_color_vec[covariate_col]), NA_character_)
    )

  upset_segments <- upset_long %>%
    dplyr::filter(is_member) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(row_id, row_label) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      x_min = min(as.integer(covariate_label)),
      x_max = max(as.integer(covariate_label)),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  p_upset <- ggplot() +
    geom_point(
      data = upset_long,
      aes(x = covariate_label, y = row_label),
      color = "grey85", size = 2.2
    ) +
    geom_segment(
      data = upset_segments,
      aes(x = x_min, xend = x_max, y = row_label, yend = row_label),
      color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.6
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data = dplyr::filter(upset_long, is_member, !is_active),
      aes(x = covariate_label, y = row_label),
      color = "grey20", size = 2.6
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data = dplyr::filter(upset_long, is_active),
      aes(x = covariate_label, y = row_label, color = dot_color),
      size = 3.4
    ) +
    scale_color_identity() +
    scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey93"),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x.top    = element_text(size = 7, angle = 40, hjust = 0),
      axis.text.y        = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y       = element_blank(),
      plot.margin        = margin(r = 2)
    )

  p_pvalue <- ggplot(interaction_rows, aes(x = 1, y = row_label)) +
    geom_text(aes(label = p_label), size = 3, hjust = 0.5) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.9, 1.1), breaks = NULL) +
    labs(x = "p-value", y = NULL) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      panel.grid   = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y  = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      panel.border = element_blank(),
      plot.margin  = margin(l = 2)
    )

  n_total  <- nrow(data)
  n_events <- sum(data$Infection_status, na.rm = TRUE)

  p_forest <- ggplot(interaction_rows, aes(x = estimate, y = row_label, color = active_cov)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high), height = 0.2) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = sig), size = 2.2) +
    scale_shape_manual(name = "p < 0.05", values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 1)) +
    scale_color_manual(
      name = "Interaction\ncovariate",
      values = covariate_color_vec,
      breaks = covariate_vars,
      labels = unname(covariate_labels[covariate_vars])
    ) +
    scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 10)) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.1, 10)) +
    labs(x = "Interaction Hazard Ratio (log scale)", y = NULL,
         title = paste0("Does any covariate modify the ", contrast_label, " effect?"),
         subtitle = paste0(nrow(interaction_rows),
                           " interaction terms across univariate + joint models (up to ", max_size,
                           " simultaneous interactions); n=", n_total, ", ", n_events, " events")) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "bottom",
          plot.margin = margin(l = 2, r = 2))

  p_combined <- p_upset + p_forest + p_pvalue +
    patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(1, 2.4, 0.4))

  list(rows = interaction_rows, plot = p_combined)
}

## --------------------------------------------------------
## 5. Covariate label lookup and covariate-set definitions per
## contrast (unchanged from the original testSex/modelCoxbyAgeWeight
## chunks' covariate-set definitions).
## --------------------------------------------------------
covariate_labels_full <- c(
  Sex        = "Sex",
  Adjuvant   = "Adjuvant",
  weight_c   = "Weight",
  ageChall_c = "Age at Challenge",
  ageImmun_c = "Age at Immunization"
)

## ALVAC vs DNA: vaccinated-only, so Adjuvant is meaningful -> keep it
covars_with_adjuvant <- c("Sex", "Adjuvant", "weight_c", "ageChall_c", "ageImmun_c")

## ALVAC vs Naive / DNA vs Naive: Naive animals have NA Adjuvant and
## no immunization date (never immunized) -> drop both
covars_without_adjuvant <- c("Sex", "weight_c", "ageChall_c")

## Covariate set for the INTERACTION panel specifically. AgeChallenge
## and AgeImmun are highly collinear (fixed immunization-to-challenge
## interval), so only AgeChallenge is used as a representative for the
## interaction panel -- this lets ALVAC vs DNA's interaction panel go
## up to size 4 (every non-empty subset) without ever combining
## AgeChallenge and AgeImmun.
covars_with_adjuvant_forInteraction <- c("Sex", "Adjuvant", "weight_c", "ageChall_c")

```



```{r forestplots, results='asis', fig.height=8, fig.width=8}



## --------------------------------------------------------
## Generalized builder for the UpSet + forest + p-value combo panel.
## Wrapped as a function so the same logic can be reused across all
## three platform contrasts (ALVAC vs DNA, ALVAC vs Naive, DNA vs
## Naive) without copy-pasting the covariate-subset/model-fitting/
## plotting code three times.
##
## Arguments:
##   data           -- the dataframe to fit on (already filtered to
##                      exactly the two Platform levels in this contrast)
##   platform_level  -- the Platform value that is the *comparison of
##                      interest* (e.g. "ALVAC"); everything else in
##                      `data`'s Platform column is treated as the
##                      reference level for coxph's contrast coding
##   covariate_vars  -- character vector of covariate column names
##                      available for this contrast (Adjuvant is
##                      dropped for the two Naive contrasts, since
##                      Naive animals were never assigned an adjuvant
##                      and the column is NA for them)
##   covariate_labels -- named vector, covariate_vars -> display label
##   contrast_label  -- string used in plot titles/subtitles and the
##                      cat() tabset header
##   n_total / n_events -- sample size / event count to report in the
##                      subtitle (computed from `data` if not supplied)
## --------------------------------------------------------

build_covariate_panel <- function(data,
                                   platform_level,
                                   covariate_vars,
                                   covariate_labels,
                                   contrast_label,
                                   palette = c("green", "turquoise3", "purple4")) {

  ## ensure the platform of interest is the level coxph reports a
  ## coefficient for (i.e. NOT the reference level)
  other_level <- setdiff(unique(as.character(data$Platform)), platform_level)
  stopifnot(length(other_level) == 1)  # this function expects exactly a 2-level contrast

  data <- data %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Platform = stats::relevel(factor(Platform), ref = other_level))

  term_of_interest <- paste0("Platform", platform_level)

  ## build every subset of covariate_vars, from size 0 (unadjusted) up
  ## to size length(covariate_vars) (full model), and fit Platform +
  ## that subset each time
  all_combo_rows <- purrr::map_dfr(0:length(covariate_vars), function(k) {

    combo_list <- if (k == 0) list(character(0)) else utils::combn(covariate_vars, k, simplify = FALSE)

    purrr::map_dfr(combo_list, function(covs) {

      rhs <- if (length(covs) == 0) "Platform" else paste("Platform", paste(covs, collapse = " + "), sep = " + ")

      fit <- survival::coxph(
        stats::as.formula(paste0("survival::Surv(TOA_adj, Infection_status) ~ ", rhs)),
        data = data
      )

      coef_row <- broom::tidy(fit, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
        dplyr::filter(term == term_of_interest)

      adjustment_label <- if (length(covs) == 0) {
        "Unadjusted"
      } else {
        paste0("+ ", paste(covariate_labels[covs], collapse = " + "))
      }

      dplyr::mutate(coef_row,
        adjustment   = adjustment_label,
        n_covariates = length(covs),
        covs_raw     = list(covs)
      )
    })
  })

  ## sort within each n_covariates tier by column order (binary string
  ## over covariate_vars, in that order) rather than alphabetically --
  ## produces the standard UpSet "staircase" pattern
  all_combo_rows <- all_combo_rows %>%
    dplyr::rowwise() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      sort_key = paste(as.integer(covariate_vars %in% covs_raw), collapse = "")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()

  panel_rows <- all_combo_rows %>%
    dplyr::arrange(n_covariates, desc(sort_key)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      adjustment = factor(adjustment, rev(unique(adjustment))),
      row_id     = as.integer(adjustment),
      p_label    = dplyr::if_else(
        p.value < 0.001,
        "<0.001",
        formatC(p.value, digits = 3, format = "f")
      ),
      sig        = p.value < 0.05   ### NEW
    )

  ## --- UpSet membership matrix ---
  upset_long <- panel_rows %>%
    dplyr::select(adjustment, row_id, covs_raw) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(covariate = list(covariate_vars)) %>%
    tidyr::unnest(covariate) %>%
    dplyr::rowwise() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(is_member = covariate %in% covs_raw) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      covariate_label = factor(covariate_labels[covariate], levels = covariate_labels[covariate_vars])
    )

  upset_segments <- upset_long %>%
    dplyr::filter(is_member) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(row_id, adjustment) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      x_min = min(as.integer(covariate_label)),
      x_max = max(as.integer(covariate_label)),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  p_upset <- ggplot() +
    geom_point(
      data = upset_long,
      aes(x = covariate_label, y = adjustment),
      color = "grey85", size = 2.2
    ) +
    geom_segment(
      data = upset_segments,
      aes(x = x_min, xend = x_max, y = adjustment, yend = adjustment),
      color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.6
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data = dplyr::filter(upset_long, is_member),
      aes(x = covariate_label, y = adjustment),
      color = "grey20", size = 2.6
    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey93"),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x.top    = element_text(size = 7, angle = 40, hjust = 0),
      axis.text.y        = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y       = element_blank(),
      plot.margin        = margin(r = 2)
    )

  ## --- p-value column ---
  p_pvalue <- ggplot(panel_rows, aes(x = 1, y = adjustment)) +
    geom_text(aes(label = p_label), size = 3, hjust = 0.5) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.9, 1.1), breaks = NULL) +
    labs(x = "p-value", y = NULL) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      panel.grid   = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y  = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      panel.border = element_blank(),
      plot.margin  = margin(l = 2)
    )

  ## --- forest plot ---
  n_total  <- nrow(data)
  n_events <- sum(data$Infection_status, na.rm = TRUE)

p_forest <- ggplot(panel_rows, aes(x = estimate, y = adjustment, color = factor(n_covariates))) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high), height = 0.2) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = sig), size = 2.2) +
    scale_shape_manual(name = "p < 0.05", values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 1)) +
    scale_color_manual(
      name = "# covariates\nadjusted for",
      values = grDevices::colorRampPalette(palette)(length(covariate_vars) + 1)
    ) +
    scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 10)#, limits = c(0.1,10)
                  ) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.1, 10)) + 
    labs(x = "Hazard Ratio (log scale)", y = NULL,
         title = paste0(contrast_label, " effect across all covariate-adjustment combinations"),
         subtitle = paste0(nrow(panel_rows),
                           " models (all subsets of ", paste(covariate_labels[covariate_vars], collapse = ", "),
                           "); n=", n_total, ", ", n_events, " events")) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "bottom",
          plot.margin = margin(l = 2, r = 2))

  p_combined <- p_upset + p_forest + p_pvalue +
    patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(1, 2.4, 0.4))

  list(rows = panel_rows, plot = p_combined)
}

## --------------------------------------------------------
## Interaction panel: for a given contrast, fits every combination of
## Platform*covariate interaction terms up to `max_size` interactions
## at once (e.g. max_size=2 fits Platform*Sex + Platform*Weight
## jointly, in addition to each univariate Platform*cov alone).
##
## Each row of the output is ONE interaction term (e.g.
## PlatformALVAC:weight_c, or PlatformALVAC:SexFemale) from ONE fitted
## model -- so a model with 2 interaction terms contributes 2 rows.
## The UpSet matrix (below) shows, per row, every covariate that was
## interacted with Platform in that row's model, with the "active"
## covariate (the one this row's HR/p-value describe) drawn larger and
## in color, and any "co-adjusting" covariates (also interacted with
## Platform in the same model, but not this row's estimate) drawn as
## smaller grey dots.
##
## ROW ORDER: rows are grouped into blocks by active covariate, and
## those BLOCKS are ordered by the covariate's POSITION in
## covariate_vars (matching the UpSet matrix's left-to-right column
## order) rather than alphabetically -- e.g. Sex/Adjuvant/Weight/
## AgeChallenge if that's the order covariate_vars was supplied in,
## not the alphabetical Adjuvant/AgeChallenge/Sex/Weight that grouping
## directly on the covariate label would produce. WITHIN each
## covariate's block, rows follow the same staircase order
## build_covariate_panel() uses (increasing n_covariates, then
## desc(sort_key)), so e.g. all of Weight's univariate/pair/triple/
## quad rows appear together, ordered from simplest to most-adjusted.
##
## NOTE ON AgeChallenge/AgeImmun: these are highly collinear (fixed
## immunization-to-challenge interval), so only AgeChallenge is used
## here as their stand-in -- AgeImmun is never included in this panel,
## matching the covariate_vars passed in (which should already exclude
## it, or include only one of the pair).
##
## NOTE ON FACTOR COVARIATES: for factor covariates (Sex, Adjuvant),
## coxph/broom names the interaction term using the base term PLUS the
## non-reference factor level -- e.g. "PlatformALVAC:SexFemale", NOT
## "PlatformALVAC:Sex". Continuous covariates (weight_c, ageChall_c)
## have no level suffix, so "PlatformALVAC:weight_c" is already exact.
## Matching on startsWith() rather than exact equality handles both
## cases uniformly.
## --------------------------------------------------------
build_interaction_panel <- function(data,
                                     platform_level,
                                     covariate_vars,
                                     covariate_labels,
                                     contrast_label,
                                     max_size = length(covariate_vars),
                                     color_low = "turquoise3",
                                     color_high = "purple4") {

  other_level <- setdiff(unique(as.character(data$Platform)), platform_level)
  stopifnot(length(other_level) == 1)

  data <- data %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Platform = stats::relevel(factor(Platform), ref = other_level))

  term_of_interest <- paste0("Platform", platform_level)

  interaction_rows <- purrr::map_dfr(1:max_size, function(k) {

    combo_list <- utils::combn(covariate_vars, k, simplify = FALSE)

    purrr::map_dfr(combo_list, function(covs) {

      rhs <- paste(paste0("Platform * ", covs), collapse = " + ")

      fit <- survival::coxph(
        stats::as.formula(paste0(
          "survival::Surv(TOA_adj, Infection_status) ~ ", rhs
        )),
        data = data
      )

      fit_tidy <- broom::tidy(fit, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)

      purrr::map_dfr(covs, function(cov) {

        interaction_prefix <- paste0(term_of_interest, ":", cov)

        matched_rows <- fit_tidy %>%
          dplyr::filter(startsWith(term, interaction_prefix))

        if (nrow(matched_rows) == 0) {
          warning(paste0("No interaction term matched for prefix: ", interaction_prefix,
                         " -- available terms: ", paste(fit_tidy$term, collapse = ", ")))
        }

        matched_rows %>%
          dplyr::mutate(
            covariate    = unname(covariate_labels[cov]),
            active_cov   = cov,
            covs_raw     = list(covs),
            n_covariates = length(covs),
            p_label      = dplyr::if_else(
              p.value < 0.001,
              "<0.001",
              formatC(p.value, digits = 3, format = "f")
            ),
            sig          = p.value < 0.05   ### NEW
          )
      })
    })
  })

  interaction_rows <- interaction_rows %>%
    dplyr::rowwise() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      sort_key = paste(as.integer(covariate_vars %in% covs_raw), collapse = "")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()

  interaction_rows <- interaction_rows %>%
    dplyr::mutate(active_cov_order = match(active_cov, covariate_vars)) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(active_cov_order, n_covariates, desc(sort_key)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      row_label = paste0(covariate, " | model ", dplyr::row_number()),
      row_label = factor(row_label, rev(unique(row_label))),
      row_id    = as.integer(row_label)
    )

  ## one fixed color per covariate, interpolated between color_low and
  ## color_high across covariate_vars IN ORDER -- shared by both the
  ## UpSet matrix's active-covariate dot and the forest plot's
  ## whiskers/point, so the same covariate always gets the same color
  ## in both panels. Two explicit named colors (not grey) so nothing
  ## lands near-black.
  covariate_color_vec <- setNames(
    grDevices::colorRampPalette(c(color_low, color_high))(length(covariate_vars)),
    covariate_vars
  )

  upset_long <- interaction_rows %>%
    dplyr::select(row_label, row_id, covs_raw, active_cov) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(covariate_col = list(covariate_vars)) %>%
    tidyr::unnest(covariate_col) %>%
    dplyr::rowwise() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      is_member = covariate_col %in% covs_raw,
      is_active = covariate_col == active_cov
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      covariate_label = factor(covariate_labels[covariate_col], levels = covariate_labels[covariate_vars]),
      dot_color = ifelse(is_active, unname(covariate_color_vec[covariate_col]), NA_character_)
    )

  upset_segments <- upset_long %>%
    dplyr::filter(is_member) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(row_id, row_label) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      x_min = min(as.integer(covariate_label)),
      x_max = max(as.integer(covariate_label)),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  p_upset <- ggplot() +
    geom_point(
      data = upset_long,
      aes(x = covariate_label, y = row_label),
      color = "grey85", size = 2.2
    ) +
    geom_segment(
      data = upset_segments,
      aes(x = x_min, xend = x_max, y = row_label, yend = row_label),
      color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.6
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data = dplyr::filter(upset_long, is_member, !is_active),
      aes(x = covariate_label, y = row_label),
      color = "grey20", size = 2.6
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data = dplyr::filter(upset_long, is_active),
      aes(x = covariate_label, y = row_label, color = dot_color),
      size = 3.4
    ) +
    scale_color_identity() +
    scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey93"),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x.top    = element_text(size = 7, angle = 40, hjust = 0),
      axis.text.y        = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y       = element_blank(),
      plot.margin        = margin(r = 2)
    )

  p_pvalue <- ggplot(interaction_rows, aes(x = 1, y = row_label)) +
    geom_text(aes(label = p_label), size = 3, hjust = 0.5) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.9, 1.1), breaks = NULL) +
    labs(x = "p-value", y = NULL) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      panel.grid   = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y  = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      panel.border = element_blank(),
      plot.margin  = margin(l = 2)
    )

  n_total  <- nrow(data)
  n_events <- sum(data$Infection_status, na.rm = TRUE)

  ## forest plot color: same covariate_color_vec as the UpSet matrix's
  ## active dot -- mapped directly via scale_color_manual(values=...),
  ## NOT a ramp computed separately here, so the two panels cannot
  ## drift out of sync with each other again.
 p_forest <- ggplot(interaction_rows, aes(x = estimate, y = row_label, color = active_cov)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high), height = 0.2) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = sig), size = 2.2) +
    scale_shape_manual(name = "p < 0.05", values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 1)) +
    scale_color_manual(
      name = "Interaction\ncovariate",
      values = covariate_color_vec,
      breaks = covariate_vars,
      labels = unname(covariate_labels[covariate_vars])
    ) +
    scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 10)) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.1, 10)) +
    labs(x = "Interaction Hazard Ratio (log scale)", y = NULL,
         title = paste0("Does any covariate modify the ", contrast_label, " effect?"),
         subtitle = paste0(nrow(interaction_rows),
                           " interaction terms across univariate + joint models (up to ", max_size,
                           " simultaneous interactions); n=", n_total, ", ", n_events, " events")) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "bottom",
          plot.margin = margin(l = 2, r = 2))

  p_combined <- p_upset + p_forest + p_pvalue +
    patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(1, 2.4, 0.4))

  list(rows = interaction_rows, plot = p_combined)
}




## --------------------------------------------------------
## Render a DT table of the stats underlying a forest plot (either
## the main-effect panel from build_covariate_panel() or the
## interaction panel from build_interaction_panel()). Both return a
## list with $rows containing a broom::tidy()-style data frame plus
## the bookkeeping columns added along the way (adjustment/covs_raw/
## n_covariates/sort_key for main-effect; row_label/active_cov/etc for
## interaction). This just picks sensible display columns, formats
## them, and prints a DT::datatable.
## --------------------------------------------------------
print_forest_stats_table <- function(panel_result, is_interaction = FALSE) {

  df <- panel_result$rows

  if (is.null(df) || nrow(df) == 0) {
    cat(" ", "no model results available for this panel", "\n")
    cat("\n")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  if (is_interaction) {
    display_df <- df %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        covariates_in_model = purrr::map_chr(covs_raw, ~ paste(unlist(.x), collapse = " + ")),
        HR_CI = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f\u2013%.3f)", estimate, conf.low, conf.high)
      ) %>%
      dplyr::select(
        `Active covariate` = covariate,
        `Covariates in model` = covariates_in_model,
        Term = term,
        `HR (95% CI)` = HR_CI,
        `p-value` = p_label,
        p_numeric = p.value
      )
  } else {
    display_df <- df %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        HR_CI = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f\u2013%.3f)", estimate, conf.low, conf.high)
      ) %>%
      dplyr::select(
        Adjustment = adjustment,
        Term = term,
        `HR (95% CI)` = HR_CI,
        `p-value` = p_label,
        p_numeric = p.value
      )
  }

  display_df %>%
    DT::datatable(
      extensions = 'Buttons',
      options = list(dom = 'Blfrtip',
                     buttons = c('copy', 'csv', 'excel', 'pdf', 'print'),
                     iDisplayLength = 25,
                     lengthMenu = list(c(10, 25, 50, -1), c(10, 25, 50, "All")),
                     columnDefs = list(list(visible = FALSE,
                                            targets = which(colnames(display_df) == "p_numeric") - 1))),
    ) %>%
    DT::formatStyle(
      columns = colnames(display_df),
      valueColumns = "p_numeric",
      color = DT::styleInterval(0.05, c("blue", "black")),
      fontWeight = DT::styleInterval(0.05, c("bold", "normal"))
    ) %>%
    htmltools::tagList() %>%
    print()
}





## --------------------------------------------------------
## Covariate sets per contrast.
##  - ALVAC vs DNA: vaccinated-only, so Adjuvant is meaningful -> keep it
##  - ALVAC vs Naive / DNA vs Naive: Naive animals have NA Adjuvant
##    (never assigned one), so it's dropped from these two models
## --------------------------------------------------------

covariate_labels_full <- c(
  Sex        = "Sex",
  Adjuvant   = "Adjuvant",
  weight_c   = "Weight",
  ageChall_c = "Age at Challenge",
  ageImmun_c = "Age at Immunization"
)

covars_with_adjuvant    <- c("Sex", "Adjuvant", "weight_c", "ageChall_c", "ageImmun_c")

## ageImmun_c is ALSO dropped here (not just Adjuvant): per the Rmd,
## age_at_first_immunization -- and therefore its centered version,
## ageImmun_c -- is only ever computed on vax_only_df_cont (see
## age_immun_df_base, which explicitly filters out Naive animals
## before centering, since naive animals were never immunized and
## have no immunization date to center). df_for_cox_cont (the "all
## animals" frame the two Naive contrasts are filtered from) never
## gets an ageImmun_c column at all, so referencing it in a model
## formula on df_alvac_naive/df_dna_naive throws "object 'ageImmun_c'
## not found" -- which is exactly the error this fixes.
covars_without_adjuvant <- c("Sex", "weight_c", "ageChall_c")

## --------------------------------------------------------
## Covariate set for the INTERACTION panel specifically (used only by
## build_interaction_panel(), not build_covariate_panel()). AgeChallenge
## and AgeImmun are highly collinear (fixed immunization-to-challenge
## interval per protocol), so only one of the pair is used as a
## representative -- AgeChallenge, per instruction -- rather than
## fitting both. This drops the interaction panel for ALVAC vs DNA to
## 4 usable covariates instead of 5, so it can go all the way to size
## 4 (every non-empty subset) without ever combining AgeChallenge and
## AgeImmun.

covars_with_adjuvant_forInteraction <- c("Sex", "Adjuvant", "weight_c", "ageChall_c")
```

```{r diffBetweenGroups, results='asis', fig.height=18, fig.width=8}
### fixed pale ("baseline") colors per group, rather than computed lightening
baseline_pale_color_vec <- c(
  "DNA"   = "#FFD6AE",
  "ALVAC" = "#C4FDFF"
)

### helper: build a small custom legend grob showing, per group (row),
### a Baseline swatch (pale fill, full-color outline) and a non-baseline
### swatch (full-color fill, black outline), with column headers
build_colorTime_legend <- function(group_colors_to_use, baseline_pale_color_vec, nonbaseline_label = "non-baseline"){
  
  legend_df <- data.frame(
    group = rep(names(group_colors_to_use), each = 2),
    timepoint = rep(c("Baseline", nonbaseline_label), times = length(group_colors_to_use))
  ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      group = factor(group, names(group_colors_to_use)),
      timepoint = factor(timepoint, c("Baseline", nonbaseline_label)),
      fill_col = ifelse(timepoint == "Baseline",
                        #unname(baseline_pale_color_vec[as.character(group)]),
                        "white",
                        unname(group_colors_to_use[as.character(group)])),
      outline_col = ifelse(timepoint == "Baseline",
                           unname(group_colors_to_use[as.character(group)]),
                           "black"),
      y_pos = as.numeric(group),
      x_pos = as.numeric(timepoint)
    )
  
  legend_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(legend_df, ggplot2::aes(x = x_pos, y = y_pos)) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(shape = 22, size = 8, stroke = 2.2,
                        fill = legend_df$fill_col, color = legend_df$outline_col) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:2, labels = levels(legend_df$timepoint),
                                limits = c(0.5, 2.5), position = "top") +
    ggplot2::scale_y_reverse(breaks = 1:length(unique(legend_df$group)),
                             labels = levels(legend_df$group),
                             limits = c(length(unique(legend_df$group)) + 0.5, 0.5)) +
    ggplot2::theme_void() +
    ggplot2::theme(
      axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 10, face = "bold", vjust = 0),
      axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(size = 10, face = "bold", hjust = 1, margin = ggplot2::margin(r = 4)),
      plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(5,5,5,5)
    )
  
  legend_plot
}

### for each dataset type

for(curr_ds in ds_to_use){
  cat("#### ",paste0(curr_ds," {.tabset}"),"\n")
  cat('\n')
  
  
  ## full_df only has the variables in columns and the factorized group (plus any other covariates if they are in the model)
  
  full_df <- curr_phen_long %>%
    ## trim to only Animal_comp_time, var and curr_ds
    dplyr::select(c(Animal_comp_time,variable,!!rlang::sym(curr_ds))) %>%
    ## move comp and timepoint to var
    dplyr::mutate(Sample_ID = strex::str_before_first(Animal_comp_time,"__"),
                  var_comp_time = paste0(variable,"__",strex::str_after_first(Animal_comp_time,"__")),
                  Animal_comp_time = NULL,
                  variable = NULL) %>%
    ## make wider
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "var_comp_time", values_from = all_of(curr_ds)) %>%
    ## remove columns with only NA
    dplyr::select(where(function(x) !all(is.na(x)))) %>%
    ### add in group
    dplyr::left_join(data.frame(unique(phen_long[,c("Sample_ID",group_var_to_use)])) %>%
                       dplyr::mutate(Sample_ID = paste0("m",Sample_ID)), by = "Sample_ID") %>%
    dplyr::rename(Group_to_use=!!rlang::sym(group_var_to_use)) %>%
    tibble::column_to_rownames("Sample_ID") %>%
    ### factorize group
    dplyr::mutate(Group_f = factor(Group_to_use, intersect(
      names(group_colors_to_use),
      unique(data.frame(curr_phen_long)[,group_var_to_use])))) %>%
    dplyr::select(-Group_to_use)
  
  
  
  p_value_df1 <- data.frame("rowname"=colnames(full_df)) %>%
    dplyr::filter(rowname != "Group_f")
  
  ######### if have any columns at all
  if(dim(full_df)[2]>1){
    
    
    
    
    for (g in 1:nrow(groups_to_compare)){
      
      
      
      
      ###### only if you have both groups
      if(length(which(full_df$Group_f == groups_to_compare$group1[g])) != 0 &
         length(which(full_df$Group_f == groups_to_compare$group2[g])) != 0){
        
        
        ## wilcoxon for pairwise differences
        
        ## generate matrix with only variables for stats 
        Assay_mat <- as.matrix(full_df[,p_value_df1$rowname])
        
        ## kruskal test for if there are differences between any groups - not necessary since only 2 groups with these timepoints
        # kruskal_p_raw <- apply(Assay_mat, 2, function(x) kruskal.test(x ~ Group_f, data = full_df)$p.value)
        # kruskal_p_adj <- p.adjust(kruskal_p_raw, method = 'BH')
        
        
        
        
        ## if there are no NAs for the group comparison (i.e. we have animals in both groups for the assay/timepoint)
        if(length(which(is.na(Assay_mat[rownames(full_df)[which(full_df$Group_f == groups_to_compare$group1[g] | 
                                                                full_df$Group_f == groups_to_compare$group2[g])]
                                        ,]))) == 0)
          #then calculate as usual
        {
          curr_p_raw <- apply(Assay_mat, 2, function(x) stats::wilcox.test(x[Group_f %in% c(
            groups_to_compare$group1[g], groups_to_compare$group2[g])] ~ Group_f[Group_f %in% c(
              groups_to_compare$group1[g], groups_to_compare$group2[g])], data = full_df)$p.value)
          curr_p_adj <- stats::p.adjust(curr_p_raw, method = 'BH') 
          ##### since have zeros, can't use the wilcox function
          # curr_est <- apply(Assay_mat, 2, function(x) wilcox.test(x[Group_f %in% c(
          #   groups_to_compare$group1[g], groups_to_compare$group2[g])] ~ Group_f[Group_f %in% c(
          #     groups_to_compare$group1[g], groups_to_compare$group2[g])], data = full_df, conf.int = TRUE)$estimate)
          #### https://aakinshin.net/posts/r-hodges-lehmann-problems/
          
          ###### first define function
          hl <- function(x, y = NULL) {
            if (is.null(y)) {
              walsh <- outer(x, x, "+") / 2
              stats::median(walsh[lower.tri(walsh, diag = TRUE)], na.rm = TRUE)
            } else {
              stats::median(outer(x, y, "-"), na.rm = TRUE)
            }
          }
          
          #### then generate the vector
          curr_est <- c()
          curr_x_len <- c()
          curr_y_len <- c()
          for(i in colnames(Assay_mat)){
            x <- full_df[which(full_df$Group_f == groups_to_compare$group2[g]),i]
            y <- full_df[which(full_df$Group_f == groups_to_compare$group1[g]),i]
            ce <- hl(x, y)
            names(ce) <- i
            curr_est <- c(curr_est,ce)
            curr_x_len <- c(curr_x_len,length(x))
            curr_y_len <- c(curr_y_len,length(y))
          }
          
          
          #### combine to df
          
          curr_p_df <- data.frame(curr_p_raw, curr_p_adj, curr_est,
                                  curr_x_len,curr_y_len) %>%
            tibble::rownames_to_column() 
          colnames(curr_p_df) <- c("rowname",
                                   
                                   paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__p_raw"),
                                   paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__p_adj"),
                                   paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__est"),
                                   paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__Ngroup2"),
                                   paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__Ngroup1")
          )
          
          ## but if there are all NAs for a group (i.e. one of the groups is missing the assay/timepoint), remove rows from Assay mat that have NAs (i.e. assay/timepoints that only have one of the groups to compare)
        } else {
          ### removes column if rows have NAs
          #new_curr_df <- full_df[,colSums(is.na(full_df))==0] %>%
          #  column_to_rownames("ID")
          
          ## since a few assays have a stray NA in the one group
          ### trim to only the groups being compared
          trim_df1 <- full_df[which(full_df$Group_f == groups_to_compare$group1[g]),] #%>% dplyr::select(-Group_f)
          columns_with_noNAs1 <- colnames(trim_df1)[which(colSums(is.na(trim_df1)) == 0)]
          columns_with_someNAs1 <- colnames(trim_df1)[which(colSums(is.na(trim_df1)) > 0 & colSums(is.na(trim_df1)) < dim(trim_df1)[1])]
          columns_with_allNAs1 <- colnames(trim_df1)[which(colSums(is.na(trim_df1)) == dim(trim_df1)[1])]
          
          
          trim_df2 <- full_df[which(full_df$Group_f == groups_to_compare$group2[g]),] #%>% dplyr::select(-Group_f)
          columns_with_noNAs2 <- colnames(trim_df2)[which(colSums(is.na(trim_df2)) == 0)]
          columns_with_someNAs2 <- colnames(trim_df2)[which(colSums(is.na(trim_df2)) > 0 & colSums(is.na(trim_df2)) < dim(trim_df2)[1])]
          columns_with_allNAs2 <- colnames(trim_df2)[which(colSums(is.na(trim_df2)) == dim(trim_df2)[1])]
          
          #### if there are any columns with data for both groups
          if(length(intersect(c(columns_with_noNAs1,columns_with_someNAs1),c(columns_with_noNAs2,columns_with_someNAs2))) > 1){
            
            new_curr_df <- full_df[,intersect(c(columns_with_noNAs1,columns_with_someNAs1),c(columns_with_noNAs2,columns_with_someNAs2))] %>%
              ### also remove rows will all NA data, can't calculate est
              dplyr::filter(dplyr::if_any(!Group_f, ~ !is.na(.)))
            new_Assay_mat <- data.matrix(new_curr_df[,-which(colnames(new_curr_df) == "Group_f")])
            
            ### for the case where it is a single column
            colnames(new_Assay_mat) <- colnames(new_curr_df)[-which(colnames(new_curr_df) == "Group_f")]
            
            
            
            
            curr_p_raw <- apply(new_Assay_mat, 2, function(x) stats::wilcox.test(x[Group_f %in% c(
              groups_to_compare$group1[g], groups_to_compare$group2[g])] ~ Group_f[Group_f %in% c(
                groups_to_compare$group1[g], groups_to_compare$group2[g])], data = new_curr_df)$p.value)
            curr_p_adj <- stats::p.adjust(curr_p_raw, method = 'BH') 
            # curr_est <- apply(new_Assay_mat, 2, function(x) wilcox.test(x[Group_f %in% c(
            #    groups_to_compare$group1[g], groups_to_compare$group2[g])] ~ Group_f[Group_f %in% c(
            #      groups_to_compare$group1[g], groups_to_compare$group2[g])], data = new_curr_df, conf.int = TRUE)$estimate)
            
            ###### first define function
            hl <- function(x, y = NULL) {
              if (is.null(y)) {
                walsh <- outer(x, x, "+") / 2
                stats::median(walsh[lower.tri(walsh, diag = TRUE)], na.rm = TRUE)
              } else {
                stats::median(outer(x, y, "-"), na.rm = TRUE)
              }
            }
            
            #### then generate the vector
            curr_est <- c()
            curr_x_len <- c()
            curr_y_len <- c()
            for(i in colnames(new_Assay_mat)){
              x <- new_curr_df[which(new_curr_df$Group_f == groups_to_compare$group2[g]),i]
              y <- new_curr_df[which(new_curr_df$Group_f == groups_to_compare$group1[g]),i]
              ce <- hl(x, y)
              names(ce) <- i
              curr_est <- c(curr_est,ce)
              curr_x_len <- c(curr_x_len,length(x))
              curr_y_len <- c(curr_y_len,length(y))
            }
            
            
            
            #### combine to df
            
            curr_p_df <- data.frame(curr_p_raw, curr_p_adj, curr_est,
                                    curr_x_len,curr_y_len) %>%
              tibble::rownames_to_column() 
            colnames(curr_p_df) <- c("rowname",
                                     
                                     paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__p_raw"),
                                     paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__p_adj"),
                                     paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__est"),
                                     paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__Ngroup2"),
                                     paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__Ngroup1")
            )
            
            
          }else{
            #### so that these definitely don't get carried over
            curr_p_raw <- NA
            curr_p_adj <- NA
            curr_est <- NA
            curr_x_len <- NA
            curr_y_len <- NA
            
            #### combine to df
            
            curr_p_df <- data.frame(matrix(nrow=0, ncol=6))
            colnames(curr_p_df) <- c("rowname",
                                     
                                     paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__p_raw"),
                                     paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__p_adj"),
                                     paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__est"),
                                     
                                     paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__Ngroup2"),
                                     paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__Ngroup1"))
            curr_p_df$rowname <- as.character(curr_p_df$rowname)
            
          }
          
        }
        
        
      }else{
        #### so that these definitely don't get carried over
        curr_p_raw <- NA
        curr_p_adj <- NA
        curr_est <- NA
        curr_x_len <- NA
        curr_y_len <- NA
        
        #### combine to df
        
        curr_p_df <- data.frame(matrix(nrow=0, ncol=6))
        colnames(curr_p_df) <- c("rowname",
                                 
                                 paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__p_raw"),
                                 paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__p_adj"),
                                 paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__est"),
                                 
                                 paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__Ngroup2"),
                                 paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__Ngroup1"))
        curr_p_df$rowname <- as.character(curr_p_df$rowname)
      }
      
      
      ### add these groups to compare to the p_value_df1
      p_value_df1 <- dplyr::full_join(p_value_df1, curr_p_df, by="rowname") 
      
      
      
      
      
    }
    
    
    
    
    ## format p values
    p_value_df1 <- p_value_df1 %>%
      tibble::column_to_rownames() %>%
      ## set sig figs
      dplyr::mutate_all(signif, 2) %>%
      tibble::rownames_to_column()
    
    
    
    
    ## add up/down with sig columns 
    for(curr_comp in groups_to_compare$name){
      curr_df <- p_value_df1[,c("rowname",colnames(p_value_df1)[grepl(paste0(curr_comp,"__"),colnames(p_value_df1))])] %>%
        `colnames<-`(c("rowname","p_raw","p_adj","est","Ngroup2","Ngroup1")) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(dir = factor(ifelse(p_raw < 0.05, ifelse(est > 0, "up, p < 0.05","down, p < 0.05"),
                                          ifelse(p_raw < 0.1, ifelse(est > 0, "up, p < 0.1","down, p < 0.1"),
                                                 ifelse(p_raw>0.05,"not_sig","no_test"))),
                                   c("up, p < 0.05","up, p < 0.1","not_sig","down, p < 0.1","down, p < 0.05","no_test"))) %>%
        dplyr::select(-c(p_raw,p_adj,est,Ngroup2,Ngroup1)) %>%
        `colnames<-`(c("rowname",paste0(curr_comp,"__dir")))
      
      p_value_df1 <- dplyr::left_join(p_value_df1, curr_df, by = "rowname")
      
    }
    
    
    ## format p values
    p_value_df1 <- p_value_df1 %>%
      tibble::column_to_rownames() 
    
    
    
    
    
    
    ################################################ NOW plot heatmaps ################################################
    #### collect timepoints for this curr_var_set
    
    ### sort for olink
    if(grepl("olink",curr_var_set)){
      #tps_for_thisSet <- c("Baseline","wk12_24or72h","wk13")
      tps_for_thisSet <- c("Baseline","wk12_24or72h")
    }else{
      tps_for_thisSet <- unique(strex::str_after_last(rownames(p_value_df1),"__"))
    }
    
    vars_to_use <- sort(unique(strex::str_before_last(rownames(p_value_df1),"__")))
    
    sig_assay_df <- p_value_df1 %>%
      tibble::rownames_to_column() %>%
      ### add factored timepoint
      dplyr::mutate(Time = factor(strex::str_after_last(rowname,"__"), tps_for_thisSet),
                    variable = factor(strex::str_before_last(rowname,"__"),vars_to_use)) 
    
    #### if FC or delta, remove baseline
    if(curr_ds != "amount"){
      sig_assay_df <- sig_assay_df %>%
        dplyr::filter(Time != "Baseline")
      
      
      cat(" ", paste0("TRUE ", curr_ds),"\n")
      cat("\n")
      ### also set breakscales
      row_scale_set <- "none"
      if(curr_ds == "FC"){
        mycols <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(c("blue3","white","red3"))(1000)
        range <- 100
        breakscale <- c(0,
                        seq(0.001,99.99, length.out=length(mycols)/2-1),
                        seq(100,399, length.out=length(mycols)/2),
                        400)
        
      }else{
        ### for delta
        mycols <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(c("blue3","white","red3"))(1000)
        range <- 100
        breakscale <- c(-1*range,seq(-.9*range,.9*range, length.out=length(mycols)-1),1*range)
        
      }
    }else{
      
      cat(" ", paste0("ROWSCALED"),"\n")
      cat("\n")
      row_scale_set <- "row"
      mycols <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(c("blue4","white","red4"))(1000)
      range <- 2
      breakscale <- c(-1*range,seq(-.9*range,.9*range, length.out=length(mycols)-1),1*range)
      
      
    }
    
    #### dir columns
    dir_columns <- rev(colnames(sig_assay_df)[grepl("dir",colnames(sig_assay_df))])
    
    ##### annotation for rows, first listed will be closest to the heatmap (right side of ann cols), last will be on the left edge of the plot
    annotation_row = sig_assay_df[,c(dir_columns,"Time","variable","rowname")] %>%
      ### add simpler rowname with out the annotation
      #dplyr::mutate(rowname_clean = str_before_first(rowname,"xx__")) %>%
      tibble::column_to_rownames() 
    
    
    
    ###### annotation for columns
    annotation_col <- full_df %>%
      dplyr::select(Group_f) %>%
      ## arrange
      dplyr::arrange(Group_f)
    
    
    ##### for baseline also sort by dir
    
    if(grepl("base",fig_name_to_use)){
      #### set orders to use
      hm_orders_to_use <- list(
        "by Assay, timepoint, dir"=c("variable","Time",dir_columns),
        "by timepoint, dir, Assay"=c("Time",dir_columns,"variable")
      )
      
      
    }else{
      #### set orders to use
      hm_orders_to_use <- list(
        "by Assay, timepoint, dir"=c("variable","Time",dir_columns)
      )
      
    }
    
    ####### set annotation colors 
    ### first for time
    timepoints_df <- data.frame("tp"=c("Baseline","wk12_24or72h","wk13","wk13_14","wk14","wk14_15","wk17","Post"),
                                "color"=c("grey95",
                                          "lemonchiffon",
                                          "lemonchiffon3",
                                          "bisque1",
                                          "bisque2",
                                          "bisque2",
                                          "bisque3",
                                          "bisque4")) %>%
      tibble::column_to_rownames("tp")
    
    
    
    time_for_anncolors <- timepoints_df[tps_for_thisSet,]
    names(time_for_anncolors) <- tps_for_thisSet
    
    
    ####
    
    
    annotation_colors=list()
    annotation_colors[["Group_f"]] <- group_colors_to_use
    
    annotation_colors[["Time"]] <- time_for_anncolors
    for(curr_dir in dir_columns){
      annotation_colors[[paste0(curr_dir)]] <- c("up, p < 0.05"="red2","up, p < 0.1"="lightpink",not_sig="black",
                                                 "down, p < 0.1"="skyblue","down, p < 0.05"="blue2",no_test="white")
    }
    
    
    # hmo <- names(hm_orders_to_use)[1]
    
    
    for(hmo in names(hm_orders_to_use)){
      
      if(grepl("base",fig_name_to_use)){
        cat("##### ", paste0(hmo," {.tabset}"),"\n")
        cat("\n")
      }else{
        cat("##### ", paste0("heatmaps {.tabset}"),"\n")
        cat("\n")

      hc
      
      
      
      cat("\n")
      cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!

    cat("\n")

          )+
```
