```{r studiesUsedTable__PCA___Fig8olink, ref.label=c('studiesUsedTable')}
```




#### Supp Fig 10A: Compare groups {.tabset}



```{r PCA_compareGroups, results='asis', fig.height=4, fig.width=5}


#### for each timepoint of interest
for(curr_time in Time_Point_order){
  
  cat("##### ",paste0(curr_time," {.tabset}"),"\n")
  cat('\n')
  
  for(pca_scale_to_use in c(TRUE,FALSE)){
    
    cat("###### ",paste0("scale = ", pca_scale_to_use," {.tabset}"),"\n")
    cat('\n')
    
    
    ######## for olink, use log10
    
    if(grepl("olink", curr_var_set)){
      
      ## make true long format
      curr_phen_long1 <- curr_phen_long %>%
        ### trim to timepoint
        dplyr::filter(Time_Point == curr_time) %>%
        ### also add useful group
        dplyr::mutate(value = log10(amount)) %>%
        ### rename Group to generic
        dplyr::rename(group=!!rlang::sym(group_var_to_use)) %>%
        dplyr::arrange(group)
      
    }else{
      ## make true long format
      curr_phen_long1 <- curr_phen_long %>%
        ### trim to timepoint
        dplyr::filter(Time_Point == curr_time) %>%
        ### also add useful group
        dplyr::mutate(value = amount) %>%
        ### rename Group to generic
        dplyr::rename(group=!!rlang::sym(group_var_to_use)) %>%
        dplyr::arrange(group)
      
      
    }
    
    
    
    list_of_plotted[[paste0(fig_name_to_use,"_PCA_",curr_time)]] <- curr_phen_long1[,c("Sample_ID","group","variable","amount","value")]
    
    
    ### generate dataframe for PCA, columns are assays, rows are samples
    curr_cm_prep <- curr_phen_long1 %>%
      ### trim to only the olink columns and the animal
      dplyr::select(c(Sample_ID,group,variable,value)) %>%
      ### combine animal and group
      dplyr::mutate(group_animal = paste0(group,"_",Sample_ID),
                    #group = NULL,
                    Sample_ID = NULL) %>%
      ### make wider
      tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "variable", values_from = "value") 
    
    
    curr_cm <- curr_cm_prep %>%
      ### remove columns with all NAs for at least one group
      dplyr::select(group, curr_cm_prep %>%
                      group_by(group) %>%
                      dplyr::summarise(across(everything(), ~!all(is.na(.x)))) %>%
                      ungroup() %>%
                      dplyr::select(-group) %>%
                      dplyr::select(where(all)) %>%
                      names()) %>%
      ###remove group
      dplyr::select(-group) %>%
      ### make group_animal rownames
      column_to_rownames("group_animal") %>%
      ### also remove columns (assays) with any NA since prcomp can't handle it and would rather lose an assay than a sample
      dplyr::select(where(function(x) !any(is.na(x))))
    
    
    
    #### factorize curr_meta
    curr_meta <- curr_phen_long1 %>%
      ### select only the metadata -- now also pulling Sex
      dplyr::select(c(Sample_ID,group,Group_simp,Sex)) %>%
      ### extract ALFQA
      dplyr::mutate(ALFQA = str_after_last(Group_simp,"_"),
                    Group_simp = NULL,
                    Sex = factor(Sex, c("Male","Female")),
                    ### combined adjuvant x sex factor for shape
                    AdjSex = factor(paste0(as.character(ALFQA),"_",as.character(Sex)),
                                    names(adjSex_shape_vec))) %>%
      ### make unique
      unique() %>%
      ### combine animal and group
      dplyr::mutate(group_animal = paste0(group,"_",Sample_ID)) %>%
      ### make group_animal rownames
      column_to_rownames("group_animal") %>%
      dplyr::mutate(group_f = factor(group, group_order),
                    ### baseline-status is uniform for the whole panel (curr_time is fixed per loop iteration)
                    is_baseline = (curr_time == "Baseline"),
                    pt_fill = get_point_fill(group_f, is_baseline, group_colors_to_use),
                    pt_border = get_point_border(group_f, is_baseline, group_colors_to_use))


    
    #### print thenumber of animals
    
    cat('\n')
    cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key! 
    
    
    to_print <-  as.data.frame(table(curr_meta$group)) %>%
      dplyr::rename(Group=Var1,Num_animals=Freq) %>%
      DT::datatable(extensions = 'Buttons',
                    options = list(dom = 'Blfrtip',
                                   buttons = c('copy', 'csv', 'excel', 'pdf', 'print'),
                                   iDisplayLength = 25,
                                   lengthMenu = list(c(10,25,50,-1),
                                                     c(10,25,50,"All"))))
    
    #) , height = "100%", width = "100%")
    print(htmltools::tagList(to_print))
    
    
    
    cat('\n')
    cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key! 
    
    
    ### generate PCA
    pca <- prcomp(curr_cm, scale. = pca_scale_to_use)
    
    ### calculate % for each PC
    pc_pct_list <- list()
    for(i in 1:10){
      pc_pct_list[[paste0("PC",i)]] <- round(pca$sdev[i]^2/sum(pca$sdev^2)*100,2)
    }
    m.pc1 = round(pca$sdev[1]^2/sum(pca$sdev^2)*100,2)
    m.pc2 = round(pca$sdev[2]^2/sum(pca$sdev^2)*100,2)
    m.pc3 = round(pca$sdev[3]^2/sum(pca$sdev^2)*100,2)
    m.pc4 = round(pca$sdev[4]^2/sum(pca$sdev^2)*100,2)
    
    
    ####### only need PC1 vs PC2 as others are not useful
    pcs_pairs <- list(c("PC1","PC2"))
    pca_pairs_list <- list(c(1:2))
    # pcs_pairs <- list(c("PC1","PC2"),c("PC3","PC4"),c("PC5","PC6"),c("PC7","PC8"))
    # pca_pairs_list <- list(c(1:2),c(3:4),c(5:6),c(7:8))
    
    for(pca_pair in 1:length(pcs_pairs)){
      pcs_to_plot <- pcs_pairs[[pca_pair]]
      pca_pairs <- pca_pairs_list[[pca_pair]]
      
      xlab=paste0(pcs_to_plot[1]," (",pc_pct_list[[paste0(pcs_to_plot[1])]]," %)")
      ylab=paste0(pcs_to_plot[2]," (",pc_pct_list[[paste0(pcs_to_plot[2])]]," %)")
      
      # cat("##### ",paste0(pcs_to_plot[1], " vs ", pcs_to_plot[2]),"\n")
      # cat('\n')
      # 
      ### trim to number of loadings you want    
      pca_trim <- pca
      scores <- data.frame(pca_trim$x[, pca_pairs])
      scores[] <- lapply(scores, function(x) x / sqrt(sum((x - mean(x))^2))) 
      loadings <- as.data.frame(pca_trim$rotation)[pca_pairs]
      
      scale <- min(
        max(abs(scores[,pcs_to_plot[1]]))/max(abs(loadings[,pcs_to_plot[1]])),
        max(abs(scores[,pcs_to_plot[2]]))/max(abs(loadings[,pcs_to_plot[2]]))
      )*0.8
      
      ## add labels and positions to loadings_df
      loadings_df <- data.frame(loadings * scale) %>%
        rownames_to_column("var") 
      
      ##trim    
      top_rots <- c()
      for(curr_pc in pcs_to_plot){
        pca_trim_rot <- loadings_df
        ### add sort column
        pca_trim_rot$PC_to_sort <- abs(pca_trim_rot[,curr_pc])
        ### collect top (pos or neg)
        pca_trim_rot <- pca_trim_rot %>%
          arrange(desc(PC_to_sort)) 
        top_rots <- c(top_rots, pca_trim_rot$var[1:num_loadings_per_PC])
      }
      
      ### now trim to only the top loadings
      top_unique <- unique(top_rots)
      loadings_df2 <- loadings_df[loadings_df$var %in% top_unique,]
      
      
      
      ### plot for all paramters:
      
      #### base plot
    ### ellipse fill: pale group colors if this panel is Baseline, full group colors otherwise
      ellipse_fill_vec <- if(curr_time == "Baseline") baseline_pale_color_vec else group_colors_to_use

      p <- ggplot(scores, aes(x = !!rlang::sym(pcs_to_plot[1]), y = !!rlang::sym(pcs_to_plot[2]))) + 
        stat_ellipse(aes(fill = curr_meta$group_f), geom = "polygon", level = as.numeric(ellipse_prob), inherit.aes = TRUE, alpha = 0.4) +
        scale_fill_manual(name="Group",values=ellipse_fill_vec) +
        ### points: fill/border fixed per-row (baseline vs non-baseline), shape = AdjSex
        ggnewscale::new_scale_fill()+
        geom_point(aes(shape = curr_meta$AdjSex), 
                   fill = curr_meta$pt_fill,
                   color = curr_meta$pt_border,
                   size = 3, stroke = 0.9)+
        scale_shape_manual(name="Adjuvant/Sex",values=adjSex_shape_vec) + 
        xlab(xlab)+ylab(ylab)+
        guides(fill=guide_legend(override.aes=list(shape=21))) + ### keep ellipse/Group fill legend fillable
        
        
        ### add loadings on top for final plot
        geom_segment(data = loadings_df2,
                     aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = !!rlang::sym(pcs_to_plot[1]), yend = !!rlang::sym(pcs_to_plot[2])), 
                     color = "grey40", arrow = arrow(angle = 25, length = unit(4, "mm")))+
        geom_text_repel(data = loadings_df2, aes(x = !!rlang::sym(pcs_to_plot[1]), y = !!rlang::sym(pcs_to_plot[2]), label = var), size=3.5, color="grey25",
                        min.segment.length = 0, segment.color = 'grey60') +
        #coord_fixed() +
        theme_bw()+  
        theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank() ,
              panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
      
      plot(p)
      
      
      cat('\n')
      cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key! 
      
      ##### also print loadings dff
      
      to_print <- loadings_df %>% 
        dplyr::arrange(desc(PC1)) %>%
        DT::datatable(extensions = 'Buttons',
                      options = list(dom = 'Blfrtip',
                                     buttons = c('copy', 'csv', 'excel', 'pdf', 'print'),
                                     iDisplayLength = 25,
                                     lengthMenu = list(c(10,25,50,-1),
                                                       c(10,25,50,"All"))))
      
      #) , height = "100%", width = "100%")
      print(htmltools::tagList(to_print))
      
      
      
    }
    
    cat('\n')
    cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key! 
    
  }
  
  cat('\n')
  cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key! 
  
  
  
}

cat('\n')
cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!
```

```{r PCA_compareTime, results='asis', fig.height=4, fig.width=5}
#### for each group of interest
for(curr_group in c("DNA","ALVAC")){
  
  cat("##### ",paste0(curr_group," {.tabset}"),"\n")
  cat('\n')
  
  for(pca_scale_to_use in c(TRUE,FALSE)){
    
    cat("###### ",paste0("scale = ", pca_scale_to_use," {.tabset}"),"\n")
    cat('\n')
    
    
    
    ######## for olink, use log10
    
    if(grepl("olink", curr_var_set)){
      
      
      ## make true long format
      curr_phen_long1 <- curr_phen_long %>%
        ### trim to group
        dplyr::filter(!!rlang::sym(group_var_to_use) == curr_group) %>%
        ### also log10
        dplyr::mutate(value = log10(amount)) 
      
    }else{
      
      ## make true long format
      curr_phen_long1 <- curr_phen_long %>%
        ### trim to group
        dplyr::filter(!!rlang::sym(group_var_to_use) == curr_group) %>%
        ### don't log10
        dplyr::mutate(value = (amount)) 
      
    }
    
    
    list_of_plotted[[paste0(fig_name_to_use,"_PCA_",curr_group)]] <- curr_phen_long1[,c("Sample_ID","Time_Point","variable","amount","value")]
    
    
    ### generate dataframe for PCA, columns are assays, rows are samples
    curr_cm_prep <- curr_phen_long1 %>%
      ### trim to only the olink columns and the animal
      dplyr::select(c(Sample_ID,Time_Point,variable,value)) %>%
      ### combine animal and Time_Point
      dplyr::mutate(time_animal = paste0(Time_Point,"_",Sample_ID),
                    Sample_ID = NULL) %>%
      ### make wider
      tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "variable", values_from = "value") 
    
    
    curr_cm <- curr_cm_prep %>%
      ### remove columns with all NAs for at least one Time_Point
      dplyr::select(Time_Point, curr_cm_prep %>%
                      group_by(Time_Point) %>%
                      dplyr::summarise(across(everything(), ~!all(is.na(.x)))) %>%
                      ungroup() %>%
                      dplyr::select(-Time_Point) %>%
                      dplyr::select(where(all)) %>%
                      names()) %>%
      ###remove Time_Point
      dplyr::select(-Time_Point) %>%
      ### make time_animal rownames
      column_to_rownames("time_animal") %>%
      ### also remove columns (assays) with any NA since prcomp can't handle it and would rather lose an assay than a sample
      dplyr::select(where(function(x) !any(is.na(x))))
    
    
    
    #### factorize curr_meta
    curr_meta <- curr_phen_long1 %>%
      ### select only the metadata -- now also pulling Sex
      dplyr::select(c(Sample_ID,Time_Point,Group_simp,Sex)) %>%
      ### extract ALFQA
      dplyr::mutate(ALFQA = str_after_last(Group_simp,"_"),
                    Group_simp = NULL,
                    Sex = factor(Sex, c("Male","Female")),
                    ### combined adjuvant x sex factor for shape
                    AdjSex = factor(paste0(as.character(ALFQA),"_",as.character(Sex)),
                                    names(adjSex_shape_vec))) %>%
      ### make unique
      unique() %>%
      ### combine animal and Time_Point
      dplyr::mutate(time_animal = paste0(Time_Point,"_",Sample_ID)) %>%
      ### make time_animal rownames
      column_to_rownames("time_animal") %>%
      dplyr::mutate(Time_Point_f = factor(Time_Point, Time_Point_order),
                    ### baseline-status varies per row (Baseline vs non-baseline within the same panel);
                    ### curr_group (from the outer for-loop) supplies the fixed Group color for this panel
                    is_baseline = (as.character(Time_Point) == "Baseline"),
                    pt_fill = get_point_fill(curr_group, is_baseline, group_colors_to_use),
                    pt_border = get_point_border(curr_group, is_baseline, group_colors_to_use))
    
    
    #### print thenumber of animals
    
    cat('\n')
    cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key! 
    
    
    to_print <-  as.data.frame(table(curr_meta$Time_Point)) %>%
      dplyr::rename(Time_Point=Var1,Num_animals=Freq) %>%
      DT::datatable(extensions = 'Buttons',
                    options = list(dom = 'Blfrtip',
                                   buttons = c('copy', 'csv', 'excel', 'pdf', 'print'),
                                   iDisplayLength = 25,
                                   lengthMenu = list(c(10,25,50,-1),
                                                     c(10,25,50,"All"))))
    
    #) , height = "100%", width = "100%")
    print(htmltools::tagList(to_print))
    
    
    
    cat('\n')
    cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key! 
    
    
    ### generate PCA
    pca <- prcomp(curr_cm, scale. = pca_scale_to_use)
    
    ### calculate % for each PC
    pc_pct_list <- list()
    for(i in 1:10){
      pc_pct_list[[paste0("PC",i)]] <- round(pca$sdev[i]^2/sum(pca$sdev^2)*100,2)
    }
    m.pc1 = round(pca$sdev[1]^2/sum(pca$sdev^2)*100,2)
    m.pc2 = round(pca$sdev[2]^2/sum(pca$sdev^2)*100,2)
    m.pc3 = round(pca$sdev[3]^2/sum(pca$sdev^2)*100,2)
    m.pc4 = round(pca$sdev[4]^2/sum(pca$sdev^2)*100,2)
    
    
    ####### only need PC1 vs PC2 as others are not useful
    pcs_pairs <- list(c("PC1","PC2"))
    pca_pairs_list <- list(c(1:2))
    # pcs_pairs <- list(c("PC1","PC2"),c("PC3","PC4"),c("PC5","PC6"),c("PC7","PC8"))
    # pca_pairs_list <- list(c(1:2),c(3:4),c(5:6),c(7:8))
    
    for(pca_pair in 1:length(pcs_pairs)){
      pcs_to_plot <- pcs_pairs[[pca_pair]]
      pca_pairs <- pca_pairs_list[[pca_pair]]
      
      xlab=paste0(pcs_to_plot[1]," (",pc_pct_list[[paste0(pcs_to_plot[1])]]," %)")
      ylab=paste0(pcs_to_plot[2]," (",pc_pct_list[[paste0(pcs_to_plot[2])]]," %)")
      
      # cat("##### ",paste0(pcs_to_plot[1], " vs ", pcs_to_plot[2]),"\n")
      # cat('\n')
      # 
      ### trim to number of loadings you want    
      pca_trim <- pca
      scores <- data.frame(pca_trim$x[, pca_pairs])
      scores[] <- lapply(scores, function(x) x / sqrt(sum((x - mean(x))^2))) 
      loadings <- as.data.frame(pca_trim$rotation)[pca_pairs]
      
      scale <- min(
        max(abs(scores[,pcs_to_plot[1]]))/max(abs(loadings[,pcs_to_plot[1]])),
        max(abs(scores[,pcs_to_plot[2]]))/max(abs(loadings[,pcs_to_plot[2]]))
      )*0.8
      
      ## add labels and positions to loadings_df
      loadings_df <- data.frame(loadings * scale) %>%
        rownames_to_column("var") 
      
      ##trim    
      top_rots <- c()
      for(curr_pc in pcs_to_plot){
        pca_trim_rot <- loadings_df
        ### add sort column
        pca_trim_rot$PC_to_sort <- abs(pca_trim_rot[,curr_pc])
        ### collect top (pos or neg)
        pca_trim_rot <- pca_trim_rot %>%
          arrange(desc(PC_to_sort)) 
        top_rots <- c(top_rots, pca_trim_rot$var[1:num_loadings_per_PC])
      }
      
      ### now trim to only the top loadings
      top_unique <- unique(top_rots)
      loadings_df2 <- loadings_df[loadings_df$var %in% top_unique,]
      
      
      
      ### plot for all paramters:
      
      #### base plot
 ### ellipse fill: for each timepoint level in this panel, pale group color
      ### if that level is "Baseline", full group color otherwise -- keyed to
      ### this panel's fixed Group (curr_group, from the outer for-loop)
      ellipse_fill_vec_time <- sapply(levels(curr_meta$Time_Point_f), function(tp){
        if(tp == "Baseline") unname(baseline_pale_color_vec[curr_group]) else unname(group_colors_to_use[curr_group])
      })
      names(ellipse_fill_vec_time) <- levels(curr_meta$Time_Point_f)

      p <- ggplot(scores, aes(x = !!rlang::sym(pcs_to_plot[1]), y = !!rlang::sym(pcs_to_plot[2]))) + 
        stat_ellipse(aes(fill = curr_meta$Time_Point_f), geom = "polygon", level = as.numeric(ellipse_prob), inherit.aes = TRUE, alpha = 0.4) +
        scale_fill_manual(name="Timepoint",values=ellipse_fill_vec_time) +
        ### points: fill/border fixed per-row (baseline vs non-baseline, following the shared Group-based scheme), shape = AdjSex
        ggnewscale::new_scale_fill()+
        geom_point(aes(shape = curr_meta$AdjSex), 
                   fill = curr_meta$pt_fill,
                   color = curr_meta$pt_border,
                   size = 3, stroke = 0.9)+
        scale_shape_manual(name="Adjuvant/Sex",values=adjSex_shape_vec) +  
        xlab(xlab)+ylab(ylab)+
        guides(fill=guide_legend(override.aes=list(shape=21))) + ### keep ellipse/Timepoint fill legend fillable

        
        
        ### add loadings on top for final plot
        geom_segment(data = loadings_df2,
                     aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = !!rlang::sym(pcs_to_plot[1]), yend = !!rlang::sym(pcs_to_plot[2])), 
                     color = "grey40", arrow = arrow(angle = 25, length = unit(4, "mm")))+
        geom_text_repel(data = loadings_df2, aes(x = !!rlang::sym(pcs_to_plot[1]), y = !!rlang::sym(pcs_to_plot[2]), label = var), size=3.5, color="grey25",
                        min.segment.length = 0, segment.color = 'grey60') +
        #coord_fixed() +
        theme_bw()+  
        theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank() ,
              panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
      
      plot(p)
      
      
      cat('\n')
      cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key! 
      
      ##### also print loadings dff
      
      to_print <- loadings_df %>% 
        dplyr::arrange(desc(PC1)) %>%
        DT::datatable(extensions = 'Buttons',
                      options = list(dom = 'Blfrtip',
                                     buttons = c('copy', 'csv', 'excel', 'pdf', 'print'),
                                     iDisplayLength = 25,
                                     lengthMenu = list(c(10,25,50,-1),
                                                       c(10,25,50,"All"))))
      
      #) , height = "100%", width = "100%")
      print(htmltools::tagList(to_print))
      
      
      
    }
    
    cat('\n')
    cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key! 
    
  }
  
  cat('\n')
  cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key! 
  
  
  
}
```

```{r baselineVolcanos, fig.height=6, fig.width=9}
df_for_vp <- sig_assay_df %>%
  ### make longer
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!c(rowname, Time, variable), names_to = "stat", values_to = "value", values_transform = as.character) %>%
  ### make names generic
  dplyr::mutate(stat = str_after_first(stat, "__")) %>%
  ### return to wide
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "stat", values_from = "value") %>%
  ## make numeric
  dplyr::mutate_at(vars(c(p_raw,p_adj,est,Ngroup2,Ngroup1)), as.numeric) %>%
  ## remove rows without stats (only had one group)
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(p_raw)) %>%
  ### refactorize dir
  dplyr::mutate(dir = ifelse(grepl("p < 0.1",dir),"not_sig",dir),
                dir = factor(dir,  c("up, p < 0.05","not_sig","down, p < 0.05")),
                ## cap est at 5
                est_cap = ifelse(est > est_cap_value_plot, 
                                 est_cap_value_plot, 
                                 ifelse(est < -est_cap_value_plot, 
                                        -est_cap_value_plot,
                                        est)),
                ### add label only for sig
                label_print = ifelse(p_raw < label_p_min, str_before_last(as.character(variable),"__"), ""))

 color_df <- data.frame("category"=c("up, p < 0.05","not_sig","down, p < 0.05"),
                             "colors"=c( unname(group_colors_to_use[2]),

                                         unname(group_colors_to_use[1])))
  
      colors_to_use <- color_df$colors[which(color_df$category %in% unique(df_for_vp$dir))]

    p <- ggplot(df_for_vp,
                  aes(est_cap,-log10(p_raw),color=dir, fill=dir, label=label_print)) +
        geom_point(shape = 21, alpha = 0.65) + 
        theme_bw()  +
        geom_vline(xintercept = 0,linetype="dashed",color = "grey60") +
        geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05),linetype="dashed",color = "grey60") +

        geom_text_repel(max.overlaps = 20, size = labSize, 
                        point.padding = 3,
                        show.legend = FALSE) + #this removes the 'a' from the legend
        #scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-5,5), breaks = seq(-5,5,1))+
        scale_color_manual(values=colors_to_use)+
        scale_fill_manual(values=colors_to_use)+
        scale_size_continuous(range = c(0,3))+
        ggtitle(paste0(length(which(df_for_vp$dir == "up, p < 0.05"))," up, ",
                       length(which(df_for_vp$dir == "down, p < 0.05"))," down"))+
        theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
              axis.text = element_text(size = 13)) +
        guides(color=guide_legend(override.aes = list(size=4), title = groups_to_compare$name),fill=guide_legend(title = groups_to_compare$name))#+
       # scale_size(guide = 'none') ### remove the size from legend
```

test effect of Sex, Adjuvant, Weight, Age on other analyte outcomes



```{r OtherAnalytes, results='asis'}


## ============================================================
## Programmatically determine, for each analyte category, which
## Platform-interaction terms (Sex, Adjuvant, Weight, Age) are
## testable, based on actual data availability per study.
##
## Uses: phen_long (variable, studyLetterForMS, Group, Sample_ID,
## amount), raw_df_TOA (Sample_ID, Group_ignoreALFQA, Sex,
## studyLetterForMS), list_of_vars (named list of variable vectors
## per analyte category)
## ============================================================

## --------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Study-level reference table: Platform / Sex / Adjuvant per study
## (derived from raw_df_TOA, not hardcoded)
## --------------------------------------------------------

cat("#### ", "Studies have", "\n")
cat("\n")

study_reference <- raw_df_TOA %>%
  dplyr::filter(studyLetterForMS != "studyF" | TRUE) %>%  ## keep studyF here; drop later per-analyte if needed
  dplyr::mutate(
    Adjuvant = str_before_first(str_after_first(Group, "_"), "_"),
    Adjuvant = ifelse(Adjuvant == "", str_after_first(Group, "_"), Adjuvant),
    Adjuvant = ifelse(grepl("Naive", Group), NA_character_, Adjuvant)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!grepl("Naive", Group)) %>%
  dplyr::select(studyLetterForMS, Group_ignoreALFQA, Sex, Adjuvant) %>%
  unique() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Study = studyLetterForMS, Platform = Group_ignoreALFQA) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(Platform), Study)

study_reference %>%
  DT::datatable(
    extensions = 'Buttons',
    options = list(dom = 'Blfrtip',
                   buttons = c('copy', 'csv', 'excel', 'pdf', 'print'),
                   iDisplayLength = 25,
                   lengthMenu = list(c(10, 25, 50, -1), c(10, 25, 50, "All")))
  ) %>%
  htmltools::tagList() %>%
  print()

cat("\n")
cat(' \n \n')



## --------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Analyte category -> which studies actually have non-NA data
## Define analyte categories exactly as used in list_of_vars, keyed
## to the same names used throughout the Rmd (curr_var_set values)
## --------------------------------------------------------
analyte_categories <- list(
  # "Avidity/Ab/ADCC/Eff (Panel A)" = c(list_of_vars[["ADCC_columns"]],
  #                                      list_of_vars[["eff_columns"]],
  #                                      list_of_vars[["Abs_columns"]]),
  "RM cell responses (Panel B)"   = c(list_of_vars[["arifnew_NK"]],
                                       list_of_vars[["arifnew_mono"]],
                                       list_of_vars[["arifnew_DC"]]),
  "Systemic cell responses (Panel C)" = c(list_of_vars[["massinew_mono"]],
                                           list_of_vars[["massinew_tcells"]]),
  "Cytokines/Chemokines (Panel D)"    = list_of_vars[["olink_columns"]],

  ## finer-grained subcategories, in case you want per-block detail
  "Avidity score only"      = list_of_vars[["Abs_columns"]][grepl("Avi", list_of_vars[["Abs_columns"]])],
  "ADCC/Ab/V2pep only"            = c(list_of_vars[["Abs_columns"]][!grepl("Avi", list_of_vars[["Abs_columns"]])],
                                 list_of_vars[["ADCC_columns"]]),
  "Efferocytosis only"      = list_of_vars[["eff_columns"]]
)

## which studies have at least one non-NA observation for each category
studies_with_data <- purrr::imap_dfr(analyte_categories, function(vars_vec, cat_name) {
  studies <- phen_long %>%
    dplyr::filter(variable %in% vars_vec, !is.na(amount)) %>%
    dplyr::pull(studyLetterForMS) %>%
    unique() %>%
    as.character()

  ## guard against categories with zero matching studies (e.g. an
  ## empty vars_vec, or all-NA data) -- data.frame() can't recycle
  ## a length-1 category name against a length-0 Study vector
  if (length(studies) == 0) {
    return(data.frame(category = character(0), Study = character(0)))
  }

  data.frame(category = cat_name, Study = studies)
})

## --------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Join to study_reference to get Platform/Sex/Adjuvant per
## category, then build the testability table
## --------------------------------------------------------


cat("#### ", "Studies have for each assay category", "\n")
cat("\n")
category_design <- studies_with_data %>%
  dplyr::left_join(study_reference, by = "Study") %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Platform))  ## drop naive-only or unmatched rows

category_design %>%
  dplyr::arrange(category, Platform, Study) %>%
  DT::datatable(
    extensions = 'Buttons',
    options = list(dom = 'Blfrtip',
                   buttons = c('copy', 'csv', 'excel', 'pdf', 'print'),
                   iDisplayLength = 309,
                   lengthMenu = list(c(10, 25, 50, -1), c(10, 25, 50, "All")))
  ) %>%
  htmltools::tagList() %>%
  print()

cat("\n")
cat(' \n \n')

## --------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Helper: given a category's design df (Study, Platform, Sex,
## Adjuvant -- one row per study), determine testability of each term.
##
## NOTE: Sex, Adjuvant, and Platform are constant within a study (by
## design), so any confounding among them is fully visible from this
## study-level table -- no animal-level data is needed.
## --------------------------------------------------------
assess_testability <- function(design_df) {

  ## cross-tab of Platform x Sex, and Platform x Adjuvant
  plat_sex_tab   <- table(design_df$Platform, design_df$Sex)
  plat_adj_tab   <- table(design_df$Platform, design_df$Adjuvant)

  n_platforms <- length(unique(design_df$Platform))

  ## Platform testable if >=2 platforms present
  platform_ok <- n_platforms >= 2

  ## which studies contribute to each platform, for reporting
  DNA_studies <- design_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(Platform == "DNA") %>%
    dplyr::pull(Study) %>%
    unique() %>%
    sort() %>%
    paste(collapse = ", ")
  if (DNA_studies == "") DNA_studies <- "none"

  ALVAC_studies <- design_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(Platform == "ALVAC") %>%
    dplyr::pull(Study) %>%
    unique() %>%
    sort() %>%
    paste(collapse = ", ")
  if (ALVAC_studies == "") ALVAC_studies <- "none"

  ## Platform x Sex testable if the 2x2 (or more) table has no
  ## structural zero in any Platform x Sex cell (i.e. all combos
  ## of observed Platforms and observed Sexes are populated)
  sex_levels  <- unique(design_df$Sex)
  plat_levels <- unique(design_df$Platform)
  full_grid_sex <- expand.grid(Platform = plat_levels, Sex = sex_levels)
  sex_cells_filled <- full_grid_sex %>%
    dplyr::rowwise() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(filled = plat_sex_tab[as.character(Platform), as.character(Sex)] > 0) %>%
    dplyr::pull(filled)
  platform_x_sex_ok <- platform_ok && length(sex_levels) >= 2 && all(sex_cells_filled)

  ## check if Platform and Sex are fully confounded (aliased): each
  ## Platform level maps to exactly one Sex level, and vice versa
  plat_sex_map <- design_df %>% dplyr::select(Platform, Sex) %>% unique()
  platform_sex_confounded <- nrow(plat_sex_map) == n_platforms &&
    length(unique(plat_sex_map$Sex)) == n_platforms

  ## Platform x Adjuvant, same logic (drop NA adjuvants)
  design_adj <- design_df %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(Adjuvant))
  adj_levels <- unique(design_adj$Adjuvant)
  full_grid_adj <- expand.grid(Platform = plat_levels, Adjuvant = adj_levels)
  adj_cells_filled <- if (nrow(design_adj) == 0) {
    logical(0)
  } else {
    full_grid_adj %>%
      dplyr::rowwise() %>%
      dplyr::mutate(filled = plat_adj_tab[as.character(Platform), as.character(Adjuvant)] > 0) %>%
      dplyr::pull(filled)
  }
  platform_x_adjuvant_ok <- platform_ok && length(adj_levels) >= 2 && length(adj_cells_filled) > 0 && all(adj_cells_filled)

  ## --------------------------------------------------------
  ## Platform x Adjuvant confounding (mirrors platform_sex_confounded):
  ## TRUE if every Platform maps to exactly one Adjuvant, and vice
  ## versa -- i.e. Platform and Adjuvant are fully aliased for this
  ## category's studies. Distinct from platform_x_adjuvant_ok above,
  ## which only checks marginal cell coverage (no empty cells) and
  ## would NOT catch e.g. "DNA is always Alum, ALVAC is always ALFQA."
  ## --------------------------------------------------------
  plat_adj_map <- design_adj %>% dplyr::select(Platform, Adjuvant) %>% unique()
  platform_adjuvant_confounded <- nrow(plat_adj_map) > 0 &&
    nrow(plat_adj_map) == n_platforms &&
    length(unique(plat_adj_map$Adjuvant)) == n_platforms

  ## --------------------------------------------------------
  ## Sex x Adjuvant confounding WITHIN Platform. This is what actually
  ## breaks a joint Platform*Sex + Platform*Adjuvant model -- distinct
  ## from platform_sex_confounded (Platform vs Sex only) and from
  ## platform_x_adjuvant_ok (marginal cell coverage only, ignores Sex
  ## entirely). Since Sex/Adjuvant/Platform are constant per study,
  ## this is just: within each Platform x Adjuvant combination that
  ## appears in design_adj, how many distinct Sexes show up?
  ## --------------------------------------------------------
  if (nrow(design_adj) > 0 && length(adj_levels) >= 2 && length(sex_levels) >= 2) {

    plat_adj_sex_map <- design_adj %>%
      dplyr::distinct(Platform, Adjuvant, Sex) %>%
      dplyr::count(Platform, Adjuvant, name = "n_sexes_in_cell")

    ## confounded if NO Platform x Adjuvant cell has more than one Sex
    sex_adjuvant_confounded <- all(plat_adj_sex_map$n_sexes_in_cell <= 1)

    ## human-readable detail: which Sex(es) go with each Platform/Adjuvant
    detail_rows <- design_adj %>%
      dplyr::distinct(Platform, Adjuvant, Sex) %>%
      dplyr::group_by(Platform, Adjuvant) %>%
      dplyr::summarise(sexes = paste(sort(as.character(Sex)), collapse = ","), .groups = "drop") %>%
      dplyr::mutate(label = paste0(Platform, "/", Adjuvant, ": ", sexes))

    sex_adjuvant_detail <- paste(detail_rows$label, collapse = "; ")

    joint_sex_adjuvant_testable <- !sex_adjuvant_confounded

  } else {
    sex_adjuvant_confounded <- FALSE
    sex_adjuvant_detail <- "insufficient Sex/Adjuvant variation to assess"
    joint_sex_adjuvant_testable <- FALSE
  }

  ## --------------------------------------------------------
  ## Minimum number of distinct studies per Platform x Sex x Adjuvant
  ## cell actually used. This generalizes all the pairwise confounding
  ## checks above into one number: a cell built from only 1 study means
  ## that cell's "effect" is inseparable from study-specific quirks
  ## (housing, challenge stock, timing, cage effects, etc.), regardless
  ## of which specific interaction term you're trying to fit. Any
  ## pairwise confounding flagged above will necessarily also show up
  ## here as a low count, but this also catches cases the pairwise
  ## checks miss (e.g. a cell defined by a single study even when no
  ## two factors are fully aliased against each other).
  ## --------------------------------------------------------
  cell_study_counts <- design_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(Adjuvant)) %>%
    dplyr::count(Platform, Sex, Adjuvant, name = "n_studies_in_cell")

  min_studies_per_cell <- if (nrow(cell_study_counts) > 0) {
    min(cell_study_counts$n_studies_in_cell)
  } else {
    NA_integer_
  }

  ## Sex main effect only within a single platform is separately
  ## checkable; report whether >=2 platforms x >=2 sexes exist at all,
  ## and whether sex varies at all
  sex_main_effect_ok <- length(sex_levels) >= 2

  ## Weight/Age are continuous and don't depend on categorical
  ## crossing -- testable as long as Platform is testable at all.
  ## (NOTE: this does NOT check whether Weight/Age actually vary
  ## independently of Platform/Sex/Adjuvant for this category's
  ## animals -- see conversation notes: that would require per-animal
  ## continuous data, not just this study-level design_df, and is a
  ## separate, harder-to-flag failure mode -- near-collinearity rather
  ## than exact aliasing -- worth a follow-up check if it becomes a
  ## practical problem.)
  weight_age_ok <- platform_ok

  data.frame(
    n_studies                = length(unique(design_df$Study)),
    DNA_studies              = DNA_studies,
    ALVAC_studies            = ALVAC_studies,
    n_platforms              = n_platforms,
    n_sexes                  = length(sex_levels),
    n_adjuvants              = length(adj_levels),
    Platform_testable        = platform_ok,
    Platform_x_Sex           = platform_x_sex_ok,
    Platform_Sex_confounded  = platform_sex_confounded,
    Platform_x_Adjuvant      = platform_x_adjuvant_ok,
    Platform_Adjuvant_confounded = platform_adjuvant_confounded,     ### NEW
    Sex_Adjuvant_confounded  = sex_adjuvant_confounded,
    Sex_Adjuvant_detail      = sex_adjuvant_detail,
    Joint_PlatformSexAdjuvant_testable = joint_sex_adjuvant_testable,
    min_studies_per_cell     = min_studies_per_cell,                 ### NEW
    Platform_x_WeightAge     = weight_age_ok,
    Sex_main_effect          = sex_main_effect_ok
  )
}


## --------------------------------------------------------
## 5. Apply across all categories
## --------------------------------------------------------
testability_table <- category_design %>%
  dplyr::group_by(category) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(~ assess_testability(.x)) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()


cat("#### ", "Testable assay categories {.active}", "\n")
cat("\n")


cat("**Column definitions:**\n\n")
cat("- **n_studies**: number of studies contributing data for this analyte category.\n")
cat("- **DNA_studies**: which studies contribute DNA-platform data for this analyte.\n")
cat("- **ALVAC_studies**: which studies contribute ALVAC-platform data for this analyte.\n")
cat("- **n_platforms**: number of distinct vaccine platforms (DNA/ALVAC) represented; must be 2 for any Platform comparison.\n")
cat("- **n_sexes**: number of distinct sexes represented across studies with this analyte.\n")
cat("- **n_adjuvants**: number of distinct adjuvants (Alum/ALFQA) represented (Naive/NA excluded).\n")
cat("- **Platform_testable**: TRUE if both DNA and ALVAC platforms have data for this analyte, so a basic Platform (DNA vs ALVAC) comparison can be fit.\n")
cat("- **Platform_x_Sex**: TRUE only if every combination of Platform x Sex actually observed has at least one study with data (no empty cells), making the Platform:Sex interaction term identifiable.\n")
cat("- **Platform_Sex_confounded**: TRUE if every Platform maps to exactly one Sex (and vice versa) -- i.e. Platform and Sex are fully aliased. When TRUE, any 'Platform' effect (main or interaction) cannot be distinguished from a Sex effect, regardless of what Platform_x_Sex says.\n")
cat("- **Platform_x_Adjuvant**: TRUE only if every combination of Platform x Adjuvant actually observed has at least one study with data (no empty cells), making the Platform:Adjuvant interaction term identifiable.\n")
cat("- **Platform_Adjuvant_confounded**: TRUE if every Platform maps to exactly one Adjuvant (and vice versa) -- i.e. Platform and Adjuvant are fully aliased for this category's studies. Same logic as Platform_Sex_confounded, applied to Adjuvant instead of Sex.\n")
cat("- **Sex_Adjuvant_confounded**: TRUE if, within every Platform x Adjuvant combination present for this category, only one Sex is represented (e.g. ALVAC/ALFQA studies are all-Female while DNA/ALFQA studies are all-Male). Since Sex, Adjuvant, and Platform are constant within a study, this is directly checkable from the studies contributing to this category. When TRUE, a joint model containing both Platform:Sex and Platform:Adjuvant interaction terms cannot separate the two -- the higher-order term is non-estimable (lm()/coxph() report it as NA) even when Platform_x_Sex and Platform_x_Adjuvant above both show TRUE.\n")
cat("- **Sex_Adjuvant_detail**: which Sex is associated with each Platform/Adjuvant combination among this category's studies, e.g. 'DNA/Alum: Female,Male; DNA/ALFQA: Male; ALVAC/Alum: Male; ALVAC/ALFQA: Female' -- makes the confounding pattern, if any, directly visible.\n")
cat("- **Joint_PlatformSexAdjuvant_testable**: TRUE if a joint model with both Platform:Sex and Platform:Adjuvant interaction terms is identifiable for this category (i.e. Sex_Adjuvant_confounded is FALSE). When FALSE, expect the interaction-effect forest plot for this category to show that specific term as blank/non-estimable for every analyte, by design -- not a data or plotting error.\n")
cat("- **min_studies_per_cell**: the smallest number of distinct studies underlying any Platform x Sex x Adjuvant combination actually used by this category. A value of 1 means at least one such combination is defined by a single study -- that combination's apparent 'effect' cannot be separated from study-specific factors (housing, challenge stock, timing, cage effects), independent of which pairwise confounding flag (if any) is triggered above. Treat results involving a cell with min_studies_per_cell = 1 with extra caution even when the pairwise checks above all show FALSE/testable.\n")
cat("- **Platform_x_WeightAge**: TRUE if Platform itself is testable; Weight and Age at first challenge are available for all animals, so these continuous interactions don't depend on Sex/Adjuvant crossing. NOTE: this does not check whether Weight/Age actually vary independently of Platform/Sex/Adjuvant -- near-collinearity with a continuous covariate is a separate, harder-to-flag failure mode not currently checked here.\n")
cat("- **Sex_main_effect**: TRUE if more than one Sex is represented at all, allowing a Sex main effect to be estimated (not necessarily independent of Platform -- see Platform_Sex_confounded).\n")
cat("\n")

testability_table %>%
  DT::datatable(
    extensions = 'Buttons',
    options = list(dom = 'Blfrtip',
                   buttons = c('copy', 'csv', 'excel', 'pdf', 'print'),
                   iDisplayLength = 25,
                   lengthMenu = list(c(10, 25, 50, -1), c(10, 25, 50, "All")))
  ) %>%
  DT::formatStyle(
    columns = c("Platform_testable","Platform_x_Sex","Platform_x_Adjuvant","Platform_x_WeightAge",
                "Sex_main_effect","Joint_PlatformSexAdjuvant_testable"),
    backgroundColor = DT::styleEqual(c(TRUE, FALSE), c("lightgreen", "mistyrose"))
  ) %>%
  DT::formatStyle(
    columns = c("Platform_Sex_confounded", "Platform_Adjuvant_confounded", "Sex_Adjuvant_confounded"),
    backgroundColor = DT::styleEqual(c(TRUE, FALSE), c("orange", "white"))
  ) %>%
  DT::formatStyle(
    columns = "min_studies_per_cell",
    backgroundColor = DT::styleInterval(1, c("orange", "white"))
  )

cat("\n")
cat(' \n \n')


```





### lm for other analytes {.tabset}

```{r nonTOA_lm_setup}

## ============================================================
## Generalized Platform x Weight/Age forest-plot builder for
## NON-TOA assay outcomes (categories from the testability table:
## ADCC/Ab, Avidity, Cytokines/Chemokines, Efferocytosis, RM cell
## responses, Systemic cell responses).
##
## Mirrors the Cox-model forest-plot machinery already built for TOA
## (build_covariate_panel / build_interaction_panel), but swaps
## coxph(Surv(...) ~ ...) for lm(value ~ ...), since the outcome here
## is a continuous assay readout rather than a survival time.
##
## For each analyte, up to 4 dataset types are tested:
##   - Baseline  : Platform comparison AT baseline (checks for
##                 pre-existing imbalance -- NOT a vaccine effect;
##                 only fit if the analyte actually has baseline data)
##   - Post      : Platform comparison at the (first) post-vax timepoint
##   - Delta     : post - baseline, per animal
##   - FC        : 100 * post / baseline, per animal
## If an analyte has no Baseline timepoint at all, only "Post" is fit.
##
## Every model in the covariate-subset lineup is the lm() analog of
## the mw*/mc*/mi* Cox models already fit for TOA:
##   value ~ Platform
##   value ~ Platform + Sex
##   value ~ Platform + weight_c
##   value ~ Platform * weight_c
##   value ~ Platform + Sex + weight_c
##   value ~ Platform * Sex + Platform * weight_c
##   ... (Adjuvant swapped in for the vaccinated-only, adjuvant-testable
##        categories, same as Platform+Adjuvant / Platform*Adjuvant in TOA)
##
## ROW ORDER within every forest plot follows the SAME staircase
## convention used by build_covariate_panel() for TOA: rows are
## sorted by increasing n_covariates, then within a tier by a binary
## "sort_key" over covariate_vars (in a fixed column order), so the
## adjustment sequence reads Unadjusted -> single covariates (in a
## fixed order) -> pairs -> ... -> full model, IDENTICALLY across
## every analyte/category/dataset-type panel.
## ============================================================

## --------------------------------------------------------
## 0. Category -> variable list, keyed exactly to the testability
## table categories. Uses the same list_of_vars sources as elsewhere
## in the Rmd.
## --------------------------------------------------------
nonTOA_category_vars <- list(
  "ADCC/Ab only"                       = c(list_of_vars[["Abs_columns"]][!grepl(paste(c("Avi","pep"), collapse = '|'), list_of_vars[["Abs_columns"]])],
                                             list_of_vars[["ADCC_columns"]]),
  "V2peptides"                         = list_of_vars[["Abs_columns"]][grepl("pep", list_of_vars[["Abs_columns"]])],
  "Avidity score only"                 = list_of_vars[["Abs_columns"]][grepl("Avi", list_of_vars[["Abs_columns"]])],
    "Efferocytosis only"                 = list_of_vars[["eff_columns"]],
  ### break up since some have studyE
  "Cytokines/Chemokines (Panel D - most)"     = list_of_vars[["olink_columns"]][!grepl(paste(c("TSLP","IL4","IL27","IL13","IL10",
                                                                                               "IFNG","CCL7"), collapse = '|'),list_of_vars[["olink_columns"]])],
  "Cytokines/Chemokines (Panel D - TSLP set)"     = list_of_vars[["olink_columns"]][grepl(paste(c("TSLP","IL4","IL27","IL13","IL10",
                                                                                               "IFNG","CCL7"), collapse = '|'),list_of_vars[["olink_columns"]])],
  "RM cell responses (Panel B)"        = c(list_of_vars[["arifnew_NK"]],
                                             list_of_vars[["arifnew_mono"]],
                                             list_of_vars[["arifnew_DC"]]),
  "Systemic cell responses (Panel C)"  = c(list_of_vars[["massinew_mono"]],
                                             list_of_vars[["massinew_tcells"]])
)

# ## whether values in this category should be log10-transformed before
# ## modeling (matches existing convention: Ab titers / ADCC log10'd in
# ## Fig2/Fig3, olink NOT log10'd in the Cox models above, cell %s not
# ## log10'd). Adjust per your existing plotting conventions.
# nonTOA_category_log10 <- c(
#   "ADCC/Ab only"                      = TRUE,
#   "V2peptides"                        = FALSE,
#   "Avidity score only"                = FALSE,
#   "Cytokines/Chemokines (Panel D)"    = FALSE,
#   "Efferocytosis only"                = FALSE,
#   "RM cell responses (Panel B)"       = FALSE,
#   "Systemic cell responses (Panel C)" = FALSE
# )

## whether Adjuvant is a meaningful covariate for this category (per
## the testability table's Platform_x_Adjuvant column) -- categories
## where Naive-only studies dominate or adjuvant isn't crossed get
## Adjuvant dropped, same logic as covars_with_adjuvant/without above
nonTOA_category_use_adjuvant <- c(
  "ADCC/Ab only"                      = TRUE,
  "V2peptides"                        = TRUE,
  "Avidity score only"                = FALSE,
  "Efferocytosis only"                = TRUE,
  "Cytokines/Chemokines (Panel D - most)"     = TRUE,
  "Cytokines/Chemokines (Panel D - TSLP set)" = TRUE,
  "RM cell responses (Panel B)"       = TRUE,
  "Systemic cell responses (Panel C)" = FALSE
)

## whether Sex is testable at all for this category (per n_sexes in
## the testability table -- Systemic cell responses has only 1 sex
## represented, so Sex must be dropped there or every model errors)
nonTOA_category_use_sex <- c(
  "ADCC/Ab only"                      = TRUE,
  "V2peptides"                        = TRUE,
  "Avidity score only"                = TRUE,
  "Efferocytosis only"                = TRUE,
  "Cytokines/Chemokines (Panel D - most)"     = TRUE,
  "Cytokines/Chemokines (Panel D - TSLP set)" = TRUE,
  "RM cell responses (Panel B)"       = TRUE,
  "Systemic cell responses (Panel C)" = FALSE
)

## --------------------------------------------------------
## Fixed covariate column order used for the staircase sort in EVERY
## panel, regardless of category. Any covariate not usable for a given
## category (per the flags above) is simply absent from that
## category's models -- but when present, it always sorts in this
## relative order, so "Sex" is always the same column position, etc.
## --------------------------------------------------------
nonTOA_covariate_order <- c("Sex", "Adjuvant", "weight_c", "ageChall_c")

### --------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Pull Weight/AgeChallenge covariates (built earlier for the TOA
## Cox models) and merge onto a per-animal, Platform-labeled base
## frame. Re-derived here rather than assumed in-scope, so this chunk
## is safe to run standalone / out of order.
## --------------------------------------------------------
covariates_for_lm <- weights_df_base %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_ID, weight_at_first_challenge) %>%
  dplyr::full_join(
    age_df_base %>% dplyr::select(Sample_ID, age_at_first_challenge),
    by = "Sample_ID"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Sample_ID = as.character(Sample_ID))

## NOTE ON studyF: unlike df_for_cox (TOA/survival models), studyF is
## intentionally KEPT here. studyF (ALVAC/Alum) received an additional
## intervention (vaginal ring) that confounds the challenge/TOA outcome,
## which is why it's excluded from every Cox model above. But the
## nonTOA immune readouts (RM cell responses, cytokines, ADCC, etc.)
## were sampled BEFORE that second intervention, so studyF's data for
## those assays is not confounded by it and should be retained.
## Retaining studyF also matters for Adjuvant testability: studyF is
## the only ALVAC/Alum source besides studyD, so dropping it collapses
## the ALVAC side of several categories (e.g. RM cell responses) down
## to ALFQA-only (studyE), silently making Platform:Adjuvant
## non-identifiable even though the testability table (which does NOT
## exclude studyF) reports Platform_x_Adjuvant = TRUE for those
## categories.
animal_platform_df <- raw_df_TOA %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Platform = factor(Group_ignoreALFQA, levels = c("Naive", "DNA", "ALVAC")),
    Sex      = factor(Sex, levels = c("Male", "Female")),
    Adjuvant = factor(str_before_first(str_after_first(Group, "_"), "_"), levels = c("Alum", "ALFQA")),
    Sample_ID = as.character(Sample_ID)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_ID, Platform, Sex, Adjuvant) %>%
  dplyr::filter(Platform != "Naive") %>%          ## vaccinated only -- DNA vs ALVAC
  dplyr::mutate(Platform = droplevels(Platform)) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(covariates_for_lm, by = "Sample_ID") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    weight_c   = weight_at_first_challenge - mean(weight_at_first_challenge, na.rm = TRUE),
    ageChall_c = age_at_first_challenge - mean(age_at_first_challenge, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

covariate_labels_nonTOA <- c(
  Sex        = "Sex",
  Adjuvant   = "Adjuvant",
  weight_c   = "Weight",
  ageChall_c = "Age at Challenge"
)
```

```{r nonTOA_lm_functions}
## ============================================================
## Build the per-analyte, per-dataset-type long data frame:
## one row per animal x timepoint-comparison, with Platform/Sex/
## Adjuvant/weight_c/ageChall_c already attached, PLUS a rank_value
## column (rank of `value` computed WITHIN this exact data frame,
## i.e. within the exact set of animals/non-NA observations that
## this dataset type's models will actually use).
##
## All nonTOA lm() modeling is done on rank_value rather than the raw
## or log-transformed value, for consistency with the Mann-Whitney
## tests used everywhere else in this Rmd for pairwise group
## comparisons -- sample sizes here don't support assuming normality
## on the raw scale. Unadjusted rank-lm is asymptotically equivalent
## to Wilcoxon; covariate-adjusted rows become a genuine rank-ANCOVA.
##
## Consequence: forest plot x-axes for nonTOA panels are on a RANK
## scale, not original units or log-fold-change.
##
## Returns a *named list* of data frames, one per dataset type
## actually available for this analyte ("Baseline","Post","Delta","FC").
## ============================================================
build_analyte_lm_data <- function(analyte) {

  analyte_long <- phen_long %>%
    dplyr::filter(variable == analyte, !grepl("Naive", Group)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Sample_ID = as.character(Sample_ID))

  has_baseline <- any(analyte_long$Time_Point == "Baseline")

  ## first non-baseline timepoint actually present for this analyte
  post_tp <- analyte_long %>%
    dplyr::filter(Time_Point != "Baseline") %>%
    dplyr::pull(Time_Point) %>%
    unique()

  out <- list()

  if (length(post_tp) == 0) return(out)  ## nothing post-baseline to test -- skip analyte entirely

  post_tp_use <- post_tp[1]  ## first (should generally be only) non-baseline timepoint for a given analyte

  base_row <- animal_platform_df

  ## rank(), computed within whatever data frame is passed in --
  ## ties.method = "average" matches the mid-rank tie handling R's
  ## wilcox.test()/rstatix::wilcox_test() use internally
  add_rank <- function(df, value_col = "value") {
    df %>% dplyr::mutate(rank_value = rank(.data[[value_col]], ties.method = "average", na.last = "keep"))
  }

  ## ---- Post (always attempted if any post-baseline data exist) ----
  post_df <- analyte_long %>%
    dplyr::filter(Time_Point == post_tp_use) %>%
    dplyr::select(Sample_ID, amount) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(value = amount) %>%
    dplyr::inner_join(base_row, by = "Sample_ID") %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
    add_rank()

  if (nrow(post_df) > 0) out[["Post"]] <- post_df

  ## ---- Baseline / Delta / FC (only if baseline data exist) ----
  if (has_baseline) {

    baseline_df <- analyte_long %>%
      dplyr::filter(Time_Point == "Baseline") %>%
      dplyr::select(Sample_ID, amount) %>%
      dplyr::rename(baseline_amount = amount)

    base_out <- baseline_df %>%
      dplyr::mutate(value = baseline_amount) %>%
      dplyr::inner_join(base_row, by = "Sample_ID") %>%
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
      add_rank()
    if (nrow(base_out) > 0) out[["Baseline"]] <- base_out

    ## Delta / FC computed on RAW (untransformed) amount, per the
    ## existing convention elsewhere in the Rmd (FC/delta always
    ## computed pre-transform on raw values, see phen_long derivation).
    ## The RESULT (delta_value / FC_value) is then ranked, same as
    ## Baseline/Post above.
    delta_fc_df <- analyte_long %>%
      dplyr::filter(Time_Point == post_tp_use) %>%
      dplyr::select(Sample_ID, amount) %>%
      dplyr::inner_join(baseline_df, by = "Sample_ID") %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        delta_value = amount - baseline_amount,
        FC_value    = 100 * (amount / baseline_amount)
      )

    delta_out <- delta_fc_df %>%
      dplyr::mutate(value = delta_value) %>%
      dplyr::inner_join(base_row, by = "Sample_ID") %>%
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
      add_rank()
    if (nrow(delta_out) > 0) out[["Delta"]] <- delta_out

    fc_out <- delta_fc_df %>%
      dplyr::mutate(value = FC_value) %>%
      dplyr::inner_join(base_row, by = "Sample_ID") %>%
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
      add_rank()
    if (nrow(fc_out) > 0) out[["FC"]] <- fc_out
  }

  out
}


## --------------------------------------------------------
## Fit every covariate-subset lm() for ONE analyte x dataset-type
## combination, on rank_value, extract the Platform coefficient from
## each, and return one row per model. Rows are sorted by increasing
## n_covariates, then within a tier by a binary "sort_key" over
## covariate_vars (in a fixed column order), so the adjustment
## sequence reads Unadjusted -> single covariates (fixed order) ->
## pairs -> ... -> full model, IDENTICALLY across every
## analyte/category/dataset-type panel.
##
## covariate_vars: which of Sex/Adjuvant/weight_c/ageChall_c are
## usable for this analyte's category (already filtered by the
## category-level nonTOA_category_use_* flags before calling this)
## --------------------------------------------------------
fit_analyte_lm_subsets <- function(df, covariate_vars, covariate_labels, platform_ref = "DNA") {

  ## fix covariate_vars to the shared column order (restricted to what
  ## is actually available here) so sort_key lines up across analytes
  covariate_vars <- intersect(nonTOA_covariate_order, covariate_vars)

  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Platform = stats::relevel(factor(Platform), ref = platform_ref))

  other_level <- setdiff(levels(df$Platform), platform_ref)
  term_of_interest <- paste0("Platform", other_level)

  all_combo_rows <- purrr::map_dfr(0:length(covariate_vars), function(k) {

    combo_list <- if (k == 0) list(character(0)) else utils::combn(covariate_vars, k, simplify = FALSE)

    purrr::map_dfr(combo_list, function(covs) {

      rhs <- if (length(covs) == 0) "Platform" else paste("Platform", paste(covs, collapse = " + "), sep = " + ")

      fit <- tryCatch(
        stats::lm(stats::as.formula(paste0("rank_value ~ ", rhs)), data = df),
        error = function(e) NULL
      )
      if (is.null(fit)) return(NULL)

      coef_row <- broom::tidy(fit, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
        dplyr::filter(term == term_of_interest)

      if (nrow(coef_row) == 0) return(NULL)

      adjustment_label <- if (length(covs) == 0) {
        "Unadjusted"
      } else {
        paste0("+ ", paste(covariate_labels[covs], collapse = " + "))
      }

      dplyr::mutate(coef_row,
        adjustment   = adjustment_label,
        n_covariates = length(covs),
        n            = nrow(stats::model.frame(fit)),
        covs_raw     = list(covs)
      )
    })
  })

  if (nrow(all_combo_rows) == 0) return(all_combo_rows)

  all_combo_rows <- all_combo_rows %>%
    dplyr::rowwise() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(sort_key = paste(as.integer(covariate_vars %in% covs_raw), collapse = "")) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::arrange(n_covariates, dplyr::desc(sort_key))

  all_combo_rows
}


## --------------------------------------------------------
## Full pipeline for ONE category: loop over every analyte, fit the
## Platform-only-vs-covariate-adjusted rank-lm() lineup for every
## available dataset type (Baseline/Post/Delta/FC), and assemble one
## long data frame of results (one row per analyte x dataset-type x
## adjustment).
## --------------------------------------------------------
run_category_lm_panel <- function(category_name) {

  analytes <- nonTOA_category_vars[[category_name]]

  covariate_vars <- c("weight_c", "ageChall_c")
  if (isTRUE(nonTOA_category_use_sex[[category_name]]))      covariate_vars <- c("Sex", covariate_vars)
  if (isTRUE(nonTOA_category_use_adjuvant[[category_name]])) covariate_vars <- c(covariate_vars, "Adjuvant")

  results <- purrr::map_dfr(analytes, function(curr_analyte) {

    data_list <- build_analyte_lm_data(curr_analyte)

    purrr::imap_dfr(data_list, function(df, ds_type) {

      ## Adjuvant is undefined/NA for animals whose Adjuvant wasn't
      ## crossed with Platform in this particular analyte's available
      ## studies -- guard by dropping Adjuvant from THIS fit if either
      ## Platform level has <2 non-NA Adjuvant levels represented
      covs_use <- covariate_vars
      if ("Adjuvant" %in% covs_use) {
        adj_tab <- table(df$Platform, df$Adjuvant)
        if (any(rowSums(adj_tab > 0) < 2)) covs_use <- setdiff(covs_use, "Adjuvant")
      }
      if ("Sex" %in% covs_use) {
        sex_tab <- table(df$Platform, df$Sex)
        if (any(rowSums(sex_tab > 0) < 2)) covs_use <- setdiff(covs_use, "Sex")
      }

      fit_analyte_lm_subsets(df, covs_use, covariate_labels_nonTOA) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(analyte = curr_analyte, dataset_type = ds_type, category = category_name)
    })
  })

  results
}


## --------------------------------------------------------
## Fit every Platform*covariate interaction combination (up to
## max_size simultaneous interactions) for ONE analyte x dataset-type
## data frame, on rank_value. Returns one row PER INTERACTION TERM
## per model -- a model with 2 interaction terms contributes 2 rows.
## --------------------------------------------------------
fit_analyte_lm_interaction_subsets <- function(df, covariate_vars, covariate_labels,
                                                platform_ref = "DNA",
                                                max_size = length(covariate_vars)) {

  covariate_vars <- intersect(nonTOA_covariate_order, covariate_vars)
  if (length(covariate_vars) == 0) return(data.frame())

  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Platform = stats::relevel(factor(Platform), ref = platform_ref))

  other_level <- setdiff(levels(df$Platform), platform_ref)
  term_of_interest <- paste0("Platform", other_level)

  interaction_rows <- purrr::map_dfr(1:max_size, function(k) {

    combo_list <- utils::combn(covariate_vars, k, simplify = FALSE)

    purrr::map_dfr(combo_list, function(covs) {

      rhs <- paste(paste0("Platform * ", covs), collapse = " + ")

      fit <- tryCatch(
        stats::lm(stats::as.formula(paste0("rank_value ~ ", rhs)), data = df),
        error = function(e) NULL
      )
      if (is.null(fit)) return(NULL)

      fit_tidy <- broom::tidy(fit, conf.int = TRUE)
      n_used <- nrow(stats::model.frame(fit))

      purrr::map_dfr(covs, function(cov) {

        interaction_prefix <- paste0(term_of_interest, ":", cov)

        matched_rows <- fit_tidy %>%
          dplyr::filter(startsWith(term, interaction_prefix))

        if (nrow(matched_rows) == 0) return(NULL)

        matched_rows %>%
          dplyr::mutate(
            covariate    = unname(covariate_labels[cov]),
            active_cov   = cov,
            covs_raw     = list(covs),
            n_covariates = length(covs),
            n            = n_used
          )
      })
    })
  })

  if (nrow(interaction_rows) == 0) return(interaction_rows)

  interaction_rows <- interaction_rows %>%
    dplyr::rowwise() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(sort_key = paste(as.integer(covariate_vars %in% covs_raw), collapse = "")) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(active_cov_order = match(active_cov, covariate_vars)) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(active_cov_order, n_covariates, dplyr::desc(sort_key))

  interaction_rows
}


## --------------------------------------------------------
## Full pipeline for ONE category's INTERACTION panel: loop over
## every analyte, fit the Platform*covariate interaction lineup (on
## rank_value) for every available dataset type, and assemble one
## long data frame of results.
## --------------------------------------------------------
run_category_lm_interaction_panel <- function(category_name, max_size = NULL) {

  analytes <- nonTOA_category_vars[[category_name]]

  covariate_vars <- c("weight_c", "ageChall_c")
  if (isTRUE(nonTOA_category_use_sex[[category_name]]))      covariate_vars <- c("Sex", covariate_vars)
  if (isTRUE(nonTOA_category_use_adjuvant[[category_name]])) covariate_vars <- c(covariate_vars, "Adjuvant")

  ## restrict to the shared column order up front, same set the
  ## staircase sort uses inside fit_analyte_lm_interaction_subsets()
  covariate_vars <- intersect(nonTOA_covariate_order, covariate_vars)

  if (is.null(max_size)) max_size <- length(covariate_vars)
  if (max_size == 0) return(data.frame())

  results <- purrr::map_dfr(analytes, function(curr_analyte) {

    data_list <- build_analyte_lm_data(curr_analyte)

    purrr::imap_dfr(data_list, function(df, ds_type) {

      ## same per-fit guarding as run_category_lm_panel(): drop
      ## Adjuvant/Sex from THIS analyte's interaction models if either
      ## Platform level has <2 non-NA levels of that covariate
      covs_use <- covariate_vars
      if ("Adjuvant" %in% covs_use) {
        adj_tab <- table(df$Platform, df$Adjuvant)
        if (any(rowSums(adj_tab > 0) < 2)) covs_use <- setdiff(covs_use, "Adjuvant")
      }
      if ("Sex" %in% covs_use) {
        sex_tab <- table(df$Platform, df$Sex)
        if (any(rowSums(sex_tab > 0) < 2)) covs_use <- setdiff(covs_use, "Sex")
      }

      if (length(covs_use) == 0) return(NULL)

      fit_analyte_lm_interaction_subsets(
        df, covs_use, covariate_labels_nonTOA,
        max_size = min(max_size, length(covs_use))
      ) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(analyte = curr_analyte, dataset_type = ds_type, category = category_name)
    })
  })

  results
}

```

```{r nonTOA_lm_plot_function}

## ============================================================
## Given main-effect results and interaction results for one
## category/dataset_type, compute the UNION of analytes that are
## significant in EITHER panel. This is then used to force both
## filter_sig_analytes() and filter_sig_analytes_interaction() to
## show the same set of analytes, rather than each independently
## deciding "significant for me" and potentially diverging.
## ============================================================

get_shared_sig_analytes <- function(main_results_df, interaction_results_df,
                                     category_name, ds_type, sig_cutoff = 0.05) {

  main_hits <- main_results_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(category == category_name, dataset_type == ds_type) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(analyte) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(any_sig = any(p.value < sig_cutoff, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::filter(any_sig) %>%
    dplyr::pull(analyte)

  int_hits <- if (nrow(interaction_results_df) > 0) {
    interaction_results_df %>%
      dplyr::filter(category == category_name, dataset_type == ds_type) %>%
      dplyr::group_by(analyte) %>%
      dplyr::summarise(any_sig = any(p.value < sig_cutoff, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
      dplyr::filter(any_sig) %>%
      dplyr::pull(analyte)
  } else {
    character(0)
  }

  main_hits <- as.character(main_hits)
  int_hits  <- as.character(int_hits)

  list(
    union         = union(main_hits, int_hits),
    main_only     = setdiff(main_hits, int_hits),
    interaction_only = setdiff(int_hits, main_hits),
    both          = intersect(main_hits, int_hits)
  )
}

## ============================================================
## Filter results down to analytes with >=1 significant model
## (any adjustment level, not necessarily Unadjusted), for ONE
## category x dataset_type combination. Returns NULL if nothing
## qualifies, otherwise a filtered+ordered data frame ready to plot.
##
## Facets are sorted ALPHABETICALLY (sort_by = "alphabetical") so a
## specific analyte of interest can be found quickly. Pass
## sort_by = "pvalue" at a given call site to instead rank facets by
## best (smallest) p-value across adjustment levels.
##
## analytes_override: if supplied (e.g. the shared union list from
## get_shared_sig_analytes()), use THIS set of analytes directly
## instead of independently recomputing "any_sig" from results_df --
## mirrors filter_sig_analytes_interaction()'s override mechanism, so
## Main Effect and Interaction Effect panels can be forced to show the
## exact same set of analytes.
## ============================================================
filter_sig_analytes <- function(results_df, category_name, ds_type, sig_cutoff = 0.05,
                                 sort_by = c("alphabetical", "pvalue"),
                                 analytes_override = NULL) {

  sort_by <- match.arg(sort_by)

  df <- results_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(category == category_name, dataset_type == ds_type)

  if (nrow(df) == 0) return(NULL)

  ## keep only analytes where AT LEAST ONE model (any adjustment level)
  ## is significant -- if every adjustment level for an analyte is
  ## non-significant, drop it from this panel entirely -- UNLESS an
  ## explicit override list is supplied, in which case use that
  ## instead (intersected with what's actually present in df)
  if (!is.null(analytes_override)) {
    analytes_with_hit <- intersect(analytes_override, unique(as.character(df$analyte)))
  } else {
    analytes_with_hit <- df %>%
      dplyr::group_by(analyte) %>%
      dplyr::summarise(any_sig = any(p.value < sig_cutoff, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
      dplyr::filter(any_sig) %>%
      dplyr::pull(analyte)
  }

  if (length(analytes_with_hit) == 0) return(NULL)

  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::filter(analyte %in% analytes_with_hit)

  if (sort_by == "alphabetical") {
    analyte_order <- sort(unique(as.character(df$analyte)))
  } else {
    ## order analytes by their BEST (smallest) p-value across all
    ## adjustment levels -- not just Unadjusted
    analyte_order <- df %>%
      dplyr::group_by(analyte) %>%
      dplyr::summarise(best_p = min(p.value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
      dplyr::arrange(best_p) %>%
      dplyr::pull(analyte)
  }

  df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      analyte = factor(analyte, analyte_order),
      ## adjustment factor levels fixed by the SAME staircase order
      ## used when the rows were generated (n_covariates, desc(sort_key))
      ## rather than re-derived here, so every analyte's facet shows
      ## rows in identical order top-to-bottom
      adjustment = factor(adjustment, unique(adjustment[order(n_covariates, dplyr::desc(sort_key))])),
      p_label = dplyr::if_else(p.value < 0.001, "<0.001", formatC(p.value, digits = 3, format = "f")),
      sig = p.value < sig_cutoff
    )
}


## --------------------------------------------------------
## Filter interaction results down to analytes with >=1 significant
## interaction term (any active covariate, any adjustment level), for
## ONE category x dataset_type combination. Mirrors filter_sig_analytes()
## but operates on interaction rows (keyed by term/active_cov instead
## of by adjustment alone). Same alphabetical-by-default facet sort.
##
## Builds `row_label` as a human-readable string (needed by
## plot_category_forest_interaction()'s df_filtered$row_label), while
## also preserving covs_raw/active_cov (needed by the grid builder
## build_nonTOA_upset_grid_interaction()).
## --------------------------------------------------------
filter_sig_analytes_interaction <- function(results_df, category_name, ds_type, sig_cutoff = 0.05,
                                             sort_by = c("alphabetical", "pvalue"),
                                             analytes_override = NULL) {

  sort_by <- match.arg(sort_by)

  df <- results_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(category == category_name, dataset_type == ds_type)

  if (nrow(df) == 0) return(NULL)

  ## NEW: same override mechanism as filter_sig_analytes()
  if (!is.null(analytes_override)) {
    analytes_with_hit <- intersect(analytes_override, unique(as.character(df$analyte)))
  } else {
    analytes_with_hit <- df %>%
      dplyr::group_by(analyte) %>%
      dplyr::summarise(any_sig = any(p.value < sig_cutoff, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
      dplyr::filter(any_sig) %>%
      dplyr::pull(analyte)
  }

  if (length(analytes_with_hit) == 0) return(NULL)

  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::filter(analyte %in% analytes_with_hit)

  if (sort_by == "alphabetical") {
    analyte_order <- sort(unique(as.character(df$analyte)))
  } else {
    analyte_order <- df %>%
      dplyr::group_by(analyte) %>%
      dplyr::summarise(best_p = min(p.value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
      dplyr::arrange(best_p) %>%
      dplyr::pull(analyte)
  }

  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::rowwise() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      covs_in_model = paste(sort(unname(covariate_labels_nonTOA[unlist(covs_raw)])), collapse = " + "),
      row_label_readable = if (n_covariates == 1) {
        covariate
      } else {
        paste0(covs_in_model, " (", covariate, " term)")
      }
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      analyte    = factor(analyte, analyte_order),
      row_label  = row_label_readable,
      p_label    = dplyr::if_else(p.value < 0.001, "<0.001", formatC(p.value, digits = 3, format = "f")),
      sig        = p.value < sig_cutoff
    )

  row_order <- df %>%
    dplyr::distinct(active_cov_order, n_covariates, sort_key, row_label) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(active_cov_order, n_covariates, dplyr::desc(sort_key)) %>%
    dplyr::pull(row_label) %>%
    unique()

  df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(row_label = factor(row_label, row_order))
}

 

## ============================================================
## Simple row-label column, used in place of the UpSet grid when
## there are <=2 covariates (so the grid would only ever show 0-2
## trivial columns and isn't worth the visual overhead). Draws just
## the y-axis text for each row, at the same vertical positions the
## forest panels use, so it drops into the same patchwork "grid slot"
## the real UpSet grid would otherwise occupy -- keeping every
## analyte panel the same width regardless of covariate count.
## ============================================================
build_row_label_column <- function(rows_df, row_key) {

  label_df <- rows_df %>%
    dplyr::distinct(.data[[row_key]]) %>%
    dplyr::rename(row_label = !!row_key)

  ggplot2::ggplot(label_df, ggplot2::aes(x = 1, y = row_label)) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = row_label), size = 2.5, hjust = 1) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.05), breaks = NULL) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    ggplot2::theme_void() +
    ggplot2::theme(
      axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 2, r = 2, b = 2, l = 2)
    )
}


## ============================================================
## Build a placeholder panel for an analyte that has no data for this
## panel type (e.g. significant in Main Effect but dropped from the
## Interaction Effect fits due to insufficient Sex/Adjuvant variation,
## or vice versa). Keeps the panel grid slot occupied and the analyte
## title visible, rather than silently omitting the analyte from one
## of the two side-by-side panels.
## ============================================================
build_empty_analyte_panel <- function(analyte_name, x_lab_note = "no data for this model type",
                                       show_title = TRUE) {
  ggplot2::ggplot() +
    ggplot2::annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.5, label = x_lab_note,
                      size = 2.5, color = "grey50", fontface = "italic") +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
    ggplot2::labs(title = if (show_title) analyte_name else NULL) +
    ggplot2::theme_bw() +
    ggplot2::theme(
      plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5,
                                         margin = ggplot2::margin(b = 4)),
      axis.title = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      axis.text  = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      axis.ticks = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 2, r = 4, b = 2, l = 2)
    )
}




## ============================================================
## Grid-matrix builder for the MAIN-EFFECT panel (one row per
## adjustment level, no "active covariate" distinction needed --
## every covariate in covs_raw is just a co-adjuster). Used when a
## category has >2 covariates in play (row count would exceed 4:
## Unadjusted + up to 2 single covariates + their pair) -- see
## plot_category_forest() below for the trigger logic.
## ============================================================
build_nonTOA_upset_grid <- function(rows_df, covariate_vars, covariate_labels, row_key = "adjustment") {

  grid_base <- rows_df %>%
    dplyr::distinct(.data[[row_key]], covs_raw) %>%
    dplyr::rename(row_label = !!row_key)

  upset_long <- grid_base %>%
    dplyr::mutate(covariate = list(covariate_vars)) %>%
    tidyr::unnest(covariate) %>%
    dplyr::rowwise() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(is_member = covariate %in% covs_raw) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      covariate_label = factor(covariate_labels[covariate], levels = covariate_labels[covariate_vars])
    )

  upset_segments <- upset_long %>%
    dplyr::filter(is_member) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(row_label) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      x_min = min(as.integer(covariate_label)),
      x_max = max(as.integer(covariate_label)),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  ggplot2::ggplot() +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
      data = upset_long,
      ggplot2::aes(x = covariate_label, y = row_label),
      color = "grey85", size = 2.2
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_segment(
      data = upset_segments,
      ggplot2::aes(x = x_min, xend = x_max, y = row_label, yend = row_label),
      color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.6
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
      data = dplyr::filter(upset_long, is_member),
      ggplot2::aes(x = covariate_label, y = row_label),
      color = "grey20", size = 2.6
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
    ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    ggplot2::theme_bw() +
    ggplot2::theme(
      panel.grid.major.y = ggplot2::element_line(color = "grey93"),
      panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor   = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      axis.text.x.top    = ggplot2::element_text(size = 7, angle = 40, hjust = 0),
      axis.text.y        = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y       = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      plot.margin        = ggplot2::margin(r = 2)
    )
}


## ============================================================
## Grid-matrix builder for the INTERACTION panel. One row per
## (row_label) as constructed by filter_sig_analytes_interaction() --
## since row_label there is human-readable, we key the grid off the
## underlying (active_cov, covs_raw) combination directly, then
## re-attach row_label as the y-axis factor so ordering / joins with
## df_filtered stay consistent.
##
## Distinguishes, per row:
##   - the ACTIVE covariate (the one this row's estimate/CI describe)
##     -> larger, colored dot (colored same as forest plot's
##        active_cov color, via covariate_color_vec passed in)
##   - CO-INTERACTED covariates present in the same joint model
##     -> smaller grey dot
## ============================================================
build_nonTOA_upset_grid_interaction <- function(rows_df, covariate_vars, covariate_labels,
                                                 covariate_color_vec, row_key = "row_label") {

  grid_base <- rows_df %>%
    dplyr::distinct(.data[[row_key]], covs_raw, active_cov)

  upset_long <- grid_base %>%
    dplyr::rename(row_label = !!row_key) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(covariate = list(covariate_vars)) %>%
    tidyr::unnest(covariate) %>%
    dplyr::rowwise() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      is_member = covariate %in% covs_raw,
      is_active = covariate == active_cov
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      covariate_label = factor(covariate_labels[covariate], levels = covariate_labels[covariate_vars]),
      dot_color = ifelse(is_active, unname(covariate_color_vec[covariate]), NA_character_)
    )

  upset_segments <- upset_long %>%
    dplyr::filter(is_member) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(row_label) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      x_min = min(as.integer(covariate_label)),
      x_max = max(as.integer(covariate_label)),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  ggplot2::ggplot() +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
      data = upset_long,
      ggplot2::aes(x = covariate_label, y = row_label),
      color = "grey85", size = 2.2
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_segment(
      data = upset_segments,
      ggplot2::aes(x = x_min, xend = x_max, y = row_label, yend = row_label),
      color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.6
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
      data = dplyr::filter(upset_long, is_member, !is_active),
      ggplot2::aes(x = covariate_label, y = row_label),
      color = "grey20", size = 2.6
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
      data = dplyr::filter(upset_long, is_active),
      ggplot2::aes(x = covariate_label, y = row_label, color = dot_color),
      size = 3.4
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_color_identity() +
    ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
    ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    ggplot2::theme_bw() +
    ggplot2::theme(
      panel.grid.major.y = ggplot2::element_line(color = "grey93"),
      panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor   = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      axis.text.x.top    = ggplot2::element_text(size = 7, angle = 40, hjust = 0),
      axis.text.y        = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y       = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      plot.margin        = ggplot2::margin(r = 2)
    )
}




## ============================================================
## Compute how many rows facet_wrap(..., ncol=n) will produce for
## a given number of panels -- needed so we can repeat the single
## grid once per facet-row.
## ============================================================
n_facet_rows <- function(n_panels, ncol) {
  ceiling(n_panels / ncol)
}
```
