```{r nonTOA_lm_plot_function}
## ============================================================
## Robust replacement for build_repeated_grid_column() +
## plot_category_forest()/plot_category_forest_interaction()'s final
## combine step.
##
## Strategy: instead of building the grid as one tall stack and the
## forest as one facet_wrap() plot and hoping their row heights match,
## build ONE ggplot per analyte panel (no facet_wrap at all), and lay
## every analyte panel + the row's shared grid-panel out together in a
## single patchwork::wrap_plots(design=...) call. Every element is a
## leaf-level plot at the same nesting depth, so patchwork's internal
## alignment (which is exact for sibling plots, but NOT reliable across
## separately-nested sub-patchworks) guarantees the grid and its row of
## forest panels line up pixel-for-pixel.
## ============================================================

## --------------------------------------------------------
## Build a single analyte panel (no facets) -- these replace the
## facet_wrap(~analyte) panels one at a time.
## --------------------------------------------------------
 build_single_analyte_panel <- function(df_analyte, analyte_name, y_var, color_var,
                                        color_scale, x_lab, show_x_axis = TRUE,
                                        show_title = TRUE, x_range = NULL) {

  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(df_analyte, ggplot2::aes(x = estimate, y = .data[[y_var]], color = .data[[color_var]])) +
    ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
    ggplot2::geom_errorbarh(ggplot2::aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high), height = 0.2) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(shape = sig), size = 1.8) +
    ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(name = "p < 0.05", values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 1)) +
    color_scale +
    ggplot2::labs(
      ### x-axis TITLE is never drawn per-panel anymore -- it's added
      ### once, centered under the whole combined figure, via
      ### patchwork::plot_annotation(caption = x_lab) in
      ### plot_category_forest()/plot_category_forest_interaction().
      ### Tick labels (the numbers) still appear per-column via
      ### show_x_axis, independent of the title.
      x = NULL,
      y = NULL,
      title = if (show_title) analyte_name else NULL
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_bw() +
    ggplot2::theme(
      plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5,
                                         margin = ggplot2::margin(b = 4)),
      axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      axis.text.x = if (show_x_axis) ggplot2::element_text(size = 7) else ggplot2::element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = if (show_x_axis) ggplot2::element_line() else ggplot2::element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 2, r = 4, b = 2, l = 2)
    )

  if (!is.null(x_range)) {
    p <- p + ggplot2::coord_cartesian(xlim = x_range)
  }

  p
}

## --------------------------------------------------------
## Build ONE small grid panel (the covariate UpSet matrix), used
## once per facet-ROW. `show_x_labels` controls whether the top
## covariate-name axis text is drawn (only the very first row needs it).
## --------------------------------------------------------
build_single_grid_panel <- function(grid_rows_df, covariate_vars, covariate_labels,
                                     row_key, is_interaction = FALSE,
                                     covariate_color_vec = NULL, show_x_labels = TRUE) {

  p <- if (is_interaction) {
    build_nonTOA_upset_grid_interaction(
      rows_df             = grid_rows_df,
      covariate_vars      = covariate_vars,
      covariate_labels    = covariate_labels,
      covariate_color_vec = covariate_color_vec,
      row_key             = row_key
    )
  } else {
    build_nonTOA_upset_grid(
      rows_df          = grid_rows_df,
      covariate_vars   = covariate_vars,
      covariate_labels = covariate_labels,
      row_key          = row_key
    )
  }

  if (!show_x_labels) {
    p <- p + ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x.top = ggplot2::element_blank())
  }

  ## match vertical margins to build_single_analyte_panel() so row
  ## heights agree regardless of title/axis text presence
  p + ggplot2::theme(plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 2, r = 2, b = 2, l = 2))
}

## --------------------------------------------------------
## Master assembler: builds the full grid | forest-panels layout as
## ONE flat list of leaf plots + a patchwork::wrap_plots(design=)
## string, so every row's grid and every row's analyte panels are
## guaranteed the same height (they're siblings in one patchwork call,
## not two independently-stacked sub-patchworks being glued together).

## instead of relying on patchwork::plot_annotation(caption = x_lab)
## (which patchwork always places at the very bottom of the WHOLE
## figure, below the collected legend), we add an explicit one-row-tall
## "axis title" panel as the LAST row of the wrap_plots(design=...)
## call itself. Since that row is part of the collected plot (not an
## annotation), the subsequent `& theme(legend.position = "bottom")`
## collected legend still renders below it -- giving the order:
##   [forest panels] -> [x-axis title row] -> [collected legend]
## instead of the old:
##   [forest panels] -> [collected legend] -> [caption/x-axis title]
## ============================================================

assemble_grid_forest_layout <- function(df_filtered, y_var, color_var, color_scale,
                                         covariate_vars, covariate_labels,
                                         x_lab, ncol = 4, is_interaction = FALSE,
                                         covariate_color_vec = NULL, use_grid = TRUE,
                                         shared_x_range = TRUE,
                                         all_analytes = NULL) {

  analyte_levels <- if (!is.null(all_analytes)) {
    sort(unique(all_analytes))
  } else {
    lv <- levels(df_filtered$analyte)
    if (is.null(lv)) unique(as.character(df_filtered$analyte)) else lv
  }

  n_analytes <- length(analyte_levels)
  n_row <- ceiling(n_analytes / ncol)

  row_groups <- split(analyte_levels, ceiling(seq_along(analyte_levels) / ncol))

  analytes_with_data <- unique(as.character(df_filtered$analyte))
  first_analyte_with_data <- analyte_levels[analyte_levels %in% analytes_with_data][1]
  grid_rows_df <- dplyr::filter(df_filtered, as.character(analyte) == first_analyte_with_data)

  x_range <- NULL
  if (shared_x_range) {
    rng <- range(c(df_filtered$conf.low, df_filtered$conf.high, df_filtered$estimate), na.rm = TRUE)
    pad <- diff(rng) * 0.05
    if (is.finite(pad) && pad > 0) {
      x_range <- c(rng[1] - pad, rng[2] + pad)
    } else {
      x_range <- rng
    }
  }

  plot_list <- list()
  areas_list <- list()

  n_data_cols <- ncol
  col_offset_base <- 1

  last_row_per_col <- sapply(seq_len(n_data_cols), function(j) {
    rows_with_this_col <- which(sapply(row_groups, function(ra) j <= length(ra)))
    if (length(rows_with_this_col) == 0) NA_integer_ else max(rows_with_this_col)
  })

  for (r in seq_len(n_row)) {

    row_analytes <- row_groups[[as.character(r)]]

    if (use_grid) {
      grid_id <- paste0("grid", r)
      plot_list[[grid_id]] <- build_single_grid_panel(
        grid_rows_df, covariate_vars, covariate_labels, y_var,
        is_interaction = is_interaction, covariate_color_vec = covariate_color_vec,
        show_x_labels = (r == 1)
      )
    } else {
      grid_id <- paste0("grid", r)
      plot_list[[grid_id]] <- build_row_label_column(grid_rows_df, y_var)
    }
    areas_list[[grid_id]] <- patchwork::area(t = r, l = 1, b = r, r = 1)
    col_offset <- col_offset_base

    for (j in seq_len(n_data_cols)) {
      if (j <= length(row_analytes)) {
        a <- row_analytes[j]
        df_a <- dplyr::filter(df_filtered, as.character(analyte) == a)
        panel_id <- paste0("p_", r, "_", j)

        if (nrow(df_a) == 0) {
          plot_list[[panel_id]] <- build_empty_analyte_panel(a)
        } else {
          plot_list[[panel_id]] <- build_single_analyte_panel(
            df_a, a, y_var, color_var, color_scale, x_lab,
            show_x_axis = (r == last_row_per_col[j]),
            show_title = TRUE,
            x_range = x_range
          )
        }
      } else {
        panel_id <- paste0("pad_", r, "_", j)
        plot_list[[panel_id]] <- patchwork::plot_spacer()
      }
      areas_list[[panel_id]] <- patchwork::area(
        t = r, l = col_offset + j, b = r, r = col_offset + j
      )
    }
  }

  ## --------------------------------------------------------
  ## NEW: dedicated x-axis title row, spanning the full width
  ## (grid column + all data columns), placed in the row immediately
  ## after the last panel row. Built as a minimal ggplot with just the
  ## x-axis title text so patchwork can align/collect it like a normal
  ## panel, rather than via plot_annotation(caption=), which always
  ## renders below the collected legend.
  ## --------------------------------------------------------
  title_row <- n_row + 1

  axis_title_panel <- ggplot2::ggplot() +
    ggplot2::annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.5, label = x_lab, size = 3.6, fontface = "plain") +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
    ggplot2::theme_void() +
    ggplot2::theme(plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 4, b = 2))

  plot_list[["axis_title"]] <- axis_title_panel
  areas_list[["axis_title"]] <- patchwork::area(
    t = title_row, l = 1, b = title_row, r = col_offset_base + n_data_cols
  )

  design_areas <- Reduce(c, areas_list)

  widths  <- c(1, rep(1, n_data_cols))
  ## title row gets a small fixed-ish height relative to the panel rows
  heights <- c(rep(1, n_row), 0.18)

  patchwork::wrap_plots(plot_list, design = design_areas, widths = widths, heights = heights) +
    patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}

## ============================================================
## MAIN-EFFECT forest plot. When a category has >2 covariates in
## play (union of covs_raw across every row in the panel), the plain-
## English adjustment labels are replaced by the UpSet-style grid
## matrix (via build_nonTOA_upset_grid()); with <=2 covariates
## (<=4 rows: Unadjusted, +CovA, +CovB, +CovA+CovB), plain-English
## y-axis text labels are kept.
##
## X-axis is explicitly labeled "(rank scale)" since every estimate
## here comes from lm(rank_value ~ ...), not the analyte's original
## units -- consistent with the Mann-Whitney tests used elsewhere.
## ============================================================
plot_category_forest <- function(df_filtered, category_name, ds_type,
                                  palette = c("gold", "darkorange","magenta2", "purple4"),
                                  ncol = 4, all_analytes = NULL) {

  if (is.null(df_filtered) || nrow(df_filtered) == 0) return(NULL)

  df_filtered <- df_filtered %>%
    dplyr::mutate(adjustment = factor(adjustment, rev(levels(adjustment))))

  covariate_vars_used <- df_filtered$covs_raw %>%
    unlist() %>% unique() %>% intersect(nonTOA_covariate_order)

  use_grid <- length(covariate_vars_used) > 2

  color_scale <- ggplot2::scale_color_gradientn(name = "# covariates\nadjusted for", colors = palette)

  x_lab_shared <- "ALVAC vs DNA effect (rank scale)"

  p_combined <- assemble_grid_forest_layout(
    df_filtered       = df_filtered,
    y_var             = "adjustment",
    color_var         = "n_covariates",
    color_scale       = color_scale,
    covariate_vars    = covariate_vars_used,
    covariate_labels  = covariate_labels_nonTOA,
    x_lab             = x_lab_shared,
    ncol              = ncol,
    is_interaction    = FALSE,
    use_grid          = use_grid,
    all_analytes      = all_analytes   ### NEW
  )

  p_combined +
    patchwork::plot_annotation(
      title = paste0(category_name, " \u2014 ", ds_type),
      subtitle = "Rows (top\u2192bottom): Unadjusted \u2192 increasing covariate adjustment \u2192 full model. Point = estimate, bar = 95% CI, both on the rank scale (consistent with Mann-Whitney)."
    )


}



plot_category_forest_interaction <- function(df_filtered, category_name, ds_type,
                                              color_low = "turquoise3", color_high = "blue4",
                                              ncol = 4, all_analytes = NULL) {

  if (is.null(df_filtered) || nrow(df_filtered) == 0) return(NULL)

  covs_present <- intersect(nonTOA_covariate_order, unique(df_filtered$active_cov))
  covariate_color_vec <- setNames(
    grDevices::colorRampPalette(c(color_low, color_high))(length(covs_present)),
    covs_present
  )

  df_filtered <- df_filtered %>%
    dplyr::mutate(row_label = factor(row_label, rev(levels(row_label))))

  covariate_vars_used <- df_filtered$covs_raw %>%
    unlist() %>% unique() %>% intersect(nonTOA_covariate_order)

  use_grid <- length(covariate_vars_used) > 2

  color_scale <- ggplot2::scale_color_manual(
    name = "Interaction\ncovariate",
    values = covariate_color_vec,
    breaks = covs_present,
    labels = unname(covariate_labels_nonTOA[covs_present])
  )

  x_lab_shared <- "Interaction effect (rank scale)"

  p_combined <- assemble_grid_forest_layout(
    df_filtered          = df_filtered %>% dplyr::mutate(color_col = active_cov),
    y_var                = "row_label",
    color_var            = "color_col",
    color_scale          = color_scale,
    covariate_vars       = covariate_vars_used,
    covariate_labels     = covariate_labels_nonTOA,
    x_lab                = x_lab_shared,
    ncol                 = ncol,
    is_interaction       = TRUE,
    covariate_color_vec  = covariate_color_vec,
    use_grid             = use_grid,
    all_analytes         = all_analytes   ### NEW
  )

p_combined +
    patchwork::plot_annotation(
      title = paste0(category_name, " \u2014 ", ds_type, ": does a covariate modify the Platform effect?"),
      subtitle = "Rows: one interaction term per model, grouped by active covariate (univariate \u2192 jointly adjusted)."
    )
}
```

```{r nonTOA_lm_run_all, results='asis', fig.height=12, fig.width=12}
## --------------------------------------------------------
## Run every category and render its tabs. Dataset-type tabs only
## appear if that category actually produced results for them. Within
## each dataset-type tab, TWO sub-tabs are now shown:
##   "Main effect"        -- Platform effect across covariate subsets
##                            (unchanged from before: filter_sig_analytes /
##                            plot_category_forest)
##   "Interaction effect" -- does a covariate MODIFY the Platform effect?
##                            (NEW: filter_sig_analytes_interaction /
##                            plot_category_forest_interaction)
## --------------------------------------------------------

nonTOA_all_results <- list()
nonTOA_all_results_interaction <- list()   ## NEW: collect interaction results too

for (curr_category in names(nonTOA_category_vars)) {

  cat("#### ", paste0(curr_category, " {.tabset}"), "\n")
  cat("\n")

  cat_results <- run_category_lm_panel(curr_category)
  nonTOA_all_results[[curr_category]] <- cat_results

  cat_results_int <- run_category_lm_interaction_panel(curr_category)
  nonTOA_all_results_interaction[[curr_category]] <- cat_results_int

  if (nrow(cat_results) == 0) {
    cat(" ", "no analytes with fittable data in this category", "\n")
    cat("\n")
    cat("\n")
    cat(' \n \n')
    next
  }

  ds_types_present <- intersect(c("Baseline", "Post", "Delta", "FC"), unique(cat_results$dataset_type))

  for (curr_ds in ds_types_present) {

    cat("##### ", paste0(curr_ds, " {.tabset}"), "\n")
    cat("\n")

    n_total_analytes <- length(unique(cat_results$analyte[cat_results$dataset_type == curr_ds]))

    ## NEW: compute the shared analyte list ONCE, from both main-effect
    ## and interaction results together, so both sub-tabs below use the
    ## exact same set -- an analyte significant in either panel now
    ## appears in both, with the non-significant panel simply showing
    ## its (non-significant) rows rather than being omitted entirely.
## NEW: get_shared_sig_analytes() now returns a list with the union
    ## plus the main-only / interaction-only / both breakdown
    shared_hits <- get_shared_sig_analytes(
      main_results_df        = cat_results,
      interaction_results_df = cat_results_int,
      category_name           = curr_category,
      ds_type                 = curr_ds
    )
    shared_analytes <- shared_hits$union

    breakdown_str <- paste0(
      length(shared_hits$main_only), " main effect only, ",
      length(shared_hits$interaction_only), " interaction only, ",
      length(shared_hits$both), " both"
    )

    ## ---- Main effect sub-tab ----
    cat("###### ", "Main effect", "\n")
    cat("\n")

    df_filtered <- filter_sig_analytes(cat_results, curr_category, curr_ds,
                                        analytes_override = shared_analytes)

    if (!is.null(df_filtered)) {

      n_kept <- length(unique(df_filtered$analyte))
      cat(" ", paste0(n_kept, " of ", n_total_analytes,
                      " analytes were significant (main effect or interaction): ",
                      breakdown_str, "."), "\n")
      cat("\n")

      p <- plot_category_forest(df_filtered, curr_category, curr_ds, all_analytes = shared_analytes)
      print(p)

    } else {
      cat(" ", paste0("no analytes (of ", n_total_analytes,
                      ") had any significant model or interaction for this dataset type -- panel omitted"), "\n")
    }

    cat("\n")
    cat(' \n \n')

    ## ---- Interaction effect sub-tab ----
    cat("###### ", "Interaction effect", "\n")
    cat("\n")

    n_total_analytes_int <- if (nrow(cat_results_int) > 0) {
      length(unique(cat_results_int$analyte[cat_results_int$dataset_type == curr_ds]))
    } else {
      0
    }

    if (nrow(cat_results_int) == 0) {

      cat(" ", "no interaction models could be fit for this dataset type (e.g. no usable covariates for this category) -- panel omitted", "\n")

    } else {

      df_filtered_int <- filter_sig_analytes_interaction(cat_results_int, curr_category, curr_ds,
                                                           analytes_override = shared_analytes)

      if (!is.null(df_filtered_int)) {

        n_kept_int <- length(unique(df_filtered_int$analyte))
        cat(" ", paste0(n_kept_int, " of ", n_total_analytes_int,
                        " analytes were significant (main effect or interaction): ",
                        breakdown_str, "."), "\n")
        cat("\n")

        p_int <- plot_category_forest_interaction(df_filtered_int, curr_category, curr_ds, all_analytes = shared_analytes)
        print(p_int)

      } else {
        cat(" ", paste0("no analytes (of ", n_total_analytes_int,
                        ") had any significant model or interaction for this dataset type -- panel omitted"), "\n")
      }
    }



    cat("\n")
    cat(' \n \n')
  }

  cat("\n")
  cat(' \n \n')
}
```

#### stratified followup tests {.tabset}

```{r findWhichAnalytesNeedTests, results='asis'}
## ============================================================
## SECTION A: analyte x dataset_type x covariate summary
## ============================================================

summary_covariates <- c("Sex", "Adjuvant", "weight_c", "ageChall_c")
alpha           <- 0.05
min_sig_models  <- 1   # interaction rule: >= this many sig. interaction models for a covariate

main_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(nonTOA_all_results)
int_all  <- dplyr::bind_rows(nonTOA_all_results_interaction)

cov_key <- function(x) paste(sort(as.character(unlist(x))), collapse = "+")

## --- Analyte-level main-effect stability (hard p cutoff) -------------
summarize_main_stability <- function(df) {

  unadj <- df %>% dplyr::filter(adjustment == "Unadjusted")
  adj   <- df %>% dplyr::filter(adjustment != "Unadjusted")
  if (nrow(unadj) == 0 || nrow(adj) == 0) return(NULL)

  sig_unadj  <- unadj$p.value[1] < alpha
  sign_unadj <- sign(unadj$estimate[1])
  sig_adj    <- adj$p.value < alpha

  status_change <- sig_adj != sig_unadj
  # sign flips only matter when both are significant (otherwise already a status change)
  sign_change   <- sig_unadj & sig_adj & (sign(adj$estimate) != sign_unadj)
  n_changed     <- sum(status_change | sign_change, na.rm = TRUE)

  data.frame(
    main_est_unadj = unadj$estimate[1],
    main_p_unadj   = unadj$p.value[1],
    main_p_min     = min(adj$p.value, na.rm = TRUE),
    main_p_max     = max(adj$p.value, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_adj_models   = nrow(adj),
    n_main_changed = n_changed,
    main_stable    = n_changed == 0
  )
}

## --- Per-covariate leave-one-out flips (used only for CONFOUNDED) ----
count_main_flips_for_covariate <- function(df, covariate) {

  df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(cov_key = purrr::map_chr(covs_raw, cov_key))

  with_c <- df %>%
    dplyr::filter(purrr::map_lgl(covs_raw, ~ covariate %in% unlist(.x)))
  if (nrow(with_c) == 0) return(NA_integer_)

  base_key <- purrr::map_chr(with_c$covs_raw, ~ cov_key(setdiff(unlist(.x), covariate)))
  idx      <- match(base_key, df$cov_key)
  ok       <- !is.na(idx)

  sig_with <- with_c$p.value < alpha
  sig_base <- df$p.value[idx] < alpha
  flip <- (sig_with != sig_base) |
    (sig_with & sig_base & sign(with_c$estimate) != sign(df$estimate[idx]))

  sum(flip[ok], na.rm = TRUE)
}

## --- Per-covariate interaction summary --------------------------------
summarize_interaction_for_covariate <- function(df_int, covariate) {

  rows_cov <- df_int %>% dplyr::filter(active_cov == .env$covariate)
  if (nrow(rows_cov) == 0) return(NULL)

  n_sig <- sum(rows_cov$p.value < alpha, na.rm = TRUE)

  data.frame(
    int_p_min       = min(rows_cov$p.value, na.rm = TRUE),
    int_est_at_pmin = rows_cov$estimate[which.min(rows_cov$p.value)],
    int_n_sig       = n_sig,
    int_any_sig     = n_sig >= min_sig_models
  )
}

## --- Build long table ---------------------------------------------------
build_analyte_summary_long <- function() {

  combos <- main_all %>% dplyr::distinct(category, analyte, dataset_type)

  purrr::pmap_dfr(combos, function(category, analyte, dataset_type) {

    df_main <- main_all %>% dplyr::filter(analyte == !!analyte, dataset_type == !!dataset_type)
    df_int  <- int_all  %>% dplyr::filter(analyte == !!analyte, dataset_type == !!dataset_type)

    main_summ <- summarize_main_stability(df_main)
    if (is.null(main_summ)) {
      main_summ <- data.frame(main_est_unadj = NA, main_p_unadj = NA, main_p_min = NA,
                              main_p_max = NA, n_adj_models = NA, n_main_changed = NA,
                              main_stable = NA)
    }

    purrr::map_dfr(summary_covariates, function(cov) {

      int_summ <- summarize_interaction_for_covariate(df_int, cov)
      if (is.null(int_summ)) {
        int_summ <- data.frame(int_p_min = NA, int_est_at_pmin = NA,
                               int_n_sig = NA, int_any_sig = NA)
      }

      dplyr::bind_cols(
        data.frame(category = category, analyte = analyte,
                   dataset_type = dataset_type, covariate = cov,
                   n_main_flips_cov = count_main_flips_for_covariate(df_main, cov)),
        main_summ,
        int_summ
      )
    })
  })
}

analyte_summary_long <- build_analyte_summary_long()

## --- 4-level classification (analyte x dataset_type level) -------------
analyte_summary_long <- analyte_summary_long %>%
  dplyr::group_by(analyte, dataset_type) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(any_cov_sig_interaction = any(int_any_sig %in% TRUE)) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    main_unstable = (main_stable %in% FALSE),
    model_summary = dplyr::case_when(
      !main_unstable & !any_cov_sig_interaction ~ "INDEPENDENT",
      !main_unstable &  any_cov_sig_interaction ~ "MASKED",
      main_unstable  &  any_cov_sig_interaction ~ "CONFOUNDED_MODIFIED",
      TRUE                                      ~ "CONFOUNDED"
    ),
    ## which covariates get a stratified follow-up
    save_cov = dplyr::case_when(
      model_summary %in% c("MASKED", "CONFOUNDED_MODIFIED") ~ (int_any_sig %in% TRUE),
     # model_summary == "CONFOUNDED"                         ~ (n_main_flips_cov %in% 1:1000),
      TRUE                                                  ~ FALSE
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-main_unstable)

 cat("##### ", "Prep Tables {.tabset}", "\n")
    cat("\n")


     cat("###### ", "Timepoint x model summary classification", "\n")
    cat("\n")


analyte_summary_long %>%
        dplyr::distinct(analyte, dataset_type, model_summary) %>%
        dplyr::count(dataset_type, model_summary) %>%
  ### make wider
  dplyr::mutate(model_summary = factor(model_summary, c("INDEPENDENT","CONFOUNDED","CONFOUNDED_MODIFIED","MASKED"))) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(model_summary) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "model_summary", values_from = "n") %>%
  flextable::flextable() %>%
  theme_zebra()
  
   cat("\n")
  cat(' \n \n')

## ============================================================
## SECTION B: test_spec
## ============================================================

test_spec <- analyte_summary_long %>%
    
  dplyr::filter(save_cov) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    analyte, strat_var = covariate, dataset_type,
    reason = tolower(model_summary),
    ## main-effect verification columns (analyte level)
    main_stable, main_est_unadj, main_p_unadj, main_p_min, main_p_max,
    n_adj_models, n_main_changed,
    ## interaction verification columns
    any_cov_sig_interaction,          # analyte level: does ANY covariate interact?
    cov_int_any_sig = int_any_sig,    # this covariate meets the interaction rule
    cov_int_n_sig   = int_n_sig,
    cov_int_p_min   = int_p_min,
    ## leave-one-out flips (what selects covariates for "confounded")
    n_main_flips_cov
  )

analyte_flag_counts <- test_spec %>% dplyr::count(analyte, dataset_type, name = "n_covariates_flagged")

test_spec <- test_spec %>%
  dplyr::left_join(analyte_flag_counts, by = c("analyte", "dataset_type")) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n_covariates_flagged), analyte, strat_var)

  cat("###### ", "Covariate x model summary classification", "\n")
    cat("\n")

cat("\ntest_spec rows generated:", nrow(test_spec), "\n")
as.data.frame.matrix(table(test_spec$strat_var, test_spec$reason)) %>%
  rownames_to_column("Covariate") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Covariate = factor(Covariate, c("Sex","Adjuvant","weight_c","ageChall_c"))) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Covariate) %>%
    flextable::flextable() %>%
  theme_zebra()

 cat("\n")
  cat(' \n \n')
  
    cat("###### ", "Which analytes/covariates for followup", "\n")
    cat("\n")

as.data.frame(test_spec) %>%
  DT::datatable(
    extensions = 'Buttons',
    options = list(dom = 'Blfrtip',
                   buttons = c('copy', 'csv', 'excel', 'pdf', 'print'),
                   iDisplayLength = 40,
                   lengthMenu = list(c(10, 25, 50, -1), c(10, 25, 50, "All"))
  )) 

 cat("\n")
  cat(' \n \n')
```

```{r runStratifiedTests, results='asis', fig.height=6, fig.width=6}
#                    "Post","Post","Post","Post","Post","Post","Post","Post","Post","Post",
#                     "FC","FC","FC","FC","FC","FC","FC","FC",
#                     "FC","FC","FC","FC","FC","FC","FC","FC",
#                     "FC","FC","FC","FC","FC","FC","FC","FC"
#                    
#                    
#                    ),
#   stringsAsFactors = FALSE
# )
# 


## ============================================================
## Stratified confirmatory tests for the two interaction findings:
##   1. Arif_ADCC_NoFab   x Adjuvant (Alum vs ALFQA)
##   2. M766DV1gp120AntibodyTiter x Sex (Male vs Female)
##
## Predictions (from the interaction-term signs, both on Post data):
##   NoFab:      Alum -> ALVAC-vs-DNA gap strongly negative (ALVAC worse)
##               ALFQA -> gap smaller / near zero / possibly reversed
##   gp120Titer: Male -> ALVAC-vs-DNA gap strongly positive (ALVAC better)
##               Female -> gap smaller / near zero / possibly reversed
##
## Uses the SAME rank-based approach as the rest of the nonTOA pipeline
## (rank(value) then lm()), for consistency with Mann-Whitney framing.
## Assumes build_analyte_lm_data(), animal_platform_df, and
## covariate_labels_nonTOA already exist in the environment from the
## main Rmd run -- this chunk is meant to be pasted in and run after
## that pipeline has executed (or after loading the saved list_of_stats
## objects + re-deriving animal_platform_df/build_analyte_lm_data).
## ============================================================

# library(dplyr)
# library(purrr)
# library(broom)
# library(ggplot2)

## --------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Generic stratified-test runner.
##    analyte      : variable name, e.g. "Arif_ADCC_NoFab"
##    strat_var    : "Adjuvant" or "Sex" (must exist in animal_platform_df)
##    dataset_type : "Post" (matches names(build_analyte_lm_data(analyte)))
##    platform_ref : reference level for Platform (default "DNA", so the
##                   estimated coefficient is the ALVAC effect)
## --------------------------------------------------------
run_stratified_platform_test <- function(analyte, strat_var, dataset_type = "Post",
                                          platform_ref = "DNA") {

  data_list <- build_analyte_lm_data(analyte)

  if (!dataset_type %in% names(data_list)) {
    stop(paste0("No '", dataset_type, "' data available for analyte: ", analyte))
  }

  df <- data_list[[dataset_type]]

  strata <- levels(droplevels(df[[strat_var]]))

  purrr::map_dfr(strata, function(s) {

    df_s <- df %>% dplyr::filter(.data[[strat_var]] == s)

    ## need both platforms present in this stratum
    if (length(unique(df_s$Platform)) < 2) {
      return(data.frame(
        analyte = analyte, dataset_type = dataset_type,
        stratum_var = strat_var, stratum = s,
        n = nrow(df_s), estimate = NA, conf.low = NA, conf.high = NA,
        p.value = NA, note = "only one Platform level present -- skipped"
      ))
    }

    ## re-rank WITHIN this stratum (not reusing the overall rank_value),
    ## since Mann-Whitney-equivalent rank-lm should rank within the
    ## exact comparison group being tested
    df_s <- df_s %>%
      dplyr::mutate(rank_value_strat = rank(value, ties.method = "average", na.last = "keep")) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(Platform = stats::relevel(factor(Platform), ref = platform_ref))

    fit <- stats::lm(rank_value_strat ~ Platform, data = df_s)

    coef_row <- broom::tidy(fit, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
      dplyr::filter(term != "(Intercept)")

    data.frame(
      analyte      = analyte,
      dataset_type = dataset_type,
      stratum_var  = strat_var,
      stratum      = s,
      n            = nrow(df_s),
      n_DNA        = sum(df_s$Platform == platform_ref),
      n_ALVAC      = sum(df_s$Platform != platform_ref),
      estimate     = coef_row$estimate,
      conf.low     = coef_row$conf.low,
      conf.high    = coef_row$conf.high,
      p.value      = coef_row$p.value,
      note         = ""
    )
  })
}

## --------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Fixed level orders for common stratifying variables -- used so
## plots always show e.g. Alum before ALFQA, Male before Female,
## regardless of the order levels happen to appear in the data. Add
## more entries here as needed for other strat_vars.
## --------------------------------------------------------
strat_level_orders <- list(
  Adjuvant = c("Alum", "ALFQA"),
  Sex      = c("Male", "Female")
)

order_stratum_levels <- function(strata_present, strat_var) {
  preferred <- strat_level_orders[[strat_var]]
  if (is.null(preferred)) return(sort(strata_present))
  intersect(preferred, strata_present)  ## keeps preferred order, drops missing levels
}

## --------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Generalized driver: takes a data frame with one row per test
## (columns: analyte, strat_var, dataset_type[, platform_ref]),
## runs run_stratified_platform_test() for every row, and returns:
##   - results: combined long data frame of every stratified test
##   - plots:   a NAMED LIST of one ggplot per input row (so each
##              analyte x strat_var x dataset_type combo gets its own
##              plot, in the same order as test_spec)
## Optional platform_ref column lets different rows use different
## reference levels; defaults to "DNA" if the column is absent or NA
## for a given row.
## --------------------------------------------------------
## ============================================================
## Updated run_stratified_tests_from_spec(): now accepts predictions
## via test_spec$prediction (added by your predict_stratified_effect()
## step) and attaches each row's prediction text as a wrapped caption
## on that row's plot.
##
## Only the plot-building block inside the function changes -- the
## test-running logic (run_stratified_platform_test, results
## assembly) is untouched. Drop this in to replace your existing
## run_stratified_tests_from_spec() definition.
## ============================================================

run_stratified_tests_from_spec <- function(test_spec, sig_cutoff = 0.05) {

  if (!"platform_ref" %in% colnames(test_spec)) {
    test_spec$platform_ref <- "DNA"
  }
  test_spec$platform_ref[is.na(test_spec$platform_ref)] <- "DNA"

  has_prediction <- "prediction" %in% colnames(test_spec)

  results_list <- purrr::pmap(
    list(test_spec$analyte, test_spec$strat_var, test_spec$dataset_type, test_spec$platform_ref, seq_len(nrow(test_spec))),
    function(analyte, strat_var, dataset_type, platform_ref, row_id) {

      res <- tryCatch(
        run_stratified_platform_test(
          analyte      = analyte,
          strat_var    = strat_var,
          dataset_type = dataset_type,
          platform_ref = platform_ref
        ),
        error = function(e) {
          data.frame(
            analyte = analyte, dataset_type = dataset_type,
            stratum_var = strat_var, stratum = NA, n = NA,
            n_DNA = NA, n_ALVAC = NA,
            estimate = NA, conf.low = NA, conf.high = NA, p.value = NA,
            note = paste0("ERROR: ", conditionMessage(e))
          )
        }
      )

      res$row_id <- row_id
      res
    }
  )

  results <- dplyr::bind_rows(results_list)

  ## one plot per input row, keyed by row_id -> preserves test_spec order
  plots <- purrr::map(seq_len(nrow(test_spec)), function(row_id) {

    df_row <- dplyr::filter(results, row_id == !!row_id)

    if (nrow(df_row) == 0 || all(is.na(df_row$estimate))) return(NULL)

    analyte      <- unique(df_row$analyte)
    strat_var    <- unique(df_row$stratum_var)
    dataset_type <- unique(df_row$dataset_type)
    platform_ref <- test_spec$platform_ref[row_id]
    other_level  <- if (platform_ref == "DNA") "ALVAC" else "DNA"

    level_order <- order_stratum_levels(unique(as.character(df_row$stratum)), strat_var)

    df_row <- df_row %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        stratum  = factor(stratum, level_order),
        p_label  = dplyr::if_else(p.value < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p.value)),
        sig      = p.value < 0.05,
        n_label  = paste0("n=", n, " (", n_DNA, " ", platform_ref, " / ", n_ALVAC, " ", other_level, ")")
      )

    ## --------------------------------------------------------
    ## caption text (from test_spec$prediction, now already \n-joined
    ## by predict_stratified_effect()) + whether the underlying
    ## interaction term was significant, read directly from int_all
    ## (same lookup logic as predict_stratified_effect() uses) rather
    ## than string-matching the prediction text
    ## --------------------------------------------------------
    caption_text <- NULL
    caption_sig  <- FALSE

    if (has_prediction) {
      pred_raw <- test_spec$prediction[row_id]
      if (!is.na(pred_raw) && nzchar(pred_raw)) {
        caption_text <- pred_raw  ## already has \n line breaks baked in

        int_row_check <- int_all %>%
          dplyr::filter(analyte == !!analyte, dataset_type == !!dataset_type,
                        active_cov == !!strat_var, n_covariates == 1)
        if (nrow(int_row_check) > 0) {
          caption_sig <- int_row_check$p.value[1] < sig_cutoff
        }
      }
    }

    caption_color <- if (caption_sig) "#8B0000" else "grey20"  ## dark red vs grey
    caption_face  <- if (caption_sig) "bold.italic" else "italic"

    ggplot(df_row, aes(x = estimate, y = stratum, color = stratum)) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
      geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high), height = 0.15) +
      geom_point(aes(shape = sig), size = 3) +
      geom_text(aes(label = paste0("p = ", p_label)), vjust = -1.3, size = 3.2, color = "black") +
      geom_text(aes(label = n_label), vjust = 2.3, size = 2.6, color = "grey40") +
      scale_shape_manual(name = "p < 0.05", values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 1)) +
      scale_color_viridis_d(guide = "none", option = "D", end = 0.8) +
      labs(
        x = paste0(other_level, " vs ", platform_ref, " effect (rank scale)"),
        y = NULL,
        title = paste0(analyte, " \u2014 ", dataset_type),
        subtitle = paste0("stratified by ", strat_var),
        caption = caption_text
      ) +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 8.5, face = caption_face,
                                    color = caption_color, margin = margin(t = 8)),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.margin = margin(10, 20, 15, 10)
      )
  })

  names(plots) <- paste0(test_spec$analyte, " | ", test_spec$strat_var, " | ", test_spec$dataset_type)

  list(results = results, plots = plots)
}

## --------------------------------------------------------
## Predictions for each stratified test, derived from the previously
## fitted rank-lm MAIN effect (Platform, adjusted for the stratifying
## covariate) and INTERACTION (Platform x covariate) results.
##
## Coding in those models: Platform ref = DNA, so estimates are
## ALVAC - DNA on the rank scale. Reference stratum = first level in
## strat_level_orders (Alum / Male); other = second (ALFQA / Female).
##   e_ref   = ALVAC-vs-DNA effect in the reference stratum
##   e_other = e_ref + interaction estimate
## The stored main effect (Platform + covariate) is roughly the
## stratum-size-weighted average of the two stratum effects:
##   m ~ (1-w)*e_ref + w*e_other,  w = fraction of animals in "other"
## so:  e_ref ~ m - w*i,   e_other ~ m + (1-w)*i
## --------------------------------------------------------
main_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(nonTOA_all_results)
int_all  <- dplyr::bind_rows(nonTOA_all_results_interaction)


predict_stratified_effect <- function(a, sv, ds, near_zero_frac = 0.1, sig = 0.05) {

  lv  <- strat_level_orders[[sv]]
  ref <- lv[1]; oth <- lv[2]

  main_row <- main_all %>%
    dplyr::filter(analyte == a, dataset_type == ds, n_covariates == 1,
                  adjustment == paste0("+ ", covariate_labels_nonTOA[[sv]]))

  int_row <- int_all %>%
    dplyr::filter(analyte == a, dataset_type == ds,
                  active_cov == sv, n_covariates == 1)

  if (nrow(main_row) == 0 || nrow(int_row) == 0) {
    return("no prediction: main/interaction result not available for this analyte/covariate")
  }

  df <- build_analyte_lm_data(a)[[ds]]
  if (is.null(df)) return("no prediction: no data")
  n <- nrow(df)
  w <- mean(df[[sv]] == oth, na.rm = TRUE)

  m     <- main_row$estimate[1]
  i     <- int_row$estimate[1]
  p_int <- int_row$p.value[1]

  e_ref <- m - w * i
  e_oth <- m + (1 - w) * i

  thr <- near_zero_frac * n
  describe <- function(e) {
    if (abs(e) < thr) "ALVAC ~ DNA"
    else if (e > 0)   "ALVAC > DNA"
    else              "ALVAC < DNA"
  }

  reversed <- (e_ref * e_oth < 0) && abs(e_ref) >= thr && abs(e_oth) >= thr
  weak <- if (p_int < sig) "" else " [interaction not significant: weak prediction]"

  ## --------------------------------------------------------
  ## Build with explicit \n line breaks instead of "; " separators:
  ##   line 1: ref stratum
  ##   line 2: other stratum
  ##   line 3 (optional): direction REVERSED note
  ##   line 4: interaction summary (+ weak-prediction flag if any)
  ## --------------------------------------------------------
  line1 <- paste0(ref, ": ", describe(e_ref), " (~", round(e_ref, 1), " ranks)")
  line2 <- paste0(oth, ": ", describe(e_oth), " (~", round(e_oth, 1), " ranks)")
  line3 <- if (reversed) "direction REVERSED between strata" else NULL
  line4 <- paste0(
    "Interaction (", oth, " vs ", ref, ") = ", round(i, 1),
    ", p = ", signif(p_int, 2), weak
  )

  paste(c(line1, line2, line3, line4), collapse = "\n")
}



## ============================================================
## Continuous-covariate analog of run_stratified_platform_test() /
## run_stratified_tests_from_spec(). For a Platform x continuous
## covariate (weight_c or ageChall_c) interaction, instead of
## splitting into strata, this computes the PREDICTED ALVAC-vs-DNA
## effect (with 95% CI) as a continuous function of the covariate --
## i.e. a "simple slopes" / marginal effects plot -- evaluated across
## the observed range of that covariate in the exact data used to fit
## the model. ***followup_out$curves**** contains the curve data plotted
##
## Model fit: rank_value ~ Platform * covariate
## Effect of interest at covariate = x:
##   beta_Platform + beta_interaction * x
## Variance of that linear combination, for the CI band, uses the full
## coefficient covariance matrix (vcov()), not just the two marginal
## SEs, since Platform and Platform:covariate are correlated estimates.
## ============================================================

## --------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Core computation for ONE analyte x covariate x dataset_type.
##    covariate_var: "weight_c" or "ageChall_c" (must exist in the
##    data frame returned by build_analyte_lm_data())
##    n_points: how many x-values to evaluate the line/ribbon at
## --------------------------------------------------------
run_continuous_interaction_effect <- function(analyte, covariate_var, dataset_type = "Post",
                                               platform_ref = "DNA", n_points = 50) {

  data_list <- build_analyte_lm_data(analyte)

  if (!dataset_type %in% names(data_list)) {
    stop(paste0("No '", dataset_type, "' data available for analyte: ", analyte))
  }

  df <- data_list[[dataset_type]]

  if (!covariate_var %in% colnames(df)) {
    stop(paste0("Covariate '", covariate_var, "' not found in data for analyte: ", analyte))
  }

  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[covariate_var]])) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Platform = stats::relevel(factor(Platform), ref = platform_ref))

  other_level <- setdiff(levels(df$Platform), platform_ref)
  if (length(unique(df$Platform)) < 2) {
    stop(paste0("Only one Platform level present for analyte: ", analyte))
  }

  fit <- stats::lm(
    stats::as.formula(paste0("rank_value ~ Platform * ", covariate_var)),
    data = df
  )

  platform_term <- paste0("Platform", other_level)
  interaction_term <- paste0(platform_term, ":", covariate_var)

  ## guard: if the interaction term isn't in the model (e.g. covariate
  ## constant within a Platform level), bail out cleanly
  if (!(platform_term %in% names(coef(fit))) || !(interaction_term %in% names(coef(fit)))) {
    stop(paste0("Expected terms not found in model for analyte: ", analyte,
               " (check covariate variation within each Platform level)"))
  }

  b_platform <- coef(fit)[[platform_term]]
  b_interact <- coef(fit)[[interaction_term]]
  V <- vcov(fit)

  ## evaluate across the observed range of the covariate (pooled
  ## across both Platform levels, since that's the range the
  ## interaction line is being drawn over)
  x_range <- range(df[[covariate_var]], na.rm = TRUE)
  x_seq <- seq(x_range[1], x_range[2], length.out = n_points)

  ## effect(x) = b_platform + b_interact * x
  ## Var(effect(x)) = Var(b_platform) + x^2*Var(b_interact) + 2*x*Cov(b_platform, b_interact)
  var_platform <- V[platform_term, platform_term]
  var_interact <- V[interaction_term, interaction_term]
  cov_pi       <- V[platform_term, interaction_term]

  effect_est <- b_platform + b_interact * x_seq
  effect_var <- var_platform + (x_seq^2) * var_interact + 2 * x_seq * cov_pi
  effect_se  <- sqrt(effect_var)

  ## df for the t-based CI: model residual df
  t_crit <- stats::qt(0.975, df = fit$df.residual)

  data.frame(
    analyte       = analyte,
    dataset_type  = dataset_type,
    covariate_var = covariate_var,
    x             = x_seq,
    estimate      = effect_est,
    conf.low      = effect_est - t_crit * effect_se,
    conf.high     = effect_est + t_crit * effect_se,
    interaction_p = summary(fit)$coefficients[interaction_term, "Pr(>|t|)"]
  ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      n         = nrow(df),
      n_DNA     = sum(df$Platform == platform_ref),
      n_ALVAC   = sum(df$Platform != platform_ref),
      other_level  = other_level,
      platform_ref = platform_ref
    )
}

## --------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Human-readable label per covariate, matched to
## covariate_labels_nonTOA already in your environment
## --------------------------------------------------------
continuous_covariate_labels <- covariate_labels_nonTOA  ## Sex/Adjuvant/weight_c/ageChall_c -> labels

## --------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Prediction text for a continuous interaction, analogous to
## predict_stratified_effect() but describing a SLOPE rather than two
## strata: does the ALVAC-vs-DNA effect get stronger/weaker/reverse
## sign as the covariate increases, and where (if anywhere in the
## observed range) does it cross zero?
## --------------------------------------------------------
predict_continuous_effect <- function(a, cv, ds, sig = 0.05, near_zero_frac = 0.1) {

  int_row <- int_all %>%
    dplyr::filter(analyte == a, dataset_type == ds,
                  active_cov == cv, n_covariates == 1)

  if (nrow(int_row) == 0) {
    return("no prediction: interaction result not available for this analyte/covariate")
  }

  curve_df <- tryCatch(
    run_continuous_interaction_effect(a, cv, ds),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(curve_df)) return("no prediction: could not fit continuous interaction model")

  p_int <- int_row$p.value[1]
  i     <- int_row$estimate[1]

  n <- curve_df$n[1]
  thr <- near_zero_frac * n

  e_low  <- curve_df$estimate[1]
  e_high <- curve_df$estimate[nrow(curve_df)]
  x_low  <- round(curve_df$x[1], 1)
  x_high <- round(curve_df$x[nrow(curve_df)], 1)

  describe <- function(e) {
    if (abs(e) < thr) "ALVAC ~ DNA"
    else if (e > 0)   "ALVAC > DNA"
    else              "ALVAC < DNA"
  }

  ## does the fitted line cross zero within the observed range?
  crosses_zero <- (e_low * e_high < 0)
  zero_x <- if (crosses_zero) {
    ## linear interpolation: x where estimate == 0
    frac <- abs(e_low) / (abs(e_low) + abs(e_high))
    round(x_low + frac * (x_high - x_low), 1)
  } else {
    NA
  }

  label <- unname(continuous_covariate_labels[cv])

  line1 <- paste0("At low ", label, " (", x_low, "): ", describe(e_low), " (~", round(e_low, 1), " ranks)")
  line2 <- paste0("At high ", label, " (", x_high, "): ", describe(e_high), " (~", round(e_high, 1), " ranks)")
  line3 <- if (crosses_zero) paste0("Effect crosses zero around ", label, " = ", zero_x) else NULL
  weak <- if (p_int < sig) "" else " [interaction not significant: weak prediction]"
  line4 <- paste0("Interaction slope = ", signif(i, 3), " per unit ", label, ", p = ", signif(p_int, 2), weak)

  paste(c(line1, line2, line3, line4), collapse = "\n")
}

## --------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Plot builder: ribbon + line, with the same significance-colored
## caption convention as the stratified plots. x-axis in the
## covariate's own units is more interpretable than the centered
## value -- if you'd rather show the CENTERED covariate (matching how
## the model was fit), just drop the "+ mean(...)" shift below.
## --------------------------------------------------------
plot_continuous_interaction <- function(a, cv, ds, sig_cutoff = 0.05, platform_ref = "DNA") {

  curve_df <- tryCatch(
    run_continuous_interaction_effect(a, cv, ds, platform_ref = platform_ref),
    error = function(e) {
      warning(paste0("Could not build continuous interaction plot for ", a, "/", cv, "/", ds, ": ", conditionMessage(e)))
      NULL
    }
  )
  if (is.null(curve_df)) return(NULL)

  label <- unname(continuous_covariate_labels[cv])
  other_level  <- curve_df$other_level[1]
  platform_ref_used <- curve_df$platform_ref[1]
  n <- curve_df$n[1]
  n_DNA <- curve_df$n_DNA[1]
  n_ALVAC <- curve_df$n_ALVAC[1]

  pred_text <- predict_continuous_effect(a, cv, ds)
  int_row_check <- int_all %>%
    dplyr::filter(analyte == a, dataset_type == ds, active_cov == cv, n_covariates == 1)
  caption_sig <- if (nrow(int_row_check) > 0) int_row_check$p.value[1] < sig_cutoff else FALSE

  caption_color <- if (caption_sig) "#8B0000" else "grey20"
  caption_face  <- if (caption_sig) "bold" else "italic"

  ggplot(curve_df, aes(x = x, y = estimate)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.2) +
    geom_line(color = "steelblue4", linewidth = 1) +
    labs(
      x = paste0(label, " (raw units, centered value's original scale)"),
      y = paste0(other_level, " vs ", platform_ref_used, " effect (rank scale)"),
      title = paste0(a, " \u2014 ", ds),
      subtitle = paste0("Predicted platform effect across observed ", label, " range (n=", n,
                        ", ", n_DNA, " ", platform_ref_used, " / ", n_ALVAC, " ", other_level, ")"),
      caption = pred_text
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
      plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 8.5, face = caption_face,
                                  color = caption_color, margin = margin(t = 8)),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      plot.margin = margin(10, 20, 15, 10)
    )
}

## --------------------------------------------------------
## 5. Generalized spec-driven driver, mirroring
## run_stratified_tests_from_spec() but for continuous covariates.
## test_spec here needs columns: analyte, covariate_var (weight_c or
## ageChall_c), dataset_type[, platform_ref]
## --------------------------------------------------------
run_continuous_tests_from_spec <- function(test_spec, sig_cutoff = 0.05) {

  if (!"platform_ref" %in% colnames(test_spec)) {
    test_spec$platform_ref <- "DNA"
  }
  test_spec$platform_ref[is.na(test_spec$platform_ref)] <- "DNA"

  results_list <- purrr::pmap(
    list(test_spec$analyte, test_spec$covariate_var, test_spec$dataset_type, test_spec$platform_ref, seq_len(nrow(test_spec))),
    function(analyte, covariate_var, dataset_type, platform_ref, row_id) {
      res <- tryCatch(
        run_continuous_interaction_effect(analyte, covariate_var, dataset_type, platform_ref = platform_ref),
        error = function(e) {
          data.frame(
            analyte = analyte, dataset_type = dataset_type, covariate_var = covariate_var,
            x = NA, estimate = NA, conf.low = NA, conf.high = NA, interaction_p = NA,
            n = NA, n_DNA = NA, n_ALVAC = NA, other_level = NA, platform_ref = platform_ref,
            note = paste0("ERROR: ", conditionMessage(e))
          )
        }
      )
      res$row_id <- row_id
      res
    }
  )

  results <- dplyr::bind_rows(results_list)

  plots <- purrr::map(seq_len(nrow(test_spec)), function(row_id) {
    row <- test_spec[row_id, ]
    plot_continuous_interaction(
      a = row$analyte, cv = row$covariate_var, ds = row$dataset_type,
      sig_cutoff = sig_cutoff, platform_ref = row$platform_ref
    )
  })

  names(plots) <- paste0(test_spec$analyte, " | ", test_spec$covariate_var, " | ", test_spec$dataset_type)

  list(results = results, plots = plots)
}



run_continuous_interaction_summary <- function(analyte, covariate_var, dataset_type = "Post",
                                               platform_ref = "DNA") {

  df <- build_analyte_lm_data(analyte)[[dataset_type]] %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[covariate_var]])) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Platform = stats::relevel(factor(Platform), ref = platform_ref))

  other_level <- setdiff(levels(df$Platform), platform_ref)
  fit <- stats::lm(stats::as.formula(paste0("rank_value ~ Platform * ", covariate_var)), data = df)

  iterm <- paste0("Platform", other_level, ":", covariate_var)
  ci    <- stats::confint(fit)[iterm, ]
  p     <- summary(fit)$coefficients[iterm, "Pr(>|t|)"]

  data.frame(
    analyte       = analyte,
    dataset_type  = dataset_type,
    strat_var     = covariate_var,
    test_type     = "continuous",
    estimate_type = paste0("interaction slope (change in ", other_level, " - ", platform_ref,
                           " rank effect per 1 unit)"),
    stratum       = "slope",
    n             = nrow(df),
    n_DNA         = sum(df$Platform == platform_ref),
    n_ALVAC       = sum(df$Platform != platform_ref),
    estimate      = unname(coef(fit)[iterm]),
    conf.low      = unname(ci[1]),
    conf.high     = unname(ci[2]),
    p.value       = p,
    interaction_p = p,
    note          = ""
  )
}


## ============================================================
## Unified driver: ONE spec data frame, ONE call, routes each row to
## either the stratified-test path (Sex/Adjuvant) or the continuous
## simple-slopes path (weight_c/ageChall_c) based on strat_var, and
## returns a single combined results table + plot list so your
## tabset-printing loop only needs to iterate once.
##
## Spec columns:
##   analyte      : variable name
##   strat_var    : "Sex", "Adjuvant", "weight_c", or "ageChall_c"
##   dataset_type : "Baseline"/"Post"/"Delta"/"FC"
##   platform_ref : optional, defaults to "DNA"
##
## Uses the SAME column name (strat_var) for both categorical and
## continuous covariates, so your existing test_spec table doesn't
## need a schema change -- just add weight_c/ageChall_c rows to the
## same strat_var column you already use for Sex/Adjuvant.
## ============================================================

## which strat_var values route to the continuous (simple-slopes) path
continuous_covariate_vars <- c("weight_c", "ageChall_c")


## --------------------------------------------------------
## Unified per-row prediction text: dispatches to
## predict_stratified_effect() or predict_continuous_effect()
## depending on whether strat_var is continuous.
## --------------------------------------------------------
predict_effect_unified <- function(a, sv, ds) {
  if (sv %in% continuous_covariate_vars) {
    predict_continuous_effect(a, sv, ds)
  } else {
    predict_stratified_effect(a, sv, ds)
  }
}

## --------------------------------------------------------
## Unified driver
## --------------------------------------------------------
run_followup_tests_from_spec <- function(test_spec, sig_cutoff = 0.05) {

  if (!"platform_ref" %in% colnames(test_spec)) {
    test_spec$platform_ref <- "DNA"
  }
  test_spec$platform_ref[is.na(test_spec$platform_ref)] <- "DNA"

  ## attach predictions up front if not already present, using the
  ## unified dispatcher -- so callers can pass a spec without
  ## precomputed predictions and still get captions
  if (!"prediction" %in% colnames(test_spec)) {
    test_spec$prediction <- purrr::pmap_chr(
      list(test_spec$analyte, test_spec$strat_var, test_spec$dataset_type),
      predict_effect_unified
    )
  }

  is_continuous_row <- test_spec$strat_var %in% continuous_covariate_vars

  ## --------------------------------------------------------
  ## split into the two sub-specs, run each through its existing
  ## pipeline, THEN reassemble results/plots back into original
  ## row_id order so the combined outputs line up with test_spec
  ## row-for-row regardless of which path each row took
  ## --------------------------------------------------------
  test_spec$orig_row_id <- seq_len(nrow(test_spec))

  spec_strat <- test_spec[!is_continuous_row, , drop = FALSE]
  spec_cont  <- test_spec[is_continuous_row, , drop = FALSE]

    results_all <- vector("list", nrow(test_spec))
  curves_all  <- vector("list", nrow(test_spec))
  plots_all   <- vector("list", nrow(test_spec))
  plot_names_all <- character(nrow(test_spec))

  if (nrow(spec_strat) > 0) {
    strat_out <- run_stratified_tests_from_spec(spec_strat, sig_cutoff = sig_cutoff)

    ## interaction p for each categorical row, so both test types have the column
    int_p_lookup <- function(a, sv, ds) {
      r <- int_all %>% dplyr::filter(analyte == a, dataset_type == ds,
                                     active_cov == sv, n_covariates == 1)
      if (nrow(r) == 0) NA_real_ else r$p.value[1]
    }

    for (k in seq_len(nrow(spec_strat))) {
      orig_id <- spec_strat$orig_row_id[k]
            results_all[[orig_id]] <- dplyr::filter(strat_out$results, row_id == k) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(
          strat_var     = stratum_var,
          test_type     = "categorical",
          estimate_type = "platform effect within stratum",
          interaction_p = int_p_lookup(analyte[1], strat_var[1], dataset_type[1])
        ) %>%
        dplyr::select(-stratum_var, -row_id)
      plots_all[[orig_id]] <- strat_out$plots[[k]]
      plot_names_all[orig_id] <- names(strat_out$plots)[k]
    }
  }

  if (nrow(spec_cont) > 0) {
    spec_cont2 <- spec_cont %>% dplyr::rename(covariate_var = strat_var)
    cont_out   <- run_continuous_tests_from_spec(spec_cont2, sig_cutoff = sig_cutoff)

    for (k in seq_len(nrow(spec_cont2))) {
      orig_id <- spec_cont2$orig_row_id[k]

            results_all[[orig_id]] <- tryCatch(
        run_continuous_interaction_summary(spec_cont2$analyte[k], spec_cont2$covariate_var[k],
                                           spec_cont2$dataset_type[k], spec_cont2$platform_ref[k]),
        error = function(e) data.frame(
          analyte = spec_cont2$analyte[k], dataset_type = spec_cont2$dataset_type[k],
          strat_var = spec_cont2$covariate_var[k], test_type = "continuous",
          estimate_type = "interaction slope", stratum = "slope",
          n = NA, n_DNA = NA, n_ALVAC = NA,
          estimate = NA, conf.low = NA, conf.high = NA, p.value = NA, interaction_p = NA,
          note = paste0("ERROR: ", conditionMessage(e)))
      )

      ## full 50-point grid kept separately, for plotting/export only
      curves_all[[orig_id]] <- dplyr::filter(cont_out$results, row_id == k) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(strat_var = spec_cont2$covariate_var[k]) %>%
        dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of(c("row_id", "covariate_var")))
      plots_all[[orig_id]] <- cont_out$plots[[k]]
      plot_names_all[orig_id] <- names(cont_out$plots)[k]
    }
  }

  results_combined <- dplyr::bind_rows(results_all) %>%
    dplyr::relocate(analyte, dataset_type, strat_var, test_type, stratum, estimate_type,
                    n, n_DNA, n_ALVAC, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p.value, interaction_p, note)
  names(plots_all) <- plot_names_all

  list(results = results_combined,
       curves  = dplyr::bind_rows(curves_all),
       plots   = plots_all,
       spec    = test_spec)
}




followup_out <- run_followup_tests_from_spec(test_spec)


 cat("##### ", "Predictions ", "\n")
```

```{r heatmapSummary, results='asis', fig.height=25, fig.width=17}
## ---- 1. prep all rows ------------------------------------------------
res <- followup_out$results %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    row_lab = paste(analyte, dataset_type, sep = " | "),
    stars   = dplyr::case_when(is.na(p.value) ~ "",
                               p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
                               p.value < 0.01  ~ "**",
                               p.value < 0.05  ~ "*",
                               TRUE ~ ""),
    int_sig = !is.na(interaction_p) & interaction_p < 0.05
  )

## ---- NEW: explicit display order for categories -----------------------
## Edit this vector to control category order in the "sort by category"
## heatmap pass. Any category present in the data but NOT listed here
## gets appended at the end (alphabetically), so nothing silently
## disappears if this list falls out of sync with nonTOA_category_vars.
category_display_order <- c(
  "ADCC/Ab only",
  "V2peptides",
  "Avidity score only",
  "Efferocytosis only",
  "RM cell responses (Panel B)",
  "Systemic cell responses (Panel C)",
  "Cytokines/Chemokines (Panel D - most)",
  "Cytokines/Chemokines (Panel D - TSLP set)"
)

## ---- NEW: analyte -> category lookup, then join onto res -------------
## category lives on main_all/int_all (one row per analyte x dataset_type
## x model), not on followup_out$results, so build a simple one-row-per-
## analyte lookup and join it in. If an analyte appears in more than one
## category (shouldn't normally happen, but just in case), take the
## first category (per category_display_order) so the join stays 1:1.
analyte_category_lookup <- dplyr::bind_rows(main_all, int_all) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(analyte, category) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ## any category not in category_display_order sorts after all listed
    ## ones (alphabetically among themselves), via a high dummy rank
    .cat_rank = dplyr::coalesce(match(category, category_display_order), 9999L)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(analyte, .cat_rank, category) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(analyte) %>%
  dplyr::slice(1) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(-.cat_rank)

## full factor level set: listed categories first (in the given order),
## then any leftover categories actually present in the data, alphabetical
categories_present <- sort(unique(analyte_category_lookup$category))
category_levels_full <- c(
  intersect(category_display_order, categories_present),
  setdiff(categories_present, category_display_order)
)

res <- res %>%
  dplyr::left_join(analyte_category_lookup, by = "analyte") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    category = dplyr::coalesce(category, "(uncategorized)"),
    ## NEW: factor with the explicit display order, so arrange(category, ...)
    ## downstream sorts by this order instead of alphabetically
    category = factor(category, levels = c(category_levels_full, "(uncategorized)"))
  )

## ---- NEW: untestable category x covariate lookup ----
## nonTOA_category_vars splits some analyte_categories groupings finer
## than testability_table does (e.g. "ADCC/Ab only" + "V2peptides" vs
## testability_table's single "ADCC/Ab/V2pep only"; "Cytokines/Chemokines
## (Panel D - most)" + "...- TSLP set" vs testability_table's single
## "Cytokines/Chemokines (Panel D)"). Map the finer names onto the
## testability_table names so the join lines up, rather than relying on
## exact string equality.
category_name_map <- c(
  "ADCC/Ab only"                               = "ADCC/Ab/V2pep only",
  "V2peptides"                                 = "ADCC/Ab/V2pep only",
  "Cytokines/Chemokines (Panel D - most)"      = "Cytokines/Chemokines (Panel D)",
  "Cytokines/Chemokines (Panel D - TSLP set)"  = "Cytokines/Chemokines (Panel D)"
)

map_to_testability_category <- function(cat) {
  dplyr::if_else(cat %in% names(category_name_map), category_name_map[cat], cat)
}

## Ground truth for "was this covariate ever a candidate for this
## category" is nonTOA_category_use_sex / nonTOA_category_use_adjuvant --
## these use nonTOA_category_vars' (finer) category names directly, no
## remapping needed here.
category_covariate_candidate <- tibble::tibble(
  category = names(nonTOA_category_vars)
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Sex        = unname(nonTOA_category_use_sex[category]),
    Adjuvant   = unname(nonTOA_category_use_adjuvant[category]),
    weight_c   = TRUE,
    ageChall_c = TRUE
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-category, names_to = "strat_var", values_to = "is_candidate")

## testability_table data-level checks, keyed by testability_table's
## (coarser) category names
testability_by_coarse_category <- testability_table %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    category = category,
    Sex      = !Platform_x_Sex      | Platform_Sex_confounded | !Sex_main_effect,
    Adjuvant = !Platform_x_Adjuvant | Platform_Adjuvant_confounded,
    weight_c   = !Platform_x_WeightAge,
    ageChall_c = !Platform_x_WeightAge
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-category, names_to = "strat_var", values_to = "untestable_data")

## bring the data-level checks onto the FINE category names, via the map
category_covariate_untestable <- category_covariate_candidate %>%
  dplyr::mutate(coarse_category = map_to_testability_category(category)) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    testability_by_coarse_category,
    by = c("coarse_category" = "category", "strat_var")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    is_candidate    = dplyr::coalesce(is_candidate, FALSE),
    untestable_data = dplyr::coalesce(untestable_data, TRUE),
    untestable      = !is_candidate | untestable_data
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(category, strat_var, untestable)

## ---- sanity checks: re-run these after the fix ----

# dplyr::filter(category_covariate_untestable, category == "V2peptides")

## join onto res: untestable per (analyte's category) x (this row's strat_var)
res <- res %>%
  dplyr::left_join(category_covariate_untestable, by = c("category", "strat_var")) %>%

  stats::sd(df[[sv]], na.rm = TRUE)
}

    col_lab = "slope per SD",

## ---- 2. complete grid so untested combos show as grey tiles ----------

  dplyr::distinct(row_lab, analyte, dataset_type) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dataset_type, analyte) %>%
  dplyr::pull(row_lab) %>% rev()


cat_cols <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(strat_level_orders), function(v)
```
